defects.summary: Concurrent create into ONE SHARED directory costs 8.3x more wall per node at 32 nodes than the same creates into per-node private directories (1842 ms vs 222 ms for 8 creates; 9.3x on the mean, 34x on p95), and the cost is ENTIRELY IN THE TAIL -- the shared arm's p50 is 10 ms and flat in N, so every node pays roughly one multi-second stall per 8 creates rather than a uniformly slower create. 74.5% of blocked samples sit in the CAW inode-grant wait (mxfs_pal_cond_timedwait under caw_lock_body), against 7.0% in the SCSI transport, so this is the DLM's EX rotation among 32 contenders on one directory inode. A second, smaller term rides underneath: the PRIVATE arm is not flat either, growing 6x from 1 to 32 nodes (37 -> 222 ms) with nothing shared but the mount. (sess380 re-measured all of this after fixing tests/create_scale_curve.sh, whose private arm had been running a 32-way mkdir on a shared parent INSIDE the measured window; the previously recorded '42x, private scales flat' figures came from that contaminated control.)
evidence:
SESS380 THE LOAD IS READS, AND THEY ARE THE PROBE WALK — NOT THE CAS COLLISION, WHICH IS WHAT THIS ENTRY (AND I, EARLIER THE SAME SESSION) SPENT THE MOST EFFORT ON. New harness tests/shared_dir_slot_cost.sh counts every SCSI command the whole cluster issues to the ONE CAW slot of a shared directory while 32 nodes do 256 creates into it. Repeated over 6 runs on 0.15.6-0.15.10, stable:
    READ(16)+FUA       5,844 - 8,587   = 23 - 34 per create
    COMPARE AND WRITE    424 -   515   = 1.7 - 2.0 per create (50-52% MISCOMPARE)
  reads are 93% of ALL traffic on that sector and outnumber writes 13-16 to 1.
P383-SLOTREAD then tagged every one of those reads with its caller (7,653 tagged reads, one run):
    find_slot_skip                6,373   83.3%   <- the open-addressing PROBE WALK
    caw_wait_for_grant              880   11.5%   <- the grant poll loop
    caw_count_resource_slots        398    5.2%
    bast_poll_fn                      2    0.0%
So ~25 of the ~30 reads per create are slot RESOLUTION, re-walked from scratch on every lookup, and the resource's home slot IS the hot sector, so every walk reads it at least once. The grant poll loop — the thing four sessions of this entry's history blamed — is 11.5%.

SESS380 FOUR HYPOTHESES REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT, recorded so nobody re-runs them. Each was cheap and each was wrong; together they are what narrowed the search to the probe walk.
  (1) 'The unlock CAS keeps losing to peers REGISTERING INTEREST, so skip the backoff when the miscompare was a pure registration.' Built an exact-transition classifier (reconstructs byte for byte the only image a registration could produce, then memcmps) and ran it with the acting knob OFF: of 475 unlock miscompares, 1 was benign (0.2%), 7 were holder changes, ZERO were yield_to moves, and 467 (98.3%) were MULTI-GENERATION — several unrelated writes landed between our compare image and our re-read. The optimisation would fire on 0.2% of cases. mxfs.caw_unlock_fastretry ships DEFAULT 0 and should stay there; the classifier is retained because its histogram is what produced this finding.
  (2) 'Releases wake the whole waiter field, so every handoff costs N reads.' P382-WAKE says the wake-the-field branch is taken 0.0% of the time: 75.7% mint a single successor, 24.3% use an existing ticket, mean 1.25 nodes woken against 4.70 waiters present.
  (3) 'The 2ms fastpoll window is the amplifier' (a suspicion written into the mxfs.caw_inode_fastpoll knob's own comment years ago). Turning it OFF made reads WORSE: 26.6 -> 32.9 per create.
  (4) 'The reads are exponential-backstop timeouts, and the nudge would carry the grants anyway' — supported by P297-TKT showing 96.6% of ticketed waiters wake by NUDGE with ZERO swallowed nudges. Raising mxfs.caw_poll_max_ms from 25 to 200 made BOTH worse: reads 22.8 -> 29.6 per create and per-node wall 1577 -> 2612 ms. Removing the fastpoll window on top of that: 33.5 reads, 2767 ms.
Also refuted structurally: there is NO I/O and no blocking call between the slot read and the CAW in the unlock loop, so the collision window is pure CPU and cannot be narrowed.

SESS380 MECHANISM, MEASURED ON BOTH SIDES OF THE SAME SLOT. The contended resource is not the transport and not a long holder doing real work -- it is that ONE 512B CAW slot is the single mutable cell holding a directory's ENTIRE lock state (holder bitmaps per mode, waiter bitmap, waiter_ex bitmap, yield ticket, generation). At 32 contenders, a waiter REGISTERING its waiter bit and the holder CLEARING its holder bit are COMPARE AND WRITE against the same word, so they invalidate each other. Both halves are now counted directly:
  RELEASE SIDE (P381-UNLK-CONTEND, new this session, fires only when the unlock CAS lost a race):
    112 contended unlocks in one 32-node shared-directory create run
    mean retries 1.96, mean MISCOMPAREs 1.96, mean backoff sleep 10.1 ms,
    mean unlock wall 27.9 ms, max 77 ms; the backoff sleep is 36% of that wall and the
    remaining 64% is the extra find_slot READ + CAW that each losing retry issues.
    78 of the 112 were on ino=131, the directory under test.
  ACQUIRE SIDE (P139-LOCKTOTAL -EAGAIN attribution, same run):
    121 acquire retries, of which 109 are ea_regwait -- LOST THE WAITER-REGISTER CAS --
    12 ea_compat, and ZERO ea_claim. The losses are on registering interest, not on
    claiming a free slot.
  HOLDER-SIDE COST BREAKDOWN (P138-BAST, ino=131): dur_us 26,565 / 36,542 / 42,830 / 48,457 with
    sx (the WIRE UNLOCK proper) = 25,976 / 32,919 / 40,624 / 46,384 us, i.e. 95-98% of the release.
    The mandatory drain pipeline (sa+sb+sc+sd) is only 2-4 ms of it. The release is not slow
    because of the durability work; it is slow because the unlock cannot win its own CAS.
THE FEEDBACK LOOP IS THE POINT: every waiter that registers extends the holder's release, the longer release lengthens the queue, and the longer queue brings more registering waiters. Cost is therefore superlinear in N, which is what the 1 -> 32 ladder shows (37 -> 1842 ms, 49.8x). This is precisely the failure mode the sess379 RULE: CONSULT ANOTHER MODEL WHEN STUCK review predicted for this format -- 'every successful update invalidates all competing comparisons ... N simultaneous distinct bit updates approach O(N^2) total work ... no backoff changes the serialization bound' -- and its prescribed fix is the same one that applies here: a writer GATE record plus incarnation-tagged PER-NODE reader records at independently writable locations, so registering interest writes to the node's OWN sector instead of CASing the shared word. See docs/rulings/hot-slot-caw-fix-shape.md.

SESS380 WHY THIS DEFECT RESISTED ATTRIBUTION FOR SO LONG -- TWO BLIND PROBES AND A BROKEN CONTROL, all three fixed this session. (1) P138-WAIT fires when ONE wait_for_grant call exceeds 5 ms, but a contended acquire is many sub-5 ms waits with outer retries between them: on a run whose creates measured p95 424 ms it produced FOUR lines fleet-wide. (2) P139-LOCKTOTAL brackets the whole acquire including retries -- the right probe -- but its floor was hardcoded at 800 ms, ABOVE the entire distribution, so it produced ZERO lines. It is now a knob (mxfs.caw_locktotal_ms, default unchanged at 800); at a 50 ms floor the same workload yields 118 acquires totalling 57.1 s, which matches the workload's own total create time -- i.e. the census now accounts for essentially all of the tail instead of 0.4% of it. (3) tests/caw_grant_wait_anatomy.sh only ever ran the PRIVATE shape and let each node mkdir inside the measured window, so it censused the parent inode's mkdir rather than the shared directory under test; it now takes SHAPE=shared|private, pre-creates every directory from one node, arms the P139 floor on all nodes and restores it, and harvests P139-LOCKTOTAL / P139-TAILCENSUS / P34-ACQ-SLOW as well as the per-wait probes. Any pre-sess380 number from these three tools understates the tail or measures the wrong resource.

SESS380 CLEAN LADDER, on a harness whose private arm is FINALLY a control. tests/create_scale_curve.sh was fixed this session to pre-create BOTH shapes' directories from one node; before that, every node in the `private` arm ran `mkdir -p $dirbase/r$i` INSIDE the measured window, so all P nodes took the same parent inode EX and both arms contended on a shared directory. That artifact is the most likely explanation for the two irreconcilable private-arm numbers already in this entry ('wall 33..41ms, FLAT in N' vs 'mean 5.2..191.8ms, 37x in N'). With the fix, 32 healthy nodes (all mounted, max loadavg 0.56, full 27/27 board green minutes earlier), fresh fs, 8 creates/node, MXFS 0.15.4 sv DACACDDE464B211CF68DE3F on SCST +caw-abort-reclaim.3:
  participants          1      2      4      8     16     32
  PRIVATE wall_p50     37    170    104    125    220    222  ms   <- 6.0x from 1 to 32
  PRIVATE mean        3.9   11.9   10.8   13.3   25.3   25.0  ms
  PRIVATE p50           4     12      8     10     16     19  ms
  PRIVATE p95           7     43     36     46     90     63  ms
  SHARED  wall_p50     37     87    160    385   1000   1842  ms   <- 49.8x from 1 to 32
  SHARED  mean        3.9    8.5   18.1   44.2  122.5  233.2  ms
  SHARED  p50           3      7      7      8     10     10  ms   <- FLAT in N
  SHARED  p95           8     31    105    305   1021   2170  ms   <- ALL the cost is here
SHARED vs PRIVATE at 32 nodes: 1842 vs 222 ms wall = 8.3x; 233.2 vs 25.0 ms mean = 9.3x; 2170 vs 63 ms p95 = 34x. So the shared-directory framing of this entry is CONFIRMED, at 8-34x rather than the previously recorded 42x, and it lives ENTIRELY IN THE TAIL -- the shared arm's p50 is 10 ms at 32 nodes, flat in N and no worse than the private arm's 19 ms. Every node pays roughly one multi-second stall per 8 creates. Separately, the private arm is NOT flat either (37 -> 222 ms, 6x), which is a smaller but real common-mode scaling cost that this entry should not lose sight of.

SESS380 STALL-SITE CENSUS ON THE FIXED TARGET (tests/create_stall_stacks.sh 8 32, 776 blocked samples at 50 ms across 32 nodes). Task state 77.7% S / 22.3% D. Nearest non-generic blocking frame:
  74.5%  mxfs_pal_cond_timedwait   (caw_lock_body <- mxfs_dlm_caw_lock <- mxfs_v5_dlm_inode_lock
                                     <- mxfs_dlm_inode_lock_routed <- mxfs_dlm_ilock_begin)
   9.8%  mxfs_dlm_ilock_begin      (xfs_ilock <- xfs_ilock_data_map_shared <- xfs_dir_lookup)
   7.0%  blk_execute_rq            (the SCSI READ(16)+FUA inside read_slot)
   1.5%  mxfs_pal_sleep_ms | 1.4% mxfs_inode_cluster_durable | 1.4% xfs_iget | 1.4% xfs_buf_iowait
This is the SAME verdict as the earlier census (then 75.3% caw_acquire_poll_sleep, since replaced by a condvar) and it is decisive for attribution: the cost is WAITING FOR A DLM GRANT on one directory inode, not transport. The transport share actually FELL from 14.2% to 7.0% once the target's wait-for cycle was fixed, and this entry's own CAW attempt census already measured CAW service time at 1.5% of grant wait with zero I/O errors. Do NOT re-attribute this defect to D-HOT-SLOT-CAW-SERIALIZES-LUN-PER-LBA-379 (DISPROVED sess380): that entry was about per-LBA command serialization at the target, which is now measured at 1.6x, while this is the DLM's own EX rotation among 32 contenders.

Measured on the live 32-node cluster, per-create latency, files written into per-node PRIVATE subdirectories of ONE shared parent so the only contended resource is the parent directory inode (tests/create_scale_curve.sh):
  participants   1     2     4     8    16    32
  p50  ms        5     6     7     8    12    11   <- FLAT in N
  mean ms      5.2   9.2  10.8  26.0  71.7 191.8   <- 37x in N
Shared-dir shape is only ~1.3x worse than private-subdir (247.9 vs 191.8 mean at 32), so dirent/leaf serialisation is SECONDARY; the cost is the parent inode lock. Native local-fs reference on the same nodes: 2.6ms mean. Uncontended MXFS is healthy at 5.2ms.
Stall site read off the kernel, not guessed (tests/create_stall_stacks.sh, 1005 blocked /proc/PID/stack samples): 75.3% caw_acquire_poll_sleep under mxfs_dlm_inode_lock_routed -> mxfs_v5_dlm_inode_lock -> mxfs_dlm_caw_lock -> caw_wait_for_grant; 14.2% read_slot's SCSI READ(16)+FUA; 4.2% ilock.
CAW attempt census per logical grant (tests/caw_grant_wait_anatomy.sh, the measurement GPT named as decisive): CAW submissions mean 6.1 max 33; miscompares mean 5.1 max 32; io errors 0; CAW SERVICE TIME 617ms = 1.5% of 42.1s of grant wait; slot poll READs mean 52.6 max 223. So the wait is ~52 poll cycles per grant, NOT transport service time (1.5%) and NOT CAS throughput (~1.2% at 0.65ms per CAW). The contended resource is ONE directory inode with mixed demand: measured slot masks ino=131 req_mode=PR waiters=0xfb4dffff waiters_ex=0x28440804 holders_pr=0x4820000 holders_ex=0 => 28 waiters of which 6 want EX, 3 hold PR, none holds EX.

sess43 ROUND DECOMPOSITION (new, tests/drc_phase_census.py over all 32 nodes' DRCph kmsg markers, 0.11.353, 286 phase samples): round wall median 9.16s. Segments (median s, share): create-start->sync1 1.97 (20%), wave1->wave2 1.71 (17%), create-done->wrbar 2.51 (25%, the write-barrier WAIT = cross-node skew), wrbar->presync 0.72 (7%), presync->dc 1.03 (10%, drop_caches), dc-real->ls 1.04 (11%, cold ls), ls->lookups 0.52 (5%), verify->rm 0.34 (3%). CREATES + THEIR BARRIER WAIT = 6.2s = 68% of the round. Cross-node wall spread median 1.97s. Cost model that fits: 2 create-waves x 32 nodes = 64 directory-EX turns/round at ~50ms/turn (matches the prior P138 clean-handoff 13ms + queueing, and the 12.7-54ms wire-unlock CAW figure) ~= 3.2s.

sess43 LEVER A/B REFUTED: dir_ex_batch_grace_ms 10/60/150 at 32/caw gave 7/6/5 rounds — longer grace is monotonically WORSE (waiter pile-up), confirming the sess39 finding on a current build. Holding the tenure longer is NOT the lever.

sess43 CONFOUNDER FOUND — HOST LOAD modulates this criterion and invalidates uncontrolled A/Bs. Same build 0.11.353, same day: 8-10 rounds/100s at hypervisor load 11-17 (morning board) vs 5-7 rounds at load 28-30 (Wow.exe 384%% + worldserver 315%% + other tenants); guest-internal load stayed <1 while steal accumulated (test1 steal=7851 ticks). A fresh re-prep at high load still gave 7 then 6, so this is NOT mount-degradation-with-use and NOT the grace parameter. The ~1-round margin over DRC_MIN_ROUNDS=8 is thin enough that host contention alone crosses it — which is why the historical failures cluster in high-load windows. MITIGATION SHIPPED: run.sh now stamps hostload= into every recorded result so pace numbers are comparable and A/B arms under drifting load are detectable.

sess43 STAMPED PACE SERIES (0.11.354, 32/caw, hostload now recorded with every result): hostload=24.24 -> 44 checks = 6 rounds (FAIL, under the 8 floor); hostload=19.69 -> 65 checks = 9 rounds (PASS). Together with the unstamped morning data (load 11-17 -> 8-10 rounds) and the high-load block (load 28-30 -> 5-7 rounds, including after a full re-prep), the relationship is monotonic across ~15 runs on two builds: this criterion's margin over DRC_MIN_ROUNDS=8 is roughly one round, and hypervisor contention alone moves it by 3-4 rounds. Any future pace claim MUST cite its hostload= stamp; comparisons across different loads are meaningless.

sess126 ROOT CAUSE PROVEN BY DIRECT WALL ATTRIBUTION (0.11.452/A1C4A05CB6356F02B8625F6, fleet-confirmed). NEW TOOL tests/cc_stackprof.sh + tests/mxfs_stackprof.py: 20Hz /proc/PID/task/*/stack sampling, 8 nodes, 30310 ticks/34300 samples of a virgin-fs crash_consistency run. 26.28% of ALL samples are mxfs_pal_cond_timedwait < caw_nudge_wait < caw_wait_for_grant < mxfs_dlm_caw_lock < mxfs_v5_dlm_inode_lock; 16.59% are open_last_lookups (queued behind it on the local dir i_rwsem); 39.61% do_wait + 13.59% pipe_read are the parent shells on those same children. Device path, CAS contention and AG locks are ABSENT (<2%). So ~100% of workload blocking wall is the CAW INODE grant wait. THE CONTENDED INODE IS THE MOUNT ROOT, ino 128 (stat /mnt/shared) -- NOT the shared test directory (.crash_consistency = ino 29360256 took ONE >5ms grant, 294ms, all run). Every prior session chased the wrong inode. P138-WAIT is ALWAYS-ON (dlm_caw.c:5918, INODE, >5ms, capped 4000/boot) -- instr=1 is UNNECESSARY and perturbs hard (86s run -> >240s). New harness tests/cc_grantwait.sh arm|disarm|report. 202 grant waits >5ms cluster-wide: ino 128 mode=3(PR) 202 grants, 713681ms summed, mean 3533ms, ffw_share 100%, caw_svc_ms 0.8% of wall, caw_miss p50=0. P139-TAILCENSUS n=172: bit_lost=0 (NOT queue-position loss), chosen nonzero 3/172, free_defer 2/172, foreign_yt p50=15 in ALL 172, doze250 p50=15 in ALL 172 => 15 x MXFS_CAW_DEFER_POLL_MS(250) = 3750ms. THE PROOF -- P204-YT-DEFER raw, test5, ino=128, 12 consecutive samples spanning 3 seconds: yt=20000 FROZEN, hpr=8209288 (7 PR holders) BIT-IDENTICAL AND FROZEN, hex=0 (nobody holds EX), wex=27da0000 (10 EX waiters), w growing, age_ms 2037->4980 then the 5000ms MXFS_CAW_YIELD_TIMEOUT_MS stale-ticket valve fires and the cycle repeats. Ticket age at defer ino=128 n=1141: p50=2873 p90=4588 max=4994ms. Queue shape: waiters 19.2, waiters_ex 10.5, holders_ex 0.00, holders_pr 6.79. modes: 3=PR, 5=EX. MECHANISM: (1) a node wants EX on the mount root -- on a virgin fs `mkdir -p $MNT/.crash_consistency` races on all 32 nodes, and the dir is never removed, which is why the SECOND run is fast (sess125's empty-dir recipe was a correct observation with the wrong explanation). (2) A yield ticket is armed for that EX waiter. (3) The 7 PR holders DO NOT RELEASE under the EX BAST for 3+ seconds -- stack evidence 'msleep < mxfs_drain_ilock_read < mxfs_dlm_bast_process < mxfs_dlm_bast_work_fn': the release path drains local ilock readers while all 32 nodes path-walk the root continuously for their dd/md5sum opens, so new readers arrive faster than the drain retires them (read-side livelock; nothing bars new readers once a BAST is pending). (4) Meanwhile every PR requester -- COMPATIBLE with the existing PR holders, hex=0 -- is forced to defer on the foreign EX ticket (strict writer preference) and dozes 250ms at a time. (5) Nothing progresses until the 5s valve fires. The system runs on its safety valve. sess24 already documented half of this at dlm_caw.c:155-245 (mxfs_caw_pr_batch_nodefer, default 0): 'a PR requester is COMPATIBLE the whole time and defers purely on policy: strict writer preference, unbounded... yt_age is the wrong clock, the release path re-arms yield_set_ms whenever the ticket VALUE changes.' sess126 confirms it on the ROOT inode at 32 nodes and supplies the other half: the EX waiter the ticket guards can never be granted either.

sess127 (0.11.452/A1C4A05CB6356F02B8625F6, VIRGIN fs, hostload 12.68 = quiet rig) RE-ROOTED this at the BAST RECEIVE path and REFUTED the sess126 ilock hypothesis. The run FAILED at 90s/90s. NEW INSTRUMENTS: tests/cc_bastcensus.sh (holder side: pairs the always-on P70-BP ENTRY/EXIT=full by realns and prints a STALLED/UNDELIVERED/CHURN discriminator) and a FOCUS section added to tests/mxfs_stackprof.py + cc_stackprof.sh agg (tick occupancy + full signatures for stacks containing mxfs_dlm_bast*/mxfs_drain_ilock_read, i.e. the release side isolated from the requester side). REFUTATIONS: P132-ILOCK-STUCK/-TIMEOUT = 0 on ALL 32 nodes; FOCUS = 1.18% of 30231 ticks over 8 nodes; msleep<mxfs_drain_ilock_read<bast_process = 4 of 724 focus samples (0.55%) -- the ilock drain is NOT the blocker. P36 is also not the cause: 295 P36-MHT-REARM on ino=128 with pr=0 ex=0 pin=0 in 295 of 295 (so the firing predicate is the unprinted i_dlm_acq_inflight>0), strikes max=10 (~80ms/episode) vs the 2500 strikeout. HOLDER CENSUS ino=128: P70-BP ENTRY=332 EXIT=full=158; ENTRY mode PR=137 NL=187(no-op) EX=8; ENTRY->EXIT release wall p50=319ms p90=1670ms p99=3802ms max=5093ms, >=250ms in 53.2%, >=1000ms in 35; held_ms at BAST entry p50=92203ms (the root tenure spans the WHOLE run). Only 145 real PR/EX release pipelines cluster-wide in 90s = ~1.6 handoffs/s for an inode 19 nodes are queued on -- the limiter is handoff RATE, not release cost. THE ROOT, from FOCUS full signatures (724 samples): 35.22% (255) blk_execute_rq<scsi_execute_cmd<mxfs_pal_scsi_read_fua_bdev<mxfs_pal_bdev_read_prio<read_slot<find_slot_skip<mxfs_dlm_caw_held<mxfs_v5_dlm_inode_held<mxfs_dlm_bast_notify<v5_bast_cb<bast_recv_fn; +4.14% (30) the same read under mxfs_caw_orphan_forensic; +0.97% (7) under caw_count_resource_slots<mxfs_dlm_caw_self_held_scan. => ~43% of ALL DLM release-side blocked wall is the single-threaded UDP BAST receive thread doing synchronous SCSI slot reads INLINE. bast_recv_fn (dlm_caw.c:10640) is one thread per node and calls ctx->bast_cb() synchronously inside the recvfrom loop; mxfs_dlm_caw_held() (dlm_caw.c:8493) answers 'do I hold this resource?' -- a question about our OWN bit -- via find_slot() -> a shared-LUN read -> node_held_mode(slot, ctx->node_bit), while the node already keeps ctx->held.slots[]/held.count under held.lock in memory (bast_poll_fn iterates exactly that list) and XFS has ip->i_dlm_mode. CONSEQUENCE MEASURED: test5 /proc/net/snmp Udp InErrors=8085 RcvbufErrors=8085 -- every UDP error on the node is a receive-buffer OVERFLOW, i.e. BAST hints are being SILENTLY DROPPED -- and the socket is NOT under-buffered (mxfs_pal_udp_open, pal/linux/kern.c:2420-2426, already sets sk_rcvbuf=4MB + SOCK_RCVBUF_LOCK from sess8), so overflowing 4MB means the thread stalls for seconds. This closes the loop on every earlier number: the holders are not refusing to release, THEY HAVE NOT BEEN TOLD -- sess126's hpr mask bit-identical for 3s, age_ms 2037->4980 before the 5000ms stale-ticket valve, mean grant wait 3533ms, and ~1.6 handoffs/s are all consistent with multi-second BAST delivery latency plus outright hint loss. PRECEDENT MISSED: dlm_caw.h:311-322 (sess35 NUDGE v2) states this exact mechanism for the GRANT NUDGE path -- 'v1 grant nudges woke EVERY blocked acquirer on every node; each did a READ(16)+FUA re-check, and at a 32-node single-dir create convoy those ~28 serialized reads at the one SCSI target WERE the measured ~21.6ms per-handoff latency' -- and fixed it with wake_mask so receivers skip the disk read. The BAST path never got the same treatment.

2026-08-04 sess130 — MEASURED ON 0.11.453 (BAST dispatch queue live, fleet-confirmed F20024E38213A9E64DB6718), VIRGIN fs, quiet console. FIRST, A CONFOUND THAT INVALIDATES THE MAGNITUDES OF THE sess126 BASELINE: tests/cc_grantwait.sh arm|mark and tests/cc_bastcensus.sh mark ran `dmesg -n 8`, raising console_loglevel to 8 so every mxfs pr_warn is pushed synchronously to each VM's EMULATED isa-serial console (backed by a host log file). run.sh's prep_cluster sets kernel.printk='1 4 1 1' precisely to avoid this; the mark harnesses silently reversed it. `dmesg -n 8` buys NOTHING for harvesting (printk always stores to the ring buffer; console level gates only the console). defects.summary: readdir of a directory a peer created costs ~1.2 s per directory; every other syscall on the same inode costs milliseconds
defects.evidence: MEASURED 32/caw, build 0.11.243 C3D864E1F8AB80753D23D6C, tests/shared_unlink_pace.sh. 32 empty directories in one shared parent, each created by a different node which still holds it cached; then one pass from test1, one syscall class per fresh tree so nothing is confounded: stat 133 ms total (4 ms/op) | open(O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY) 1463 ms (45 ms/op) | rmdir 3846 ms (120 ms/op) | opendir+getdents (`ls -f`) 39701 ms (1240 ms/op). Independently reproduced standalone: 32 dirs, readdir-only pass = 37495 ms (1172 ms/op). CONTROL: the identical 32 children created LOCALLY by the same node and removed by it = 152 ms total (4 ms/op) -- so the shared parent is not the bottleneck and neither is the removal. RULE: TIMEOUTS ARE PERFORMANCE ASSERTIONS, NOT SAFETY NETS: native XFS readdir of an empty directory is microseconds; this is ~10^5x over the ceiling.
defects.mechanism: ROOT PROVEN (RULE: TROUBLESHOOTING IS A LOOP, NOT A GUESS step 2b), build 0.11.245 6764F19681F7272375144DA. xfs/xfs_dir2_readdir.c:1005 -- `for (p48_try = 0; p48_try < 200 && dp->i_dlm_stale && !shutdown; p48_try++) { msleep(1); dp->i_dlm_stale = true; mxfs_dlm_reload_inode(dp, ..., true); }`. 200 x msleep(1) is ~1.2 s at this kernel's timer granularity, which is EXACTLY the observed cost and explains its stability (1201-1215 ms on every sample: the loop always runs its full bound). IT CAN NEVER SUCCEED ON THIS PATH: xfs_readdir holds ILOCK_SHARED across iteration, so the reload's write acquire is blocked by THIS task -- sess14 proved that and made mxfs_dlm_reload_inode bail immediately with P173-RELOAD-SELFREAD. It returns with i_dlm_stale still set, and the loop body re-arms the flag before each attempt, so all 200 rounds bail. P173 was the top probe in the capture (110 lines over 32 dirs = the ratelimited count of 200/dir). The loop's own comment ("ILOCK holds here are sub-ms so waiting is safe") is about OTHER holders; it does not cover the caller being the blocker, which is the case that actually occurs. SUPPORTING MEASUREMENTS: a phase-split probe on P62 showed mxfs_dlm_reload_inode itself costs tot_ms=0/pre_ms=0/bp_ms=0, so the cost is the sleeping, not the reload. Timed per syscall from python (a real open, not bash's `exec 9<` which returns EISDIR on a directory and made an earlier 45 ms 'open' row meaningless): stat=4ms open=0ms getdents=1202ms close=0ms. REFUTED en route: the pre-readdir wait loop at pal/linux/xfs_file.c:1888 -- its probe P95D-READDIR-WAIT is present in the module (strings) and fired ZERO times.

defects.summary: The heartbeat monitor overwrites a KNOWN nonzero cached victim incarnation with 0 when the sector reads 0, treating 'unknown' as an observation.  That is information loss, not an update: it launders an incarnation MISMATCH into the 'never observed' arm, so the next death round publishes a recovery that cannot name which incarnation it is recovering.
defects.evidence: MEASURED sess91 on the live 32-node rig.  With nt->last_epoch holding the victim's real incarnation 1634619062121349274, a sector whose epoch read 0 drove the epoch-change arm to rebase nt->last_epoch to 0 (disklock.c:1156 rebase_epoch, applied at :1358).  Round 1 correctly refused: 'P237-RECOV-INC-MISMATCH ... victim_inc=1634619062121349274 slot_inc=0 ... refusing to publish'.  Round 2, with the cached value now destroyed, took the opposite branch on the SAME facts: 'P237-RECOV-INC-UNOBSERVED slot=4 victim=4085327405 on-disk=0 — the caller never observed the victim's incarnation' and published 'P234-RECOV-FENCED ... epoch=0'.  The caller HAD observed it, 62 seconds earlier, and said so in the log.
defects.mechanism: dlm/disklock.c:1147 fires the epoch-change arm on any difference including a transition to 0; :1156 sets rebase_epoch = rhb->epoch unconditionally and :1358 commits it into nt->last_epoch.  There is no inc_valid() test on the incoming value, so 'known E1' + 'observed UNKNOWN' resolves to UNKNOWN instead of retaining E1 and flagging the sector as inconsistent.  A transition E1 -> E2 (both nonzero) may establish supersession under the sess86 rules; a transition E1 -> 0 cannot establish anything.  Related: the P237-RECOV-INC-UNOBSERVED text calls the sector 'the authority for which incarnation last owned this slice' — the sector is authoritative for SLOT state, but 0 is not an authoritative incarnation under inc_valid(); it is an authoritative statement that the incarnation is unavailable.
defects.containment: None.  Both branches log correctly and neither reports the downgrade, so the contradiction is only visible by reading the two rounds together.

defects.summary: CONFIRMED BY DIRECT MEASUREMENT (sess93).  A PREEMPT AND ABORT excludes the victim only at the INSTANT it completes.  Seconds later the same node re-registers with a fresh key and writes to the shared LUN — so for the entire duration of the foreign-slice replay that the fence certificate authorises, the only thing keeping a partitioned victim off the shared metadata is that victim's OWN cooperative self-fence.
evidence: STEP 1 baseline — victim writes LBA 131087 with 0xa5: rc=0, post-read matches.  The victim can write before the fence, so the rest of the probe is meaningful.

STEP 2 — test1 issues sg_persist --out --preempt-abort --param-rk=0x434d2436 --param-sark=0x37e3d796 --prout-type=5: rc=0, and READ KEYS then shows 0 descriptors matching 0x37e3d796.  The victim's registration is gone.

STEP 3 — victim writes LBA 131087 with 0x5a: rc=1, and the pre-read still shows a5 a5 a5...  REFUSED.  Exclusion genuinely works at that instant, which is what the certificate claims and all it claims.

STEP 4a — victim issues sg_persist --out --register-ignore --param-sark=0xfeed0001: rc=0.  THE TARGET ACCEPTED THE RE-REGISTRATION.  Nothing in SPC forbids REGISTER_AND_IGNORE from an unregistered initiator, and the WE-RO reservation does not prevent it.
STEP 4b — victim writes LBA 131087 with 0x33: rc=0, post-read '33 33 33 33 33 33 33 33'.  THE WRITE LANDED.  A node the cluster had just fenced put bytes on the shared LUN.

dlm/scsipr.c — MXFS's only defence is cooperative: mxfs_scsipr_self_check notices the key is gone and the node force-shuts-down (MXFS_FENCE_KIND_SELF_PREEMPTED / P131-SELF-FENCE, explicitly 'no auto-re-register').  That requires the victim's kernel to still be running and still scheduling — precisely what is in doubt about a node just declared dead by 62 s of missed heartbeats.

defects.mechanism: The certificate records a true fact with a SHELF LIFE, and nothing enforces the interval it is consumed over. A pre-0.11.422 binary mounting the same filesystem still replays foreign slices ungated and still mints uncertified FENCED/NONE descriptors, so one old node in the cluster reinstates D-VICTIM-REPLAY-WITHOUT-PROVEN-EXCLUSION for every slice it is elected to replay. 0.11.422 retired mxfs_disklock_recovery_begin() in THIS build only; the same function in a deployed older build is unmodified and still writes stage=FENCED with fence_kind=NONE.

Existing uncertified FENCED/NONE records left on disk by older builds are refused by the new gate (mxfs_recov_cert_proves_exclusion -> 'fence_kind does not prove exclusion') but are not quarantined, so they persist as descriptors that block their slot forever with no operator-visible reason.

CODE FACT: the mechanism already exists in-tree and was simply never applied to the 0.11.422 change. Three-layer C7 gate: (1) XFS_SB_FEAT_INCOMPAT_MXFS_PROTOGATE bit 30 (xfs/libxfs/xfs_format.h:412), set by mkfs_mxfs, in XFS_SB_FEAT_INCOMPAT_ALL — pre-gate kernels inherit upstream's unknown-incompat refusal (one-shot, preventative only); (2) envelope MXFS_FORMAT_F_PROTOGATE + cluster_proto_gen, enforced == MXFS_PROTO_GEN at pal/linux/xfs_super.c:3014-3029 with -EPROTONOSUPPORT plus a half-upgraded-format check; (3) disklock HB feature block — P-VERGATE-JOIN (-EPROTO) join refusal and monitor P-VERGATE-FENCE (dlm/disklock.c:1289, 2509). MXFS_PROTO_GEN is 3 (include/mxfs/mxfs_super.h:90); it went 1->2 at sess75 for recovery-descriptor v2 and 2->3 at sess86 for the nonzero mount incarnation. THE 0.11.422 CERTIFIED-REPLAY GATE DID NOT BUMP IT, so a pre-0.11.422 / post-incarnation binary is gen 3, is admitted by all three layers, and performs exactly the ungated replay this entry describes. The sess74 ruling quoted at include/mxfs/mxfs_super.h:56-88 and dlm/disklock.h:293-304 applies verbatim: per-record fail-closed is no substitute because the old replayer REPLAYS FIRST and consults the descriptor only afterwards. RULE: CONSULT ANOTHER MODEL WHEN STUCK RULING (sess131, gpt-5.6-sol; full text in docs/rulings/protogen4-and-quarantine.md): MXFS_PROTO_GEN 3->4 is APPROVED and REQUIRED — the certified-replay rule is a cluster protocol generation change even though the descriptor encoding is byte-identical, because the set of permitted participants and writes changed. FOUR MANDATORY BLOCKERS before this entry may close: (B1) recovery must be unreachable until envelope admission — a gen-3 kernel could begin foreign replay before discovering the envelope says 4, and layer 3 cannot repair replay that already happened; require an immutable proto_admitted mount-state bit asserted at EVERY recovery entry point, and audit normal mount, remount/retry, partial-mount error recovery, deferred recovery workers, mount-time XFS journal recovery callbacks, snapshot/secondary-sb paths, and administrative recover-only entry points. (B2) 3->4 must be an OFFLINE CLUSTER TRANSITION, not an offline metadata write: an already-mounted or suspended gen-3 node does not reread the envelope and may resume and replay before the gen-4 monitor fences it — stop/unmount every member, take an exclusive maintenance/storage lease, revoke/preempt all old PR registrations, invalidate the old membership epoch, and keep suspended nodes off the LUN until remount. (B3) the generation update must be a crash-safe activation transaction: all authoritative envelope copies written with FUA/flush, an unambiguous interrupted-upgrade state, and readers FAIL CLOSED on disagreement rather than picking an older valid copy. (B4) gen 4 names a BEHAVIORAL CONTRACT — certified-replay check, descriptor-write restrictions and mount ordering are conformance requirements for any build claiming 4, with mixed-build tests proving every gen-3 build is rejected BEFORE recovery starts. ROLLOUT: 'accept N and N-1 read-only' is REJECTED as unsafe — a read-only mount may still perform journal recovery and foreign replay IS mount-time recovery. Hard refusal is the correct default. LIMITATION that must be written into the upgrade procedure: the bump is PROSPECTIVE; it does not prove no gen-3 node already performed an ungated replay, and the ABSENCE of a stale FENCED/NONE descriptor is not proof of safety because an unsafe replay may have completed and been purged. Finding legacy or suspicious recovery records must trigger scrub/fsck and an operator-visible 'previously exposed to ungated replay' status.

2026-08-04 sess131 — QUARANTINE DESIGN (next_step item 2) RULED UNSOUND AS PROPOSED. I proposed that any survivor durably set MXFS_RECOV_F_QUARANTINED (dlm/disklock.h:357) on a legacy uncertified FENCED/NONE descriptor, since today such a descriptor merely fails mxfs_recov_cert_proves_exclusion() with reason 'fence_kind does not prove exclusion' (dlm/disklock.c:3483) and blocks its slot forever with no operator-visible reason. REJECTED. (B5) 'one-way and strictly more restrictive' is NOT a substitute for write authority: a survivor can hold a stale sector image and race the victim's heartbeat update, a recovery owner advancing or replacing the descriptor, a purge or reuse for a NEW incarnation, another survivor becoming owner, or a sector-level read-modify-write over unrelated fields — overwriting newer state, quarantining a REUSED slot, or corrupting the CRC-protected sector. (B6) a survivor must not write the victim's sector before the victim is excluded; proven exclusion is required for ANY survivor-side descriptor mutation unless an independent atomic quarantine location exists that the victim never writes. Owner-only quarantine is acceptable ONLY with ownership acquired via the existing owner/epoch protocol, identity + incarnation + sequence + expected-old-contents revalidated at commit, the same durable/conditional serialization as other descriptor advances, and victim-sector write safety already established. OTHERWISE the correct runtime behavior is: refuse replay, leave the descriptor UNCHANGED, and publish a persistent health event / named rate-limited alert. (B7) no disposition or repair model exists yet for legacy obligations — an unmarked blocked descriptor is NOT equivalent to a quarantined one, because the unmarked one can still be repaired by future software while the terminal flag forbids it; choose ONE policy first: permanent abandonment, certified reconstruction (fresh certified exclusion, revalidate identity/incarnation and journal state AFTER exclusion, build a NEW recovery transaction, never bless the old NONE descriptor), or offline administrative discharge. DO NOT add a generic clear-quarantine operation. UPGRADER: chk_mxfs --upgrade-protogate should INVENTORY AND REPORT, not auto-quarantine — scan all descriptor locations and redundant copies, classify each, emit a durable report naming slot/victim identity/incarnation/stage/reason, and offer leave-unresolved-and-activate, an explicit destructive --quarantine-legacy, or a designed reconstruction. (B8) it must NEVER synthesize a fence certificate because the tool believes the cluster is offline; administrative offline status is not proof the victim was excluded at the relevant time. Explicitly REJECTED: refusing the whole generation upgrade whenever a NONE descriptor exists — leaving the volume at gen 3 preserves an old binary's ability to mount and replay ungated, which is strictly worse.

defects.summary: incident474 arm B: the 8-node arm-A wedge was NOT contained - it cascaded to total 32-node fleet collapse within ~7 minutes (last survivor test1 withdrew 15:56:19Z). Survivors correctly fenced/replayed/purged the victims, but (1) victim-held EX inode locks stayed unreclaimable after purge, (2) withdrawn victims KEPT SENDING network announces - test21's retired identity was still heartbeating 6 minutes after being purged, and (3) the 'holders alive' liveness extension used those announces to stretch survivor lock waits to the 480s cap on locks whose holders were dead filesystems - so replayers died one by one until none remained.
defects.evidence: sess209 forensics on tests/evidence/incident474/*.klog.gz (10-node UTC klogs collected before state disturbed): survivors show P238-FENCE-DONE + P163-RECOVERY-PENDING for victim slots, then their own lock waits extended to 480s on inodes whose EX holder had withdrawn; test21's node identity observed announcing 6min post-purge; test1 (last survivor, elected replayer) timed out after 360s waiting EX on ino 12585558 (held by wedged test14) and withdrew 15:56:19Z.
defects.mechanism: Three cooperating non-containment holes, all evidence-backed: (a) purge of a dead node does not reclaim/invalidate the EX inode locks it held (or reclamation is gated on a drain the dead holder can never complete); (b) a withdrawn node's network announce path keeps running after withdraw - shutdown does not stop the announcer, so its identity stays 'alive' to peers; (c) the liveness extension trusts announces alone ('holder is alive') without checking the holder's fs is still mounted/serviceable, converting a dead holder into a 480s wait instead of an immediate reclaim.
defects.containment: None. Any multi-node wedge that triggers shutdown becomes a fleet-wide outage; defeats the purpose of per-node fencing/recovery.

Fix must make the oracle distinguish 'HB thread alive' from 'fs serviceable' (e.g. victim self-reports wedge/shutdown state in its HB record, or extension capped when holder's grant has not progressed). 3) Hole (b) PROVEN sess213 (recovery ordering deadlock, see hole_b_evidence_sess213). 4) DONE sess214: RULE: CONSULT ANOTHER MODEL WHEN STUCK ruling received (gpt-5.6-sol; docs/rulings/incident474-fix-set.md). No observation of the cascade on a smaller cluster exists, so observed is 32. WHAT WAS MEASURED AT 8 AND 4 NODES (tests/multi_victim_containment.sh, written for this record: two nodes taken down together under a load that shares a parent directory with them, and a verdict on whether the survivors contained it). Queue j30a on 0.90.30, laps 10-17, eight laps, all PASS. Victims power-cut: 8/tcp three times, 4/tcp, 8/cawd, 4/cawd. Victims WITHDRAWN (KILL_MODE=withdraw: the filesystem forced down with its log unflushed and the node left up, the state of the incident's eight nodes behind their wedge): 8/tcp (lap 14, tests/evidence/multi_victim/20260929T200523Z_8tcp_j30a_wt2) and 8/cawd (lap 15, the directory ending _8cawd_j30a_wc2). In both withdraw laps each victim stamped its withdrawal (P163-WITHDRAW-STAMP rc=0), the six survivors replayed both slices (8/tcp at +78 s and +84 s, 8/cawd at +18 s and +23 s), kept their mounts, logged no shutdown and no fault, met no load error and stalled 63-77 s (tcp) and 3-4 s (cawd) against a budget of 240 s; chk_mxfs 0. Queue h29a (0.90.29) had passed six power-cut laps of the same kind. So at 8 and 4 nodes two nodes leaving together, dead or withdrawn, were contained on both transports in 14 laps of 14. NOT EXERCISED AT ANY SIZE: a node that is WEDGED and has not withdrawn (hole c: its heartbeat thread beats while its filesystem serves nothing); every victim of these laps lost power or declared its death. OBSERVED IN LAP 14, OF HOLE (c)'S FAMILY: toward a withdrawn node that keeps its TCP connection a request times out rather than fails to send, and one inode acquire on each survivor spent its whole budget of 60 attempts in timeouts (P-ACQ-LADDER-END rc=-110 timeouts=59 transport=0, 61.4 s, ending 4 s before the first replay); the callers retried and nothing reached an application. With eight victims at 32 nodes the replays end later than one budget, so the next measurement of this record is the same harness at 32 nodes with eight withdrawn victims, read for acquires that end -110 and for what their callers then do.

defects.mechanism: IDENTIFIED (sess232, forensic — repro pending): foreign-replay ATOMIC-SKIP over a PARTIALLY-WRITTEN-HOME committed victim txn. test13 foreign-replayed the 12 victims' slices; ALL 29 txns were P227-FR-ATOMIC-SKIPped (every one contained untagged inode images — inode log items carry no authority tokens, so the #1 containment skips essentially every real txn). Token decode (AG base daddr = ag*4186440; off 2=AGI, 24=inobt root, 32=finobt root) shows skipped AGI+inobt+finobt txns for EXACTLY AG1 (victim slots 1@23:19:31, 26@23:21:02) and AG4 (slots 28@23:21:14, 29@23:21:27x2) — the two damaged AGs — plus AG5 (slot 5, UNdamaged). Victims committed the free txns, their AILs wrote AGI+finobt home but not inobt, then withdrew; the skip abandoned the only completion path. AG5 = all-or-none writeback, no damage: the discriminator. Skip paths in ifree exonerated by code audit: difree+iunlink_remove are ONE txn (xfs_inode_uninit), preflight logs nothing, -ESTALE fires before first mod. defects.mechanism: SESS481 EVIDENCE CORRECTION — ANY INFERENCE IN THIS RECORD THAT RESTS ON THE PRESENCE OF P165-AFFINE-STALE LINES MUST BE RE-DERIVED.  That probe is VACUOUS on every build up to and including 0.64.37: measured over one full 32-node crash_consistency row, 229,444 of 229,444 P165 lines carried d_time=0 — 100.0%, with dp_epoch=1 on 99.2%.  The cause is structural, not statistical: d_time is stamped in exactly ONE place (pal/linux/xfs_super.c, the ret==1 tail of the coordinated validation) and the affine fast path RETURNS BEFORE REACHING IT, so a dentry taking that exit is never stamped, keeps d_time=0, and can never equal an epoch that starts at 1 (xfs_mxfs_dlm.c:38672 sets i_dlm_epoch=1 for exactly that reason).  The probe therefore fires on EVERY affine fast-path blessing of a never-validated dentry — about 8% of the entire kernel log — and cannot distinguish a resurrected stale dentry from a brand-new one, which is the only distinction it was written to make.  CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS RECORD: 'P165-AFFINE-STALE lines are present at the failure second' establishes NOTHING, because those lines are present at essentially every second on every node.  A P165 line naming a SPECIFIC name/ino still places an affine fast-path blessing of that name at that moment, which may remain useful as a positional fact, but it is NOT evidence that the dentry was stale.  0.65.0 fixes the probe to fire only when d_time != 0 && d_time != epoch — a dentry that DID pass coordinated validation at one epoch being blessed under another, which is the real resurrection signature — and counts the fresh population separately as P165-AFFINE-FRESH so the denominator stays visible.  Evidence from 0.65.0 onward is admissible; evidence from before it is not. || OPEN -- observed, not proven. What the capture establishes: the double-free is on the FREE side, in the deferred-ops drain of a truncate (do_truncate from an O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_TRUNC open by a shell redirect -> xfs_setattr_size -> xfs_itruncate_extents_flags -> xfs_bunmapi_range -> xfs_defer_finish -> xfs_extent_free_finish_item -> __xfs_free_extent -> xfs_free_ag_extent), i.e. an EFI completed for an extent that is already recorded free. The AGF was otherwise coherent (agf_freeblks=523271 agf_longest=523268 matching pagf), so this is one wrong extent, not a wrecked AG. SEQUENCE ON THE FENCED NODE (its own dmesg, monotonic): t=15613.80 P236-SELF-FENCE slot=10 'our heartbeat slot was taken over by a recovery' + P131-SELF-FENCE reason=SLOT_TAKEOVER (this is fence_during_write doing its job) -> t=15618.16 remounted, 'mount recovery barrier complete cohort=0x0 late=0x0 replayed=0 published=0x0 quarantined=0x0' -> workload -> t=15801.45 the free fails. Immediately before the failure the same inode number had been FREED AND RE-BOUND on this node: P140-RECLAIM-COMMIT, P144-EPOCH-FREE-RESET ino=41943174 slot=33094 'cleared stale dir_epoch/last_ex_slot at inode free', P141-UNLK-EXCLR ino=41943174, then P-RELOAD-IDENTICAL ino=41943174 cc=10 gen=4087327847 fmt=2 nx=1 size=6742 (twice), then P165-AFFINE-STALE name=f4 ino=41943174 dp=41943168 child_gen=4087327847. LEADING HYPOTHESES, NONE INSTRUMENTED YET: (a) the fenced node's own abandoned journal-slice intents -- a peer replayed its slice while it was fenced and an EFI is completed twice, once by the replayer and once by the rejoined node (D-FOREIGN-SLICE-INTENTS-ABANDONED is exactly this shape and is OPEN); (b) stale in-core BMAP surviving the fence/rejoin so the truncate unmaps extents a peer already freed (the P-RELOAD-IDENTICAL / P165-AFFINE-STALE lines put a reused inode at the scene); (c) the extent was freed by the fenced node's own pre-fence dirty state and again after rejoin. RULE: TROUBLESHOOTING IS A LOOP, NOT A GUESS: instrument before patching -- the EFI/EFD provenance of the failing extent is the measurement that separates (a) from (b). || OCCURRENCE 2 ADDS: (d) the alloc side fails the same way, so any hypothesis must explain BOTH a free of an already-free extent and a size-tree/bnobt disagreement at allocation -- that is one inconsistent free-space picture, not two bugs. (e) Occurrence 2 had NO fence, NO refusal and NO quarantine: it was the first board group after a prep_cluster that itself followed a 31-node prep and several destroyed/restarted VMs. That points at the mkfs/mount boundary rather than at recovery. The known hazard there is documented in the harness itself (tests/setup/prep_node.sh step 5b): the block device buffer cache SURVIVES umount+rmmod, so a peer that does not re-mkfs can mount on top of stale OLD-filesystem pages; prep_node.sh runs `blockdev --flushbufs` before every mount for exactly this reason, but it only WARNs if that fails. Occurrence 2's directory symptoms fit a stale metadata view: a P26-DSCAN-MISS storm on ino=8388765 (428 dirents scanned, name not in any data block), P21H-LEAFHOLE, P26-REBUILD-OK, then the alloc error one millisecond later. NOT PROVEN -- prep_node.sh's flushbufs may well have succeeded on every node; the measurement below is what decides it. || THIRD HYPOTHESIS, ADDED THE SAME SESSION AND CURRENTLY THE ONE I WOULD TEST FIRST: (f) the HOST STORAGE was degrading under both occurrences. Twenty minutes after occurrence 2, a third node (test4) wedged with an unkillable D-state sync -- and its stacks are ext4/jbd2 on dm-0, the node's OWN ROOT DISK, with MXFS nowhere in the path: 'jbd2/dm-0-8 __wait_on_buffer <- jbd2_journal_commit_transaction', 'kworker/u10:2+flush-252:0 do_get_write_access <- ext4_mb_new_blocks', even 'dmesg' blocked in ext4_dirty_inode. Host measurement at that moment: clyde's nvme0n1 (which hosts BOTH the VM root images and the SCST fileio backing store for the shared LUN) at 88% full with block-layer r_await=96-157ms and w_await=17-25ms, against the documented healthy figures on D-DIR-REUSE-COHERENCY-32-FLAKY (write await p50 1.19ms healthy / 4.29ms degraded, p90 15ms healthy / 49ms degraded). That entry DISPROVED a different flake as host storage-path degradation on exactly this hardware. A backing store that delays or reorders writes to the shared LUN could produce an inconsistent free-space picture on more than one node at once, which is what both occurrences look like. THIS DOES NOT DISPOSE OF THE DEFECT and must not be used to: no SCSI/dm error was observed on either corrupting node, and 'the host was busy' is not evidence about what the filesystem did. It is a hypothesis with a cheap discriminator -- see next step 0b.

0. THE DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT, before any other work: prove whether every node mounted the SAME mkfs generation. The on-disk super already carries an identity (fs_gen = folded volume_id of the mkfs generation; the disklock layer uses it to reject pre-mkfs ghosts, dlm/disklock.c hb_gen_foreign), but the mount path does not log it, so 'this node is running the previous filesystem' is currently undetectable from a board harvest. Log volume_id/fs_gen on the mount line, then assert across the fleet that all N nodes report the same value after every prep. That single check separates 'stale view of a re-mkfs'd LUN' (a harness/operator hazard the FS should also refuse) from a genuine free-space coherency defect, and it is cheap.
0b. DISCRIMINATE HOST-STORAGE FROM FILESYSTEM. On any future occurrence, harvest from the corrupting node, in the same breath as the corruption lines: SCSI/dm/multipath errors ('I/O error', 'reservation conflict', 'path down', 'blk_update_request'), and from the HOST: nvme block-layer await and a 4K O_DSYNC probe. A corruption with a clean transport on a healthy host implicates the filesystem; one that coincides with degraded host await does not settle anything either way but must be recorded. Add that harvest to the board's node-fault path so it is captured automatically rather than reconstructed afterwards.

defects.summary: A terminal refusal quarantine PERMANENTLY occupies one disklock heartbeat slot (its RECOVERY_GUARD record is the durable verdict, so it must stay). The number of usable slots is the volume's log-slice count. On a cluster formatted with exactly as many slices as nodes -- which is the default (tests/setup/prep_fs.sh MXFS_LOG_SLICES=32) and what the 32-node rig runs -- there is then NO free slot, and the recovered node CANNOT MOUNT AT ALL: 'disklock: no free heartbeat slot in 0..31 -- the volume has 32 log slices ... Cluster is full; reformat with more slices (mkfs_mxfs -n) to admit more nodes' -> claim_slot -28 -> 'MXFS DLM init failed - aborting mount'. One refused slice therefore costs the cluster a node PERMANENTLY, and the operator is told to REFORMAT when the actual state is a quarantine awaiting repair. ESCALATED WITHIN THE SESSION, TWICE: (1) 32 IS A HARD CAP, not a default -- 'mkfs.mxfs: -n must be 1-32 (XFS caps the internal log at 2GiB-10MiB, so at most 32 ~64MB per-node slices fit; the slice count is the cluster's hard node limit for this filesystem)'. So at the maximum supported cluster size there is NO formatting option that leaves headroom, and the mount error's own advice ('reformat with more slices') is impossible to follow. (2) There is NO IMPLEMENTED REPAIR PATH. The quarantine message says 'needs operator repair + remount', but no tool and no knob clears a quarantined RECOVERY_GUARD record: chk_mxfs (-a/-y/-U) does not touch it, caw_slotdump is read-only, and the only in-kernel clear-to-EMPTY path is the clean-release CAS, which refuses any record that is not the caller's own live record. The only way to free the slot is mkfs_mxfs -f -- a reformat, i.e. total data loss, which also destroys the verdict the quarantine exists to preserve. Net effect: one refused slice permanently reduces a 32-node cluster to 31 nodes with no recovery short of rebuilding the filesystem.

defects.mechanism: PROVEN, code + platter. dlm/disklock.c claim path: when no free slot is found and ctx->slot_limit < MXFS_DISKLOCK_HB_SLOTS it returns -ENOSPC with the 'reformat with more slices' message; slot_limit is the volume's xfs_log_node_count (struct mxfs_ondisk_super, byte offset 96) because a slot beyond the slice count would have no journal. The quarantined slot is not free: its sector is a MXFS_DISKLOCK_FLAG_RECOVERY_GUARD (=3) record and recov_desc_present() requires exactly that flag, so the record IS the durable verdict every closure gate reads. Keeping it is correct -- the defect is the interaction: usable slots = slice count, and nothing reserves headroom for the verdict records a refusal will create. Measured on the rig: platter super says max_nodes=64 but log_slices=32, so slots 0..31 only; with 32 nodes mounted the table is 32/32 occupied; after a refusal the table is 31 live + 1 GUARD, still 32/32, and the rejoining node aborts its mount.
defects.containment: Fail-closed and loud: the mount aborts with an explicit ENOSPC message rather than admitting a node without a journal slice. Nothing is corrupted. The cost is availability -- the cluster runs one node short until an operator repairs the quarantine -- plus the misleading 'reformat' guidance.

defects.summary: When MXFS cannot prove it retired its own PR registration at unmount, it LOGS AND CARRIES ON. The 0.14.11 fix makes the failure detectable (P301-PR-AUTHORITY-NOT-RETIRED / P301-DEPARTURE-INCOMPLETE) but nothing acts on it: the node finishes unmounting while its initiator may still be registered on the shared LUN, and no survivor is told. The RULE: CONSULT ANOTHER MODEL WHEN STUCK ruling was explicit that this is not sufficient -- 'verify and log is not enough. The load-bearing invariant is that membership departure and PR authority retirement are coupled by either successful verification or an authorized fail-closed recovery action.' A stale registration on a LIVE initiator nexus can authorize non-filesystem I/O to the shared device even though MXFS is unmounted.
defects.evidence: Code state on 0.14.11 (the fail-closed branch simply does not exist), plus the sess377 rig observation that a pre-fix leftover key persisted across a complete 32-node clean unmount with no cluster-side reaction of any kind. The RULE: CONSULT ANOTHER MODEL WHEN STUCK ruling text is in docs/rulings/3-pr-unregister-leak-fix-shape.md.
defects.mechanism: THREE GAPS, all present in 0.14.11. (a) NO FAIL-CLOSED ACTION. pal/linux/xfs_super.c's late unregister raises xfs_alert P301-DEPARTURE-INCOMPLETE and returns; put_super continues and the mount goes away. Nothing isolates the initiator sessions that could still use the registration, nothing self-fences, and no durable record hands the problem to an authorized survivor. (b) NO SERIALIZATION AGAINST RE-REGISTRATION. Nothing prevents a path addition, multipath recovery, or a userspace multipathd key replay from re-registering the departing key AFTER the verification succeeded. The verification is a point-in-time observation with no interlock. (c) NO AUTHORIZED REAPER FOR ORPHANS. A registration left by a pre-fix incarnation, or by a node whose path was unavailable during its unmount, stays forever: REGISTER-based deregistration can only act as the corresponding I_T nexus, so removing an inaccessible nexus's surviving registration requires an authorized PREEMPT from another nexus, and MXFS has no such path. Observed directly: key 0xa5c5a98f survived a full 32-node clean unmount and was only cleared when its owner happened to remount and depart again.
defects.containment: Detection only: P301-PR-AUTHORITY-NOT-RETIRED and P301-DEPARTURE-INCOMPLETE in the departing node's log, and 'chk_mxfs --pr-keys <dev>' from any node, which with the cluster fully unmounted must show an EMPTY table.

defects.summary: A node takes a metadata READ error on a healthy, freshly-mkfs'd cluster and shuts the filesystem down, which cascades: every other node's coherency checks against its data then fail. test22 hit 'Metadata I/O Error (0x1) detected at xfs_trans_read_buf_map+0x178 (xfs/xfs_trans_buf.c:313)' inside an inode create, declared voluntary death, and turned a green board red.
evidence: TIMELINE on a common wall clock derived from matched uptime<->realns pairs (dmesg -T and btime+uptime were ~5 s apart between these two nodes and INVERTED this ordering on the first attempt, so they are not usable here): 04:20:29.399Z test22 'XFS (dm-1): Metadata I/O Error (0x1) detected at xfs_trans_read_buf_map+0x178/0x320 [mxfs] (/src/mxfs/xfs/xfs_trans_buf.c:313). Shutting down filesystem.' -> P-WITHDRAW-QUEUE -> P163-WITHDRAW-STAMP slot=11 node=3671298124. 04:20:29.871Z test5 P236-FENCE-INTENT slot=11 victim=3671298124, i.e. 472 ms LATER. The fence is a CONSEQUENCE of the withdrawal, not its cause - the withdraw stamp is what tells peers to fence, so the fence cannot precede its own trigger.

The error surfaced inside an inode create: 'P-CREATE-ERR2 dir_create_child err=-5 t_dfops_empty=1 dp_ino=41943175 new_ino=46137488' then 'P-CR3-CANCEL error=-5 dp_ino=41943175 dialloc_ino=46137488 new_ino=46137488 trans_dirty=1 comm=bash', followed by three P-AGMETA-RECLAIM drops (xfs_agi, xfs_finobt, xfs_inobt).

Post-shutdown, reads of the same inodes report 'P9-ICD-MIDLOOP ino=46137487 imap_rc=-5 bp=0 plainrd_rc=0 magic=0x494e ... shutdown=1' - the PLAIN read of that location succeeds and carries a valid XFS_DINODE_MAGIC while the imap path returns -EIO. Those lines are AFTER the shutdown so the EIO there is expected; the valid magic is recorded only because it argues the on-platter content was intact.

BOARD IMPACT: cache_coherency FAILED nodes_pass=0/32 faildist[8x27,9x4,13x1] - 27 nodes failed 8 checks each, which are the cross-node checks against the departed node's data, so the coherency failure is the cascade rather than an independent fault. strong_consistency, posix_multi, mmap_coherency and zero_silent_loss then all reported 'pre-assert: mxfs not mounted/readable on test22'. A re-prep and re-run of the identical chunk on the identical build passed 8/8, so the trigger is intermittent - which under RULE: ZERO ACCEPTED KNOWN DEFECTS is a reason to instrument, never to dismiss.

NOT caused by the sess378 fence change: that change is confined to mxfs_pal_scsi_pr_preempt() with abort=true, which runs only in the fence path, and test22 logged no fence activity before its shutdown. A UNIT ATTENTION was seen on test22 (P-FUA-READ-RETRY lba=194241 ret=0x2 resid=8192 key=0x6 try=1) but only AFTER the shutdown, consistent with test5's subsequent preemption.

A SECOND, DIFFERENT shutdown the same session, recorded as a lead rather than a claim: test5 shut down at 04:00:50Z with 'Metadata I/O Error (0x1) detected at mxfs_dlm_fence_notify+0x53/0x80' - a SELF-FENCE on PR-key-lost - during a 32-node mass unmount, while the fleet was still running 0.14.11. Whether the two share a root is unknown.

(C) an FSWIDE quarantine imported by the registration scan does NOT refuse the mount: the barrier's two unconditional FSWIDE gates both run ~0.5s BEFORE the scan, so the mount ADMITS a zombie whose every operation fails EIO -- precisely what xfs_mxfs_dlm.c:48457 says must never happen. Arm C needs no forgery in principle: any legitimate FSWIDE verdict published between the barrier's sweep and registration -- the late-mount case the scan was BUILT for -- admits the same zombie.

defects.mechanism: Consumers of mxfs_recov_outcome and their scrutiny, measured 0.19.5: (1) disklock monitor (disklock.c ~1430) -- gated on hb_still_dead_stamp, fires the cb only if oc->outcome == TERMINAL_REFUSED; no check of reason/victim_slot/ag_mask, and the outcome-kind prefilter is itself a bypass (an outcome=99 record is silently skipped every pass, so a quarantined slot never quarantines any live peer -- the D-513 park/timeout shape returns). (2) registration scan (v5_mount.c:6916) -- loops 0..63, calls read_outcome, and on rc==0 calls v5_closure_note_terminal(ctx,slot,&oc) + quar_cb(data,slot,&oc) with NO validation at all. (3) shared classifier (xfs_mxfs_dlm.c:47038 -> mxfs_freplay_import_verdict:46941) -- the ONLY validating path; rejects wrong outcome kind, unknown reason, bad domain, empty AG mask, oc->victim_slot != slot. The mount admission barrier builds its cut from get_recovery_pending_slots(), which SKIPS hb_gen_foreign records and stage >= GRANTS_RELEASED records; everything in the cut goes through the validating classifier, so the barrier is correct. The scan is what bypasses it, and it runs AFTER the barrier.

defects.mechanism: SESS482 CANDIDATE ARM (e), FROM SOURCE, NOT FROM A REPRODUCTION — THE UNMOUNT AG-RELEASE PATH DOES NOT RUN THE DRAIN PIPELINE, AND THIS RECORD'S SYMPTOM IS "AFTER A CLEAN FLEET UNMOUNT". Arms (a)-(d) are all about REPLAY; none of them looks at what unmount itself does, and that is where the divergence is observed. The facts, each verified by reading the code rather than inferred: (1) mxfs_dlm_ag_force_release_all (xfs/xfs_mxfs_dlm.c ~49924) is the unmount release. Between the top of its per-AG loop and its mxfs_v5_dlm_ag_unlock at ~49970 it runs exactly ONE drain -- mxfs_dlm_ag_drain_alloc_buflist at ~49940 -- and then two cancel_work_syncs and a state-flag block. (2) The COOPERATIVE release path (~49457 to its unlock at ~49710) runs NINE steps first: drain_alloc_buflist, drain_inode_buffers, blkdev_flush_epoch, drain_meta_buffers, blkdev_flush_epoch, xfs_log_force(XFS_LOG_SYNC), a SECOND drain_meta_buffers (the sess43 fix), a bounded meta_pending wait for in-flight bios, and a final flush. The unmount path omits eight of the nine. (3) mxfs_v5_dlm_ag_unlock (dlm/v5_mount.c ~15071) is a PURE release primitive -- a TCP unlock or a CAW slot CAS with a release gate -- so nothing internal covers the omission. (4) ORDERING: the call is made from pal/linux/xfs_super.c:2066 inside xfs_fs_put_super, and xfs_unmountfs -- which is where the synchronous log quiesce, AIL push and buftarg drain happen -- is at line 2175 of the SAME function. Nothing between the top of put_super and 2066 pushes the AIL or forces the log. So the AG grants are published as free BEFORE this node's metadata is pushed to its final on-platter home. (5) The cooperative path's own sess43 comment states the consequence of skipping exactly the step this path skips: the just-dirtied AG-meta buffers -- "AGI (agi_unlinked / freecount), AGF (freeblks), inobt/finobt" -- are "left in-core-ahead-of-disk at unlock ... so the peer's FUA read at acquire MISSES them -> stale-behind AGI unlinked-list head ... -> xfs_iunlink_remove_inode corruption + shutdown". THAT IS THIS RECORD'S SYMPTOM, ITEM FOR ITEM: an AGI freecount disagreeing with the inobt/finobt on the platter, plus an orphan still chained in an AGI unlinked bucket with mode 0 gen 0. (6) A second, independent hazard on the same path, and possibly the sharper one: after the grant is released at 2066, xfs_unmountfs at 2175 pushes THIS node's AIL. If a peer acquired the AG in that window and modified the AG-meta, our later writeback durably REVERTS the peer's change -- the same durable-clobber shape b_mxfs_relepoch exists to prevent for directory blocks. Note the asymmetry that makes it worse: the cooperative release records pag_mxfs_rel_epoch from pag_mxfs_grant_epoch before zeroing it (~39140), whereas the unmount path zeroes pag_mxfs_grant_epoch (~49956) WITHOUT setting pag_mxfs_rel_epoch, so the retiring-token guards that read it (xfs/xfs_inode.c ~8531, ~10051, gated on rel_epoch != 0) are inert on this path. WHY THIS WAS NOT CAUGHT BY THE ORACLE THAT ALREADY RUNS THERE, which matters for reading every clean sweep in this record: mxfs_agifc_release_audit(pag, "unmount") IS called at ~49968, immediately before the unlock, and is default-on (agifc_release_audit=1). It reads the AGI, inobt and finobt straight off the PLATTER and prints P-AGIFC-RELEASE-MISMATCH when the image about to be published disagrees with the btrees on the medium -- exactly this record's divergence, measured at exactly the right instant. But it has TWO systematic blind spots, both read from its source at ~42868: it returns early when xfs_is_shutdown(mp), so a shut-down or force-withdrawn node is never audited; and it bails with "multi-level: leaf walk not implemented" unless agi_level == 1 AND agi_free_level == 1, so any AG whose inobt or finobt has grown past a single level is silently skipped. The successor master imports the bit as a blocker (owner UNKNOWN during formation, since the heartbeat table has not resolved the slot yet) and nothing ever retires it on a live cluster: every later EX on that resource is refused by the ledger (P-TAUTH-DOUBLE-GRANT 'table decided a conflicting grant'). On the rig the resource was the ROOT INODE (ino=128): mount's EX on it timed out after 125-208 s on test17/19/20/32 -> 'DLM inode lock unrecoverable' -> shutdown -> 'Failed to read root inode 0x80, error 5' -> mount EIO ('can't read superblock'); other nodes spun 115x REMASTER (status=12) in one second and abandoned ('lock request failed after 10 retries'), and 13 unmounts hung. A clustered FS on which the join ramp itself makes the root inode permanently unlockable cannot mount.
defects.mechanism: dlm/dlm.c dlm_txn_finalize (0.34.0): remaster = (commit_rc == -ESTALE) || (ctx->ledger_gen != txn->gen) || page_state != MINE; on remaster after a SUCCESSFUL commit the entry is freed (P-TAUTH-GHOST) and the requester gets MXFS_ERR_REMASTER. The record (holders bit for the requester's slot) is durable; the requester never learns it holds anything and never releases; dlm_import_holder at the successor names the bit's owner via slot_node_cb, which during formation returns 0 -> MXFS_DLM_NODE_UNKNOWN, 'never BASTed'. RULE: CONSULT ANOTHER MODEL WHEN STUCK ruling docs/rulings/ghost-grant-delivery-and-unresolved-pr-bits.md: a successful commit is the proof of authority (page write + exact readback) and MUST be delivered whatever the view did afterwards (the successor imports the record naming the same holder); compensating release on send failure is UNSAFE; an unresolved shared bit stays an EX blocker until recovery names it (re-resolving on every import is fine); long-term: durable {node,inc} per shared holder.

defects.summary: On the TCP transport with the durable authority ledger (0.35.0), two SHARED holders of one resource releasing concurrently while an EX waiter is queued make the master decide the EX over a holder whose bit is still durable: promote_waiters treated EVERY PENDING_RELEASE holder as already gone, not only the one being retired in the current transition. The bundled ledger transition [release, grant EX] is refused by the ledger (P-TAUTH-DOUBLE-GRANT 'req EX vs record holders=<sibling bit>'), and the refusal strands the release: the entry is kept PENDING_RELEASE 'for the releaser to retry', the releaser's retry is ACKed OK as a duplicate, and nothing ever retires the record. The stranded entry blocks every later EX on the resource as a holder and keeps the page 'in flight' forever, so the ordered page handoff can never freeze-drain it (P-TAUTH-FREEZE-DRAIN-TIMEOUT x94 on page 1786 = the ROOT INODE's page on test2), every requester of that page gets REMASTER (P74-GRANT status=12 x4381 fleet-wide), 'lock request failed after 10 retries' x54, 26 mounts abort. A refused grant was also terminal for the requester (MXFS_ERR_LEDGER -> -EIO) although the cause was transient.
defects.mechanism: dlm/dlm.c: (1) promote_waiters used lk_is_live_holder(), which excludes PENDING_RELEASE — documented as 'the one being retired in this very transition' but applied to ALL of them; releases are processed concurrently on the master (local unlock threads vs the receive thread), so a sibling holder in PENDING_RELEASE (its own commit in flight) was invisible and the EX was decided over its durable bit. (2) dlm_txn_commit bundles release + successor grants in one ledger commit; tauth_ledger.c apply_op refuses the grant with -EBUSY (DOUBLE-GRANT, fail-closed by the sess424 ruling) which fails the whole bundle. (3) dlm_txn_finalize on a refused bundle kept the release entry PENDING_RELEASE ('the releaser retries') and ACKed MXFS_ERR_LEDGER; the releaser's resend hit process_remote_release's PENDING_RELEASE branch, which ACKed MXFS_OK as a 'duplicate' — the releaser stopped, the master never re-drove it. (4) A denied grant (MXFS_ERR_LEDGER) mapped to -EIO at the requester. Reproduced deterministically in usermode (tests/tauth/concurrent_release_test, one-shot ledger commit-delay knob): first lap on the unfixed engine = P-TAUTH-DOUBLE-GRANT 'EX vs holders=0x2', B's EX rc=-5 after 70 ms, platter record holders=0x4 stuck, 1 in-flight entry on the page forever, A's release ACKed OK. RULE: CONSULT ANOTHER MODEL WHEN STUCK ruling (sess425 consult, banked in docs/rulings/concurrent-release-fix-shape.md): (1)+(2) sound with 'every retirement triggers a promotion re-scan'; the master must re-commit the release alone and never depend on the releaser; a retry finding PENDING_RELEASE must not be ACKed OK; invariant: every PENDING_* entry has exactly one live master-owned driver.

defects.summary: The TCP authority ledger's rule that ONLY the bootstrap node (lowest live heartbeat slot) may claim an UNOWNED page assumes bootstrap tenure is exclusive. It is not: (1) a node ranks its own slot first regardless of its own health, so a lowest-slot node whose heartbeat stalled (falsely dead, still running) keeps believing it is bootstrap; (2) every other node drops that slot from 'live' at DEATH DETECTION, before the SCSI-PR fence has landed, so the next-lowest node becomes bootstrap at once. In that window both nodes can pass activate(bootstrap)'s read-then-write on the same UNOWNED page — write + readback is not a compare-and-write: A writes seq1/ACTIVE(A), A reads back its own image, B writes seq1/ACTIVE(B), B reads back its own image; both now cache the page as MINE and both may decide grants on every resource of that page until A is fenced. Two authorities for one page = the double-grant/corruption class the ledger exists to prevent. The 0.35.4 D-0345 route (non-bootstrap masters now actively ASK the bootstrap node to claim) widens the exposure from 'pages the bootstrap decides itself' to 'every never-decided page requested during the window'.

Root (dlm/tauth_store.c mxfs_tauth_page_write, pre-0.36.0): the write re-read only the copies' seqs (next=max+1, target=spare copy) and verified only its own copy's readback; nothing tied the commit to the image the caller patched. The bootstrap election cannot be made exclusive at the requester (a falsely-dead node cannot know), so the ledger write itself must arbitrate. || DESIGN-PROVEN interleaving (RULE: TROUBLESHOOTING IS A LOOP, NOT A GUESS step 1/2 pending): A = slot 1 (HB thread stalled > death timeout, process alive), B = slot 2. B: node_track[1].live=false -> lowest_live_slot()==2 -> bootstrap_cb true. A: lowest_live_slot()==1 (own slot short-circuit). Page P UNOWNED. A: activate(P,bootstrap): read UNOWNED, write ACTIVE(A) seq1, readback == own -> MINE. B: activate(P,bootstrap): read UNOWNED (before A's write lands) , write ACTIVE(B) seq1, readback == own -> MINE. Platter ends ACTIVE(B); A's cache says ACTIVE(A). A's later txn commits are page writes that overwrite B's (same-seq race is only -EIO if the readback happens to see the other image). Fence of A lands seconds later. Also needs proof of whether the death->fence ordering (fence_before_recovery) covers the bootstrap election: if the election waited for fence completion (mxfs_disklock node_track fenced flag) the window closes for (2) but not for (1) (A never learns it is dead until its own writes fail).

defects.summary: The TCP authority ledger has ONE record per resource-hash slot (MXFS_TAUTH_SLOTS=65536, page=slot/31). Two live INODE resources whose hashes collide cannot both be recorded: the second grant is refused -EEXIST at the ledger (tauth_ledger.c ~644 P-TAUTH-COLLISION, fail closed), the master denies MXFS_ERR_LEDGER, and the requester turns that into -EIO to the file operation (dlm.c ~3452 'if (ret > 0) return -EIO'). With 8000 live inodes in the s429 workload the birthday bound makes collisions certain (44 seen); a production filesystem with millions of live inodes would refuse a large fraction of inode locks. The refusal is correct fail-closed behaviour for the record; the DESIGN cannot serve more distinct live resources than slots, and the caller sees a hard EIO rather than a wait.
defects.mechanism: By construction (sess422 step 3 design, docs/tcp-authority-ledger.md): mxfs_tauth_ledger_slot(res) = resource_hash_raw % 65536; apply_op GRANT on a slot whose ACTIVE record names a different resource returns -EEXIST (l->collisions++). dlm_promote_txn: rc -EEXIST -> it->rc=-EEXIST -> deliver sends MXFS_MSG_LOCK_DENY status MXFS_ERR_LEDGER; requester dlm_lock_impl: any deny status other than REMASTER/LEDGER_BUSY -> return -EIO (no retry: the collision persists as long as the other holder lives). The CAW transport has the same 65536-slot table (MXFS_CAW_MAX_SLOTS) but its slot semantics differ (per-slot waiter bits; D-SAMENODE-WAITER-CANCEL-COLLISION covers its own collision class). NOT yet measured: which syscall received the EIO in s429 (the workload's per-file errors were not captured; only rc=124 timeouts) — add errno capture to tcp_token_plumbing_verify.

defects.summary: After a whole-cluster crash (all 32 nodes destroyed with fsynced payload), no node can mount again without operator intervention: each rebooted host's I_T nexus still carries its previous incarnation's SCSI PR key (PTPL), the plain REGISTER returns RESERVATION CONFLICT, and the sess432 D-0355 guard refuses the mount (P305-PR-PREDECESSOR-KEY-PRESENT -> 'SCSI PR register failed (-17) refusing to join unfenced'). With zero survivors nobody can PREEMPT AND ABORT anyone; the only remedy is a manual single_node_exclusive=1 mount on one chosen node. A datacenter power loss therefore leaves the filesystem unmountable until a human acts, and the remedy asserts an exclusion-by-topology that becomes false as soon as the other nodes boot.

defects.mechanism: dlm/scsipr.c mxfs_scsipr_register: -EEXIST on the plain REGISTER (predecessor key on this nexus) is refused unless replace_predecessor (single_node_exclusive). PR key = 32-bit per-mount node_id; nothing distinguishes 'predecessor from a previous BOOT of this host (dead by construction)' from 'predecessor from this same boot (may still issue I/O)'. The sess432 ruling covered only the lone-node dirty remount; the all-nodes-dead case has no automatic path. Measured: test1 rebooted at +27 s, insmod OK, armed=11, mount refused at 02:49:05Z (journalctl: P304-PREOBSERVE held=1 type=WE-AR, P305-PR-NEXUS-ALREADY-REGISTERED key 0xcc438ac9, P305-PR-PREDECESSOR-KEY-PRESENT, 'MXFS DLM init failed — aborting mount', 'reservation conflict error, dev dm-1, sector 0 op WRITE').

defects.summary: The crash-durable durability domain (fua_disable=0, i.e. target power loss / volatile write-cache loss IN scope) is not a qualified clustered-RW configuration: a tenure can become peer-claimable (release CAS) before its home writes and its newly minted epoch/lineage/token state are durable, so a target cache loss can persist the release while dropping the writes it certified (sess197 F2, HARD). 0.54.0 therefore REFUSES clustered RW mounts with fua_disable=0 (mxfs_durability_domain_admit, P-DOMAIN-REFUSED) and admits only the coherence-only domain (fua_disable=1 target_cache_protected=1). This record is the open requirement to qualify and re-admit fua_disable=0.

Required per the sess197 ruling step 7 + sess447 ruling: (1) every obligation of the outgoing tenure completed, (2) data+metadata durably ordered before any peer-claimable CAS (mxfs_blkdev_flush_durable after the last home completion, all classes incl. AG; skip only when the tenure provably created zero obligations; flush tickets coalescable), (3) newly minted epoch/lineage/token state durable before a peer can observe or claim it, (4) flush/FUA/writeback errors prevent publication and lead to bounded defer/fence/fail-closed — never 'release anyway', (5) all release/publication paths obey the ordering incl. recovery/cancel/orphan/error exits, (6) a crash exposes only the old complete or the new complete durable epoch. Plus B2-B4 of D-INODE-CLUSTER-PUBLISH-WITHOUT-AUTHORITY and the step-8 stable-media oracle (per tagged image: payload hash/class/resource/epoch/commit/submit/stable points; accepted<->lineage-valid, rejected-stale<->home-newer, sole-surviving-copy never rejected, new-tenure image never stable before its epoch mint) with target-cache-loss tests (discard acked-unflushed writes, reboot from the stable image) — node kills do NOT cover it.

defects.summary: The fencing-intent path lays a RECOVERY_GUARD on whatever incarnation the victim's sector carries, not the one the survivors declared dead. mxfs_disklock_recovery_fence_intent (dlm/disklock.c) checks flags, node_id and fs_gen but never compares cur->epoch with the victim_epoch it was asked to fence; it copies cur->epoch into desc.victim_epoch and the caller then issues the PREEMPT AND ABORT of the key frozen for the DECLARED incarnation. When the sector carries a LATER ACTIVE incarnation of the same node this is a fencing intent + P&A against a live member (the sess86 hazard that recovery_begin() closed and that this function, its replacement as the only descriptor creator, did not inherit); in every case the descriptor names an incarnation nobody observed stop, the pending recovery for the declared incarnation stays behind it forever (chain 61: slot 25 sat at GUARD/E2 for the full 180 s heal budget, P163-RECOVERY-COMPLETE=0), and every later prover exits -ESTALE silently at the descriptor-tuple check.
