defects.summary: On the vSphere shared attachment (multi-writer VMDK, fence=vcenter, vstest1/vstest2), the two-node work load of tests/vsphere_shared_fence.sh (each node writes 100 files into its own directory and 100 into one shared directory, 256 KiB each, every file fsynced) spends 13.5-13.6 s writing, against 1.96-2.90 s for the same two workers on native XFS on the same VMDK: 4.7-6.9x native, past the 2x ceiling. All of the difference is file creation: open(O_CREAT|O_TRUNC) takes p50 18-22 ms in a node's own directory and 71-78 ms in the shared one (p99 0.4 s / 1.3 s), against 0.05 ms on native XFS; write+fsync+close is p50 4.5-5.4 ms, no slower than native (6.5-11.5 ms).
defects.evidence: srcversion FDAFC867264E74A3660A07B (0.90.128, node-local EL9 build), AlmaLinux 9.8 guests on esxhost1/esxhost2, clyde concurrently running the DRBD release verification on test1/test2 for both arms. MeshXFS: tests/evidence/vsphere/shared-20261013T160904Z (work: write wall 14 s; vstest1 LAT own create p50_ms=21.77 p99_ms=415.23, shared create p50_ms=70.89 p99_ms=1059.18 sum_ms=9089; vstest2 own create p50 18.13, shared create p50 77.76 sum_ms=9582; fsync p50 4.46-5.38; DONE wall_s=13.62/13.54). Native XFS, same disk, both workers on vstest1 (tests/vsphere_shared_fence.sh baseline): shared-20261013T161201Z wall 3.31 s (workers 2.89/2.90 s, create p50 0.05 ms, fsync p50 11.2-11.5 ms) and shared-20261013T161207Z wall 2.44 s (workers 1.97/1.96 s). Guest RTT vstest1->vstest2 avg 2.56 ms max 38.1 ms (ping -c 20), against 0.149 ms test1->test2 on the KVM rig. ===== Same load on the cross-host physical-mode RDM mounted fence=vcenter (srcversion FDAFC867264E74A3660A07B, tests/evidence/vsphere/rdm-vcenter-1/laps.txt): first work 13.59/14.12 s per worker (new files), the same pattern of create cost as the VMDK. The second work on the same filesystem, which opens the SAME 400 names again with O_TRUNC (no inode is allocated, the files exist), took 3.41/3.41 s per worker, within 2x of native: open(O_TRUNC) of an existing file p50 8.6-9.7 ms, p99 17-42 ms, write+fsync+close p50 4.9-5.2 ms (rdm-vcenter-1/work/work_vstest*.txt, the second run's capture). So the excess is in allocating and linking a new inode (~20 ms own directory, ~75 ms shared), not in the data path and not in the directory lookup of an existing name.
defects.next: Same per-create cost class as D-TCP-PRIVATE-DIR-CREATE-RATE-34-PER-SECOND (~29 ms per create, 2/tcp KVM rig) and D-TCP-LEDGER-SMALLFILE-WORKLOAD-PACE-RULE0-0349 (a durable ledger page commit per create). On this attachment every on-disk swap is the emulated two-party lock (sector writes and reads with flushes on the VMDK) instead of one COMPARE AND WRITE, and the lock traffic crosses a 2.6 ms network. Measure one node's create in phases before any change: swaps per create, ledger page commits per create (P-TAUTH-PAGE-MINE), DLM round trips per create, and the wall of each, on both vSphere and the KVM 2/tcp rig, to split the per-create cost into commit count x commit cost x network.
defects.impact_why: pace only: the run that measured it wrote every file on both nodes, each node read back every file the other wrote with its content (VERIFY good=200 missing=0 mismatch=0 both ways) and listed the shared directory complete (200), with no shutdown, error or hung task

defects.summary: fence=quorum on the shared attachment lets a node frozen by its hypervisor HOST keep writing after the survivor took it over. The survivor's kind-30 certificate (the loser ended its boot) is false: the loser never resets. While the nested ESXi host is paused, commands the guest handed to ESXi stay queued, and on unpause ESXi issues them. The guest's clock did not advance across the pause, so its 3 s quorum lease still read valid, and it issued new writes. Its corosync merged back into the membership without ever reporting it inquorate. It stopped only when its heartbeat found its slot taken over (P290-AUTH-WITHDRAW reason=SLOT_TAKEOVER), 0.85 s of guest time after resume.
defects.evidence: tests/vsphere_shared_fence.sh freeze host, build CC54CCA6EE7210901855D5B, vstest1/vstest2 on the physical RDM (eui.6661313331363962), qnetd on serv. vstest2 writes O_DIRECT stamped 4 KiB blocks from 16 threads; vmrun pause esxhost2; vstest1 took over at +75 s (P238-SHARED-FENCE-ENDED kind=30 obs=quorum-loser-deadline-passed, foreign replay, P163-RECOVERY-COMPLETE); snapshot A; unpause; snapshot B differs in 4 blocks: 785, 878 and 1623 stamped 32.92-32.94 s (queued in ESXi at the pause), and 1639 (thread 7, seq 614) stamped 33.77 s, a new write 0.83 s of guest time after seq 613. Afterwards vstest2 was still on boot 5095e60e (the certified-ended one), quorate=1, member=1, mounted, FS shut down at [33.92]. The guest-suspend control (govc vm.power -suspend, quorum-10-freeze-guest): no late write; vSphere's suspend drains I/O.
defects.next: No in-guest mechanism can stop this. Queued commands are below the guest, and a resumed guest cannot see its freeze before it writes. Fix by putting a storage barrier under the vote: (1) refuse fence=quorum on a device with no SCSI persistent reservations (a multi-writer VMDK answers PR with invalid opcode), the same way fence=scsipr is refused there; (2) on a physical RDM (PR forwarded per guest, one VM per host), register a key at arm and hold a WEAR reservation, and have the survivor PREEMPT AND ABORT the victim's key before replay, so that late commands get RESERVATION CONFLICT. Verify with freeze host repeated, zero late writes, and the kill/split/restart laps.
defects.impact_why: Measured: 4 blocks of the victim's file changed on disk after the survivor had certified its boot ended and replayed its slice (tests/evidence/vsphere/quorum-11-freeze-host/late_writes.txt).

defects.summary: Loading mxfs.ko keeps one CPU from running anything else for ~0.93 s (2-vCPU rig guest), with or without debug info, so a load on a DRBD node with the link up misses DRBD's 0.5 s PingAck and the peer is fenced.
defects.evidence: tests/module_load_stall.sh test1 3 (2026-10-15, 4FD56D0D02CBB2D2A7CB8B6, 6.8.0-101, 2 vCPU): as built 89 MB insmod 1243/1276/1338 ms, longest per-CPU gap 930/968/945 ms; debug-stripped 11.7 MB insmod 1205/1138/1138 ms, gap 933/921/921 ms. In drbd_release_verify 0.90.129 (02:45Z and 02:57Z) a load with the link up was followed within ~1 s by 'meta connection shut down by peer' and a STONITH. ===== 2026-10-23: the 02:57Z occurrence named above is the DRBD board run 2/net/mesh/drbd prep_cluster INCOMPLETE 'prep failed' 2026-10-15T02:57:41Z (tests/evidence/drbd_rig/criteria.runs.jsonl:2941). Its own evidence, tests/evidence/drbd_rig/20261015T025653Z-suite/suite.log: :36 '--- prep: test1 UNLOAD_THREADS mxfs: P-THREAD-LIVE-SUM when=exit-end live=0 created=27 joined=27 join_gaveup=0', :37 '--- prep: test2 UNLOAD_THREADS mxfs: P-THREAD-LIVE-SUM when=exit-end live=0 created=19 joined=19 join_gaveup=0' (the prep unloaded the module on both nodes to load it again, with DRBD Connected: the same suite dir's check.test1/check.test2 read 'Primary/Primary UpToDate/UpToDate Connected' at 02:56:53Z), :40 'PREP FAIL: bad nodes: test2(unmounted)', :42 'ssh: connect to host test2 port 22: Connection timed out'. Host syslog (journalctl -t mxfs-rig-fence): 'Oct 14 21:57:17 clyde mxfs-rig-fence[3102928]: fenced test2 for test1 episode=b1622e34-286a-404a-9ebd-bf766674be50' (21:57:17 CDT = 02:57:17Z, inside the prep) and 'Oct 14 22:03:41 ... released test2 episode=b1622e34-...'. tests/evidence/drbd_rig/20261015T025741Z-mxfs/check.test1: 'Primary/Unknown UpToDate/Outdated WFConnection' (test1 lost the DRBD link and outdated its peer). The nodes' kernel logs of that run (drbdC_kmsg_test{1,2}.log in session efd8fea5's scratchpad) are no longer on disk, so the 'meta connection shut down by peer' line this record quotes for 02:57Z cannot be re-read; the run's surviving evidence shows the reload, the lost link and the fence in that order.
defects.next: Find where load_module spends the ~0.9 s without a reschedule (function_graph or perf on a guest during insmod: relocation, ftrace/alternatives patching, kallsyms, or module init) and break it up; then re-measure with tests/module_load_stall.sh (target: longest gap well under 0.5 s). ===== ===== 2026-10-17 (session 33) FIRST PROFILE: THE TRACED CHILDREN OF load_module ACCOUNT FOR ~170 MS OF ~1.28 S. New harness tests/module_load_profile.sh <node> [depth] [thresh_us] (function_graph, set_graph_function=load_module, tracing_thresh; debug-stripped module; tracer reset after). Run on test5 (6.8.0-101-generic, 2 vCPU, main-tree build 3AEA31FDF4AD31EFBBA6A90 stripped to 11822576 bytes, force_transport=1), depth 4, thresh 5000 us: insmod_ms=1304, load_module 1277496 us; calls >= 5 ms: blocking_notifier_call_chain_robust 113270 us (static_call_module_notify 56457, jump_label_module_notify 7332), post_relocation 22873 (module_finalize 21599, apply_returns 19714), text_poke_queue 10016 (text_poke_bp_batch 10009), do_init_module 12095 (init_xfs_fs 6895), layout_and_allocate 6619 (move_module 5639), mod_sysfs_setup 6160 (module_param_sysfs_setup 5758). The remaining ~1.1 s is spent inline in load_module or in many calls each under 5 ms (candidates: simplify_symbols/resolve_symbol per undefined symbol, apply_relocations per RELA section, ftrace_module_init, dynamic_debug_setup, the module's 790 parameters). NEXT: the same harness at depth 2 with thresh 0 (raise buffer_size_kb) and sum durations by function name to name the stretch; then decide what MXFS can change (fewer relocations or symbols, an init split, cond_resched in its own init) versus what is the kernel's load path. ===== ===== 2026-10-17 (session 36) THE STRETCH IS NAMED: ftrace's per-record kallsyms lookup, records x symbols. tests/module_load_profile.sh test5 2 0 (depth 2, no threshold; main-tree build 3AEA31FD stripped to 11822576 bytes, 6.8.0-101-generic, 2 vCPU; trace kept at tests/evidence/module_load_profile/20261017T1713Z_test5_d2t0.txt): insmod_ms=1507, load_module 1341.8 ms, of which kallsyms_lookup 5750 calls 989.1 ms, blocking_notifier_call_chain_robust 128.7 ms, text_poke_queue 5750 calls 70.9 ms, do_init_module 12.5 ms, find_symbol 272 calls 9.4 ms, mod_sysfs_setup 6.8 ms (durations are tracer upper bounds). 5750 is exactly mxfs.ko's fentry record count (__mcount_loc 0xb3b0 bytes / 8). Code (upstream /src/linux 7.1, kernel/trace/ftrace.c): ftrace_module_enable walks every record of the module and calls test_for_valid_rec -> kallsyms_lookup(rec->ip) (ftrace.c:4338-4352, :7982; x86 defines FTRACE_MCOUNT_MAX_OFFSET, arch/x86/include/asm/ftrace.h:18), and a module address lookup is find_kallsyms_symbol, a linear scan of the module's whole symtab (kernel/module/kallsyms.c:253-298). mxfs.ko has 29634 named symbols (nm: T 8581, t 5932, r 5816, d 5337, D 1543, b 1151, B 580, R 99; 4166 are static locals named x.NNN, chiefly _rs 876 ratelimit states, __func__ 711, descriptor 633), so the load costs ~5750 x ~29000 symbol visits. Upstream's loop now calls cond_resched() per record (ftrace.c:7979), so there the CPU yields between lookups; the hold the stall harness measures on 6.8 is consistent with that loop not yielding there (not yet confirmed against 6.8's own code, which is not on this host). FIX DIRECTIONS (none chosen): fewer fentry records (building the module's objects without the ftrace call sites would empty the loop but also end function tracing of MXFS, which tests/tcp_rsync_profile.sh uses, and needs a build-file change), or fewer module symbols (the scan is linear in them; half are data symbols). NEXT: measure the untraced load's split by a same-source module with the ftrace call sites removed (the build-file change needs the owner's go-ahead) or by a kprobe count of kallsyms_lookup at load; then decide.
defects.impact_why: Not on any user path measured: the packages never reload the module (no rmmod/modprobe in their install scripts) and mxfs-drbd-fence-self boot loads it before drbdadm up; only a reload with a DRBD link up (the rig harness did) fences the peer.

defects.summary: After a victim's death on net/mesh/mpath, the replayer's post-replay flush ('peer joined -- flushing XFS dirty state') waited on an AIL that a local task kept pinned: python3 in xfs_rename -> mxfs_trans_preacquire_inode_ags -> mxfs_ag_dlm_trylock held the ILOCKs of two inodes (shared dir) while retrying AG 1's lock, mastered by the dead victim, at 1 s per retry (P36-RETRY 58..1); xfsaild could not push those inodes (P129-CLSKIP why=ILOCK_NOWAIT_FAIL, P128-AILSTUCK), so the recovery completion ladder stalled until the rename's 60-retry budget ran out: all seven survivors' loads stopped ~131 s (bound 61 s).
defects.evidence: 0.90.53 (D283754F06E6D5F02655895), g8 lap s12fx8b run 20261005T213119Z-g8, tests/evidence/board_20261005T213119Z-g8_path_all_lost (row.log, stalls.txt) and the replayer's kept log board_20261005T213119Z-g8_path_peer_withdrawn/kmsg_test7_fromnode.gz: death declared and fenced 127.8, slice replay complete 24630.543, then nothing until P234-RECOV-STAGE 3->4 at 24690.496; last P36-RETRY 24689.44. Split out of D-NETMESH-MPATH-ALL-LOST-SURVIVORS-STALL-131S, whose 0.90.129 recurrence was a different mechanism (post-seal ledger mutation, fixed by the seal barrier).
defects.next: Confirm in the code that the single->multi / post-replay flush waits for the AIL to empty before the completion ladder runs, and that a task holding ILOCKs may wait on an AG lock whose master is declared dead. Fix candidates: the completion must not wait on a full AIL drain while a local task can hold inode locks across a wait on the dead master, or that wait gives up its inode locks / fails fast once its master is declared dead. ===== 2026-10-17 same incident and same code finding as D-NETMESH-SURVIVOR-ILOCK-HELD-ACROSS-DEAD-MASTER-AG-RETRY-PINS-AIL-131S (see its entry): the no-queue unanswered fix (P-ACQ-NOQUEUE-UNANSWERED) breaks the cycle on the waiter side; the flush still drains the whole AIL. Verify both records with the same log evidence. ===== 2026-10-17 KEPT-LOG SWEEP: 19 P-ACQ-NOQUEUE-UNANSWERED lines with master_live=0 in kept path_* rows (2/4/8/16 nodes, 2026-10-05..15), every such row PASS. Two are AG requests (type=3): board_20261015T003919Z-g4_path_peer_withdrawn test3 25157.433 and test5 25157.363 (identical copies in board_20261015T011608Z-g4_path_failover), ag=1 EX to dead master 3128590244 0.3 s after the replayer's claim was refused; recovery stage 3->4 5.5 s later; survivor stalls 9.1-15.8 s. None of those rows shows the full original cycle: no P271-AGWANT/AGWAIT-SEAM hand-off at that instant (so the request may be the allocator's probe, not an ILOCK holder's preacquire), no P128-AILSTUCK/P129-CLSKIP anywhere in those rows. The fix (dlm/dlm.c ~10706, no-queue + no answer in one attempt -> would-block) has no same-build switch, so an A/B needs one: a knob restoring the old retry, plus a deterministic trigger (a rename across two directories whose AG preacquire targets an AG mastered by a node that withdraws with its connections up; dl_drop_lockreq_ino matches inode resources only, an AG variant is needed). ===== ===== 2026-10-17 (session 17) A/B TOOLING WRITTEN, NOT BUILT IN THE TREE: dlm/dlm.c knob dl_noqueue_unanswered_wouldblock (1 default; 0 = the timed-out no-queue request re-sends for its whole budget, the same-build control) and injector dl_drop_lockreq_ag (AG number + 1: that AG's LOCK_REQ is reported sent and never sent, the AG twin of dl_drop_lockreq_ino). Compiles clean in a scratch copy (tests/evidence/nqu_frozen_090131, sv 2210402BF24378CE10980AB) and on all five platform kernels (tests/evidence/vmkb_20261017T072111Z). Harness tests/noqueue_unanswered_ab.sh <label> <wouldblock 0|1> [3/net/mesh/direct] [g3b]: B stages dirs with src+tgt files, A drops the target's home AG (the rename's mandatory pre-acquire) and loops 'touch dir; mv src tgt', C withdraws (mxfs_shutdown.sh flag 2), B appends to C's file; grades b_wait_s, A's post-replay flush wall, ls_s (ILOCK hold), P129-CLSKIP/P128-AILSTUCK, P-ACQ-NOQUEUE-UNANSWERED, cold audit. NEXT: make modules once no chain reloads from the tree, then run control and production arms alternately (3 each). ===== ===== 2026-10-17 (session 19) BUILT AND RUNNING: tree build 5E4D32A64FC67B3543A120C carries dl_noqueue_unanswered_wouldblock and dl_drop_lockreq_ag (modinfo). Queue tests/queues/nqu_wouldblock_ab.queue (tests/noqueue_unanswered_ab.sh, control/production alternating, 3 each, 3/net/mesh/direct g3b) launched detached 08:31Z, log tests/evidence/lapq_nquab.log; grade each lap's RESULT line and evidence dir per the harness header. ===== ===== 2026-10-17 (session 20) THE A/B MEASURED NOTHING: queue tests/queues/nqu_wouldblock_ab.queue (build 5E4D32A64FC67B3543A120C, 3/net/mesh/direct g3b, tests/evidence/lapq_nquab.log) ran 6 laps in 570 s, all VACUOUS: nquc1/nquf1/nquf3 'test15 logged no post-replay flush', nquc2/nquf2/nquc3 'no target's AG request left A for a remote master' (every target landed in one AG, ag=2, and A could decide it alone). nquc1 shows the staging does not hold the incident's shape even when a candidate is chosen: the control's rename (dl_drop_lockreq_ag on, wouldblock=0) returned rc=0 after 10.8 s with 8 P36-RETRY, long before C withdrew at +90 s, so no ILOCK was held across the recovery; A (test15) was elected, replayed C's slice and never printed 'peer joined -- flushing' (the post-replay flush this harness grades on). Next: find what prints that flush and when (it is the single->multi flush, not a per-recovery one), what ends the control rename's dropped-request wait after ~10 s, and stage the targets across AGs whose master is C (the victim) so the unanswered request is the dead master's, as in the incident. ===== 2026-10-18 (session 58) CODE READ: WHY THE nquab A/B WAS VACUOUS, AND WHAT A REPRODUCER MUST STAGE ON THE CURRENT CODE. The foreign replay no longer drains the AIL: xfs/xfs_mxfs_recovery.c:1531 and :1622 call mxfs_dlm_foreign_replay_barrier (xfs_mxfs_recovery.c:1288, log force + flush epoch + cached-view census, no xfs_ail_push_all_sync; its comment records the change from the join destage after a 0.90.57 DRBD measurement), so the replayer half of the 0.90.53 cycle (post-replay flush waiting on an AIL pinned by an ILOCK holder) cannot form there, and the 'peer joined -- flushing' line tests/noqueue_unanswered_ab.sh gates on (VACUOUS when absent) is not printed by a replay at all on this build: that gate, not only the AG staging, made nquc1/nquf1/nquf3 vacuous. The full AIL drain (mxfs_dlm_peer_joined_flush, xfs/xfs_mxfs_join.c:9-59) remains at two sites: the EFI-obligation engine's home write before its proof (xfs/xfs_mxfs_recov_obl.c:311 mxfs_recov_obl_home_flush, run only when the dead peer left open extent-free obligations) and the join (xfs/xfs_mxfs_join.c:408). NEXT: restage the A/B so the AIL-draining site actually runs while the rename holds the ILOCKs and waits on the dead master's AG: C dies with an open EFI obligation (a large-file truncate or unlink in flight at its withdraw; dbg_obl_engine_hold_ms exists for the engine's side), the rename's target AG mastered by C (establish mastership per lap with a probe), dl_noqueue_unanswered_wouldblock 0/1; grade the obligation engine's P-OBL-COMPLETE wall_ms and B's append wait instead of the replay flush line. A lap where the obligation engine did not run is VACUOUS.

defects.summary: On the physical DRBD pair, a cold read-back on either host in the minutes after a pulled host rejoins runs at about a third of that host's normal MXFS read rate: pve1 (850 EVO 250 GB, raw 217 MB/s, MXFS 134-135 MB/s otherwise) read 4.3-6.3 GB at 45-58 MB/s, pve2 (850 EVO 500 GB, raw 532 MB/s, MXFS 230 MB/s otherwise) at 71-75 MB/s. The cable-pull verify's 220 MB/s-derived bound failed on pve1 twice (6.3 GB > 118 s; 4.4 GB > 101 s) and passed once by 9 s (4.3 GB in 90.0 s, bound 99 s).
defects.evidence: 0.90.130 .deb, build 819E8893C17F0BF388CC9D7 on both, kernel 7.0.14-24-pve. tests/evidence/pve_cable_pull/20261016T021329Z (FAIL: pve1 read-back > 118 s for 1603 files, pve2 SHA_RC=0), 20261016T034055Z (FAIL: pve1 > 101 s for 1134 files at sdc 45-58 MB/s, diskstats_192.168.1.80.txt; pve2 62.5 s at 70-87 MB/s; the same 1134 files re-read on pve1 minutes later: 33.6 s = 135 MB/s, SHA_RC=0, single extents), 20261016T040003Z (PASS: pve1 90.0 s, pve2 59.4 s; ds3_192.168.1.80.txt: during the verify sdc reads 40-59 MB/s, sdc writes ~1 MB/s, sdc reads == drbd0 reads, so no competing writes, no resync and no other reader; the resync before it read 36-38 MB/s from sdc with drbd0 idle). No-pull baseline the same evening: 2048 files (8 GB) cold read-back pve1 61.2 s = 134 MB/s, pve2 35.7 s = 230 MB/s. Raw O_DIRECT 2 GB from the backing disk: pve1 217 MB/s, pve2 532 MB/s.
defects.next: Measure the average read size (diskstats reads completed and sectors) during a post-rejoin read-back versus a no-pull one: smaller reads after a rejoin (readahead lost, per-page reads under the lock path) is MXFS; the same size at a lower rate is the device. Reproduce on the KVM DRBD rig (scripts/drbd_rig.sh fence-test, then a timed cold read-back of files written across the cut) so the physical pair is not needed: a slowdown on NVMe-backed guest disks is MXFS's.
defects.impact_why: Pace only: no data lost and no stability event in three cable pulls (every acknowledged file intact on both hosts, kernel logs clean); the release bar for 2/net/mesh/drbd is integrity and stability (owner directive 2026-09-10), and the third pull's verify passed its bound.

defects.summary: After a victim loses every path (TCP lock network, multipath), a survivor task holding the ILOCKs of two inodes waits on an AG lock mastered by the dead victim (mxfs_trans_preacquire_inode_ags -> mxfs_ag_dlm_trylock -> mxfs_dlm_lock_retries, 60 retries at 1 s) while the replayer's post-replay single->multi flush waits for an AIL that those ILOCKs pin (xfsaild P129-CLSKIP ILOCK_NOWAIT_FAIL), so every survivor stalls until the retry budget runs out (~131 s).
defects.evidence: 0.90.53 (D283754F06E6D5F02655895), g8 lap s12fx8b run 20261005T213119Z-g8, tests/evidence/board_20261005T213119Z-g8_path_all_lost (row.log, stalls.txt) and the row's logs in board_20261005T213119Z-g8_path_peer_withdrawn/kmsg_test7_fromnode.gz: survivors test7..13 STALL max_ms 130992..131772 resuming within 1 s of each other; test7 replay complete at 24630.543 then 'peer joined -- flushing XFS dirty state before single->multi transition' and nothing until P234-RECOV-STAGE 3->4 at 24690.496; python3 pid 100371 in xfs_rename held the ILOCKs of 16456 and 4194434 while P-LKTIMEOUT-REMOTE master=2576642866 (the victim) and P36-RETRY retries_left 58..1; P128-AILSTUCK at 24663.56. Split out of D-NETMESH-MPATH-ALL-LOST-SURVIVORS-STALL-131S, whose 0.90.129 mechanism was a different one.
defects.next: Confirm in the code that the single->multi flush waits for the AIL to empty before the recovery completion, and that a task holding ILOCKs may wait on an AG lock mastered by a node already declared dead; the fix to argue is that such a wait fails fast (or drops its inode locks) once the master is declared dead, or the completion does not wait on a full AIL drain. ===== 2026-10-17 CODE READ: the fix for exactly this mechanism is in the tree: dlm/dlm.c dlm_lock_retries_impl, P-ACQ-NOQUEUE-UNANSWERED -- a no-queue request with no answer within one attempt answers would-block (its comment cites this 131 s incident), and mxfs_trans_preacquire_inode_ags (xfs/xfs_mxfs_ag_unlock.c) is TRYLOCK-only and on a miss hands off (drains its AG grants, unlocks the inodes, waits holding nothing). The post-replay flush still waits for a full AIL drain (mxfs_recov_obl_home_flush -> mxfs_dlm_peer_joined_flush -> xfs_ail_push_all_sync). Verification owed: kept path_all_lost/path_peer_withdrawn logs where P-ACQ-NOQUEUE-UNANSWERED fired with master_live=0 and the survivors' stall stayed in bound (a log sweep was running at the relay). ===== 2026-10-17 KEPT-LOG SWEEP: 19 P-ACQ-NOQUEUE-UNANSWERED lines with master_live=0 in kept path_* rows (2/4/8/16 nodes, 2026-10-05..15), every such row PASS. Two are AG requests (type=3): board_20261015T003919Z-g4_path_peer_withdrawn test3 25157.433 and test5 25157.363 (identical copies in board_20261015T011608Z-g4_path_failover), ag=1 EX to dead master 3128590244 0.3 s after the replayer's claim was refused; recovery stage 3->4 5.5 s later; survivor stalls 9.1-15.8 s. None of those rows shows the full original cycle: no P271-AGWANT/AGWAIT-SEAM hand-off at that instant (so the request may be the allocator's probe, not an ILOCK holder's preacquire), no P128-AILSTUCK/P129-CLSKIP anywhere in those rows. The fix (dlm/dlm.c ~10706, no-queue + no answer in one attempt -> would-block) has no same-build switch, so an A/B needs one: a knob restoring the old retry, plus a deterministic trigger (a rename across two directories whose AG preacquire targets an AG mastered by a node that withdraws with its connections up; dl_drop_lockreq_ino matches inode resources only, an AG variant is needed). ===== ===== 2026-10-17 (session 17) A/B TOOLING WRITTEN, NOT BUILT IN THE TREE: dlm/dlm.c knob dl_noqueue_unanswered_wouldblock (1 default; 0 = the timed-out no-queue request re-sends for its whole budget, the same-build control) and injector dl_drop_lockreq_ag (AG number + 1: that AG's LOCK_REQ is reported sent and never sent, the AG twin of dl_drop_lockreq_ino). Compiles clean in a scratch copy (tests/evidence/nqu_frozen_090131, sv 2210402BF24378CE10980AB) and on all five platform kernels (tests/evidence/vmkb_20261017T072111Z). Harness tests/noqueue_unanswered_ab.sh <label> <wouldblock 0|1> [3/net/mesh/direct] [g3b]: B stages dirs with src+tgt files, A drops the target's home AG (the rename's mandatory pre-acquire) and loops 'touch dir; mv src tgt', C withdraws (mxfs_shutdown.sh flag 2), B appends to C's file; grades b_wait_s, A's post-replay flush wall, ls_s (ILOCK hold), P129-CLSKIP/P128-AILSTUCK, P-ACQ-NOQUEUE-UNANSWERED, cold audit. NEXT: make modules once no chain reloads from the tree, then run control and production arms alternately (3 each). ===== ===== 2026-10-17 (session 19) BUILT AND RUNNING: tree build 5E4D32A64FC67B3543A120C carries dl_noqueue_unanswered_wouldblock and dl_drop_lockreq_ag (modinfo). Queue tests/queues/nqu_wouldblock_ab.queue (tests/noqueue_unanswered_ab.sh, control/production alternating, 3 each, 3/net/mesh/direct g3b) launched detached 08:31Z, log tests/evidence/lapq_nquab.log; grade each lap's RESULT line and evidence dir per the harness header. ===== ===== 2026-10-17 (session 20) THE A/B MEASURED NOTHING: queue tests/queues/nqu_wouldblock_ab.queue (build 5E4D32A64FC67B3543A120C, 3/net/mesh/direct g3b, tests/evidence/lapq_nquab.log) ran 6 laps in 570 s, all VACUOUS: nquc1/nquf1/nquf3 'test15 logged no post-replay flush', nquc2/nquf2/nquc3 'no target's AG request left A for a remote master' (every target landed in one AG, ag=2, and A could decide it alone). nquc1 shows the staging does not hold the incident's shape even when a candidate is chosen: the control's rename (dl_drop_lockreq_ag on, wouldblock=0) returned rc=0 after 10.8 s with 8 P36-RETRY, long before C withdrew at +90 s, so no ILOCK was held across the recovery; A (test15) was elected, replayed C's slice and never printed 'peer joined -- flushing' (the post-replay flush this harness grades on). Next: find what prints that flush and when (it is the single->multi flush, not a per-recovery one), what ends the control rename's dropped-request wait after ~10 s, and stage the targets across AGs whose master is C (the victim) so the unanswered request is the dead master's, as in the incident. ===== 2026-10-18 (session 58) CODE READ: WHY THE nquab A/B WAS VACUOUS, AND WHAT A REPRODUCER MUST STAGE ON THE CURRENT CODE. The foreign replay no longer drains the AIL: xfs/xfs_mxfs_recovery.c:1531 and :1622 call mxfs_dlm_foreign_replay_barrier (xfs_mxfs_recovery.c:1288, log force + flush epoch + cached-view census, no xfs_ail_push_all_sync; its comment records the change from the join destage after a 0.90.57 DRBD measurement), so the replayer half of the 0.90.53 cycle (post-replay flush waiting on an AIL pinned by an ILOCK holder) cannot form there, and the 'peer joined -- flushing' line tests/noqueue_unanswered_ab.sh gates on (VACUOUS when absent) is not printed by a replay at all on this build: that gate, not only the AG staging, made nquc1/nquf1/nquf3 vacuous. The full AIL drain (mxfs_dlm_peer_joined_flush, xfs/xfs_mxfs_join.c:9-59) remains at two sites: the EFI-obligation engine's home write before its proof (xfs/xfs_mxfs_recov_obl.c:311 mxfs_recov_obl_home_flush, run only when the dead peer left open extent-free obligations) and the join (xfs/xfs_mxfs_join.c:408). NEXT: restage the A/B so the AIL-draining site actually runs while the rename holds the ILOCKs and waits on the dead master's AG: C dies with an open EFI obligation (a large-file truncate or unlink in flight at its withdraw; dbg_obl_engine_hold_ms exists for the engine's side), the rename's target AG mastered by C (establish mastership per lap with a probe), dl_noqueue_unanswered_wouldblock 0/1; grade the obligation engine's P-OBL-COMPLETE wall_ms and B's append wait instead of the replay flush line. A lap where the obligation engine did not run is VACUOUS.

defects.evidence: 2026-10-17, ~/src/mxfs-b, 8/net/mesh/mpath g8 board lf8a run 20261017T130103Z-g8, row path_mount_degraded FAIL (row.log:131 'late: test14's longest stall, ms (got 35353)'; row.log:43 'test14 path b DOWN at 13:14:06, holding 40s'; row.log:47 STALL max_ms=35353 last_before_ms=1792242845506 first_after_ms=1792242880859 completed_in_window=2 errors_in_window=0 clock_off_ms=182); evidence /src/mxfs/tests/evidence/board_20261017T130103Z-g8_path_mount_degraded (kmsg_test{7..14}_fromnode.gz, stalls.txt, state_test14_*). Bound: tests/mpath/lib.sh BOUND_MS = tools/mpath_settings.sh stall-bound 30 s. lf8b (run 20261017T133521Z-g8) same row PASS late_stall_ms=16768; criteria.py shows the row FLAKY with 1 genuine FAIL in the last 11 runs.
defects.next: Read test14's kmsg for 13:14:06-13:14:46Z: what the 35 s gap was waiting on (path b's failed I/O retried on path a only after dm-multipath's no_path_retry/fast_io_fail, a DLM wait behind a peer, or an MXFS retry ladder), against the 16.8 s of the passing run; then a hypothesis. ===== ===== 2026-10-17 (session 31) THE FAILING WINDOW SAT IN A HOST WRITE STORM. The late window (test14 path b down 13:14:06Z, stall 35.4 s) began 19 s and 4 s after two tools/lun_pool.sh snapshot copies of CORRUPT noino laps started on the host's root ext4, the device that also carries every pool LUN: pmc4 (lun02, 13:13:47Z) and pdc4 (lun06, 13:14:02Z). Host sar (/var/log/sysstat/sa17, local = Z-5): nvme0n1 average await 0.42 ms (13:13), 1.26 ms (13:14), 22.4 ms (13:15), 29.0 ms (13:16), 1.6 ms (13:17), aqu-sz 104-116 at 13:15-13:16; kbdirty 13 MB, 1.36 G, 7.3 G, 3 MB at 13:13-13:16. A CAW probe under such a storm (tests/caw_host_storm_probe.sh hcs1, that record) measured the target's per-command latency rising from 10 ms to 1.95 s. Not yet shown: that the storm is what lengthened this stall. The passing run's window (lf8b, 16.8 s) must be checked against the host's state the same way, and test14's kmsg read for what the I/O waited on. Snapshots now go to /mxfs/snapshots (a separate disk), which removes the trigger from future boards but disposes nothing. NEXT: unchanged, plus sar for lf8b's path_mount_degraded window. ===== ===== 2026-10-17 (session 33) THE 35 S DECOMPOSED: ~15 S PATH FAILOVER (THE SAME IN THE PASSING RUN) + ~20 S OF SHARED-DIRECTORY HANDOFF WAITS WHOSE RELEASES RAN 10-100X SLOWER THAN IN THE PASSING RUN, IN THE MINUTE THE HOST'S DEVICE AVERAGED 22 MS PER I/O. Cuts (scripts/kmsg_window.py, raw evidence in this session's scratchpad g8/): FAIL test14 (we=1044411458) stall from mono 944.97 to 980.33 (offset 1792241900.532): 945.99-947.01 PR on shared dir 20971649 (P-LKTIMEOUT-REMOTE x1, P34-ACQ-SLOW dur_ms=2033); then a read of inode cluster daddr 10870248 stuck on path b (P-IOWAIT-STUCK 951.05/955.08/959.11, sdb TUR DID_TRANSPORT_DISRUPTED cmd_age=8s at 955.34, 'rejecting I/O to offline device' and multipath 'Failing path 8:16' at 960.458): path b went down at 945.5, so ~15 s of failover; then PR 960.5-968.69 (P34-ACQ-SLOW dur_ms=8189, P-LKTIMEOUT-REMOTE every 1.02 s to master 857071331), EX 968.82 rc=-35 then 969.87-976.17 (dur_ms=7317), EX 977.41 rc=-35 then 978.44-980.32 (dur_ms=2906). Master 857071331 = test10 (local= in its kmsg only). PASS (board_20261017T133521Z, stall 16768 ms, test14 offset 1792243171.615): path b down 13:47:21 = mono ~1669.4, P-IOWAIT-STUCK 1675.3-1683.4, offline + 'Failing path 8:16' at 1685.42, first op after at 1686.62: the whole stall is the failover; after it the dir lock came within 1.2 s. Release durations of the shared dir (P138-BAST dur_us, phases sa=log force, sb=flush, sd=durable, su=unlock): FAIL test10 475608 (su=471002), 674122 (sa=195838 su=442843), 467129; FAIL test11 342777 (sa=196417 sb=117419), 223729 (sb=96148 su=124547); PASS test10 5558, 43342, 6678; PASS test11 5305, 7003, 5353. FAIL test10's window also logs 205 P-LKTIMEOUT-HOLDER, 175 P958-ACQ-RETX and 26 P-CONVBLK-DENY on the dir (8 nodes queued on it). Host sar (sa17, local = Z-5): FAIL minute 08:15:01 nvme0n1 await 22.44 ms aqu-sz 104.45 %util 68.4, kbdirty 7.28 GB (08:14:01: 1.26 ms, 1.36 GB); PASS minute 08:48:01 await 0.73 ms aqu-sz 9.72, kbdirty 32 MB. READING (not yet a disposition): the excess over the passing run is the 8-node handoff chain of one shared directory, each handoff's I/O phases inflated by the host write storm (the two snapshot copies named above); the failover part is unchanged. NEXT: a controlled run that varies only the LUN's latency (netem delay on the g8 nodes' storage interfaces for the late window, or the storm on a quiet host) against the same row without it, to show that the late stall scales with storage latency; if it does, the record is a storage-environment effect and is disposed on that measurement; if the stall stays long without added latency, the handoff chain itself is the defect. ===== 2026-10-17 (session 38) BASELINE MEASURED (~/src/mxfs-b/tests/queues/netmesh8_path_rows_natural.queue, queue nmn, build 57C7184D46A87018889E689, 8/net/mesh/mpath g8, victim test14): path_mount_degraded PASS in all 4 rows; late stall 15847 ms (nmn1a, window 16:53:22Z), 16391 (nmn1b, 17:05:56Z), 15752 (nmn2a, 17:19:15Z), 16008 (nmn2b, 17:31:21Z), errors_in_window 0, mount_one_path_ms 4976-5261; host nvme0n1 sar await in each window's minute 0.91, 0.81, 0.73, 0.60 ms (/var/log/sysstat/sa17; nmn1b's window also runs 12 s into the minute ending 12:07:01 CDT, not read). On test14 the path taken away fails 'Failing path 8:0' 11.3 s after the first P-IOWAIT-STUCK (nmn1b 1285.884 -> 1297.157, nmn2a 2053.878 -> 2065.142, nmn2b 2750.638 -> 2761.970; nmn1a has no P-IOWAIT-STUCK in its segment, Failing path 8:0 at 574.222); the stall exceeds that interval by 5.1, 4.5 and 4.7 s, where P-IOWAIT-STUCK itself fires some seconds after the I/O stuck, so the interval understates the failover. By the queue's rules ENVIRONMENT READING REFUTED is not met (no stall over 30 s); HOLDS is not cleanly met on the literal excess reading (nmn1b 5.1 s). So on a quiet host this row passes at about half its bound; the incident's 35.4 s came with host await 22 ms. NEXT (the controlled run the queue names): the same late-window cut with injected target latency, MXFS against native XFS on the same multipath LUN and load, so the stall's growth with latency is attributed to the storage path or to MXFS.

defects.summary: After its peer is fenced on 2/net/mesh/mpath, the surviving node's file creates fail with EBUSY for up to half a second after its stall ends: xfs_dialloc returns -16 on the sole-survivor allocation path (P-DIALLOC err=-16 ino=0 single=1) and the create is cancelled, so the application's create returns an error on a healthy filesystem.
defects.evidence: Chain pfr95 (tests/evidence/lapchain_pfr95.out; laps c, e, h, board dirs tests/evidence/board_20261018T220615Z-g2e_path_fenced_return, board_20261018T221820Z-g2e_path_fenced_return, board_20261018T223645Z-g2e_path_fenced_return): row 32 'fence: no operation on test17 returned an error got=15 / 2 / 8 want=0'; the survivor test17's creates failed EBUSY 0.25-0.57 s after its stall ended (ops.log 'churn ERR EBUSY' / 'mutex ERR EBUSY'). Each failure is four lines in test17's kmsg_test17_fromnode.gz: 'P-DIALLOC dp=2097282 err=-16 ino=0 single=1', 'P-CREATE-ERR1 dialloc/icreate err=-16', 'P-CR62 new_ino=0 agno=0 err=-16 ... verdict=disk-read-err/badmagic' (new_ino=0: no inode was read), 'P-CR3-CANCEL error=-16 trans_dirty=0' (counts 15/2/8; none in laps a, b, d, f, g; none on test18). Session 99 log sweep of the three streams: no P946-VALIDATE-PUBPEND, P947-VALIDATE-NOMAGIC, PUBPEND-STORM or P-DIALLOC-VALIDATE-EIO line in the 300 lines before any failure; 40 P951-VALIDATE-OFF-SOLE lines per stream (the platter validation is off for a sole survivor). Code read (session 104): xfs_dialloc (xfs/libxfs/xfs_ialloc.c ~4236-4281) ends its AG sweep on any xfs_dialloc_try_ag error other than -EAGAIN and returns it; xfs_dialloc_try_ag (~3823) returns errors from mxfs_ag_dlm_trylock/mxfs_ag_dlm_lock (__mxfs_ag_dlm_lock, which documents 0 or -EAGAIN only), xfs_ialloc_read_agi, xfs_ialloc_ag_alloc and mxfs_dialloc_two_phase; none of the allocator's own -EBUSY returns (mxfs_dialloc_validate_candidate's P946/P947 arms) printed, so the -16 comes from a callee none of the probes names. Found while chasing D-2NODE-NETMESH-MPATH-REJOINED-NODE-WRITE-HANGS.
defects.next: HYPOTHESIS to write after one instrument (the source is not named by any probe): add a probe at each error return of xfs_dialloc_try_ag naming the step (AG trylock / AG lock / read_agi / ag_alloc / two_phase) and, for the AG lock, the DLM's own return; rerun path_fenced_return on 2/net/mesh/mpath (tests/mpath/lap_chain.sh, g2e) until a lap reproduces the EBUSY, then write the hypothesis from the named step. ===== ===== 2026-10-19 (session 105) INSTRUMENT CHAIN LAUNCHED. tests/mpath/lap_chain.sh laps 2/net/mesh/mpath g2e pfi 8 --prep --rows path_fenced_return,chk_clean from ~/src/mxfs-g (7AAA11F061B708FA7B93C88, probe P-DIALLOC-TRYAG-ERR; its xfs/libxfs/xfs_ialloc.c identical to main's), started 02:54Z; laps pfia and pfib each read path_fenced_return PASS, alloc_witness PASS and chk_clean CLEAN in their own run (the chain's rc=1 is row 32's FLAKY history on the board, not those laps). NEXT: read laps c-h (tests/evidence/board_2-net-mesh-mpath_path_fenced_return_chk_clean_g2e_pfi<x>.log and the row's kmsg captures) for 'churn ERR EBUSY' / P-DIALLOC err=-16 and the P-DIALLOC-TRYAG-ERR step that names its source; write the hypothesis from that step. ===== ===== 2026-10-19 (session 106) THE INSTRUMENT NAMES THE STEP: THE AG LOCK, REFUSED BY THE LEDGER AS A DOUBLE GRANT AGAINST THE FENCED PEER'S RECORD. Chain pfi lap c (run_id 20261019T030908Z-g2e, ~/src/mxfs-g 7AAA11F061B708FA7B93C88, 2/net/mesh/mpath, test17 survivor, test18 fenced; evidence /src/mxfs/tests/evidence/board_20261019T030908Z-g2e_path_fenced_return): row.log 'FAIL fence: no operation on test17 returned an error got=1 want=0' (stalls.txt errors_in_window=1; load_test17/ops.log:2313 '1792379453091 1792379453092 mutex ERR EBUSY', 03:10:53.091Z). kmsg_test17_fromnode.gz:184752-184757, in order: 'P-TAUTH-DOUBLE-GRANT page=5809 entry=15 type=3 ino=0 ag=2 req node=1145618859 inc=3000484936412414679 mode=5 vs record ex=140861380/7162050377496661032 holders=0x0 -- the master decided a conflicting grant; refused' (972.124918), 'P-DIALLOC-TRYAG-ERR agno=2 step=ag-lock err=-16 trylock=1 single=1 comm=python3 pid=16611 -- this AG visit failed with an error that ends the create's whole AG sweep' (972.124930), 'P-DIALLOC dp=8388738 err=-16 ino=0 single=1', 'P-CREATE-ERR1 dialloc/icreate err=-16', 'P-CR62 new_ino=0 agno=0 err=-16 ...', 'P-CR3-CANCEL error=-16 ... trans_dirty=0' (972.126203). 140861380 is test18, the fenced node (test18's P-SESSION-POISON node 140861380 at 842.580). So the -16 is the survivor's AG-2 trylock: its own DLM, master of a one-node view, decided an EX grant while the durable ledger page still recorded the fenced node's EX on that AG, and the ledger refused the conflicting grant (-EBUSY); xfs_dialloc_try_ag returned it from its ag-lock step and xfs_dialloc ended the whole sweep on it (it continues only on -EAGAIN). defects.summary: A TCP mount whose root inode lock can never be granted (its master unreachable) no longer fails: after the membership settle it spends rounds of 60 root-inode retries, parks (P-LKRETRY-PARK, 'parking and asking again, NOT shutting down') and asks again without end, so mount(8) never returns on its own; it answers SIGTERM only after 1.8-18.6 s or more, and once ignored both timeout's TERM and the ssh bound and completed only when connectivity came back. The undiscoverable-peer trigger is now refused at the settle gate (memb_unreached_refuse); any other way the root lock's master stays unreachable after the gate (a peer reachable by multicast whose lock port is blocked) still reaches this wait.

defects.summary: A shared LUN with 4096-byte logical blocks (4K-native, what most new arrays present) cannot be formatted: mkfs.mxfs fails at its first write, and every on-disk layout and I/O path assumes 512-byte logical blocks.
defects.evidence: 2026-10-19 (session 1c324e00), tests/fourkn_lun.sh + tests/fourkn_mount_probe.sh, log tests/evidence/fourkn_20261019.log: an SCST vdisk_fileio LUN with blocksize=4096 bound to test31/test32 (blockdev --getss 4096, --getpbsz 4096). Published 0.90.130 (v0.90.130 source rebuilt to srcversion 1E9C0DE7364AD47BCDDE54A, the release's) and the 0.90.131 release build (8DAEC6B8298ADB049222D74) both: 'mkfs.mxfs: pwrite at offset 4096 failed: Invalid argument', rc=1, at the journal superblock, the first write (a 512-byte O_DIRECT pwrite, tools/mkfs_mxfs.c write_sectors called with 512 bytes from format_journal); both mounts then refused 'Invalid superblock magic number'. Nothing is written before the failure. The 512-byte assumption is everywhere (scout, raw file:line): mkfs writes XFS sectsize 512 (tools/mkfs_mxfs.c:97, :1004) and log sectsize 0; MXFS_JOURNAL_SECTOR_SIZE 512 (dlm/journal.h:57); the per-sector SCSI COMPARE AND WRITE sends LBA = byte offset / 512, 1 block, 1024 bytes (pal/linux/kern.c:8406-8421, caw_manual_bio :8221, :8242) with no block-size check; only the whole-page swap checks bdev_logical_block_size == 512 (:8683); dlm/mount.c:1913 a 1024-byte CAW buffer; MXFS_TAUTH_ROOT_BYTES 512; tools/mxfs_admin.c:205 refuses sectsize != 512. The rig has only ever served 512-byte LUNs (scripts/scst_setup.sh:54 blocksize=512). UNEXPLAINED: a tester (gyptazy.com blog, 0.90.130, fdisk 'Sector size (logical/physical): 4096 bytes / 16384 bytes') reported mkfs.mxfs 'formatted successfully' through every region; a 512-byte O_DIRECT write on a device whose kernel logical block size is 4096 cannot succeed, and their mount output is not shown. ===== 2026-10-24, by hand with no tree change (scratch dir /tmp/claude-1000/-home-steve-src-mxfs/da1eb4b4-ab66-45b7-bfdb-8f606327c3ee/scratchpad/tmp.P0u19P2Z5I, not kept): 0.90.132's packaged mkfs.mxfs (dpkg-deb -x dist/0.90.132/mxfs_0.90.132_amd64.deb, 'mkfs.mxfs version 0.90.132') formatted a 2048 MiB 512-byte loop image through 'tests/mkfs_layout_identity.py image' within one wall-clock second (date +%s 1792832175 before and after); the candidate's tools/mkfs_mxfs (0.90.134) formatted the same way by hand but with SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=1792832175: 'tests/mkfs_layout_identity.py compare' -> 'IDENTICAL ... 0 differing range(s), 0 byte(s)', rc=0 (the printed size labels differ, GB vs GiB, which nothing writes to the volume). Against the script's own fixed epoch 1700000000 the same pair differs in 4246 ranges, 19101 bytes (the first 40 all in the authority ledger). So the only obstacle to the release's identity check is the test's pinned epoch. ===== 2026-10-24, candidate 0.90.134 attempt 2026-10-24T10:25:09Z (tools/mkfs_mxfs as frozen): 'tests/mkfs_layout_identity.py against <0.90.132 mkfs.mxfs from dpkg-deb -x dist/0.90.132/mxfs_0.90.132_amd64.deb> tools/mkfs_mxfs <scratch dir> 2048 512' -> reference format 1 inside wall clock second 1792841434, candidate formatted at SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=1792841434, 'IDENTICAL ... 0 differing range(s), 0 byte(s)', rc=0 (images in this session's scratchpad, not kept). The against subcommand that takes the reference's second is in the frozen tree; the release's final layout check is this command on the final build.
defects.next: 1. Fail closed with the cause: mkfs.mxfs (BLKSSZGET) and the mount (bdev_logical_block_size of the device) refuse a logical block size other than 512 with a message naming it, so no layout written for 512 can ever be mounted on a 4K-native device. 2. Learn what the tester's kernel saw: blockdev --getss and --getpbsz on their /dev/sdc and their mount output. 3. 4K-native support, design written first: the format's sector size, the journal sector, the disklock and ledger units and the CAW unit all taken from the device's logical block size; then a rig LUN of each size in the release matrix (scripts/scst_setup.sh blocksize) so both are verified. ===== 2026-10-19 (session 1c324e00) OWNER DECISION: 4K-native support is NOT in 0.90.131 (it ships refusing 4K-native LUNs at format, as 0.90.130 does); it is the work of 0.90.132. defects.summary: The F4 committed-never-submitted registry never sees a successful FUA write of a bmbt buffer: on a multi-node mount every bmbt write takes the FUA arm of xfs_buf_submit_ex (pal/linux/xfs_buf.c:13645-13649), which on success completes through xfs_buf_ioend and returns at :13796, before xfs_buf_submit_bio (:13803) where mxfs_f4_submit stamps submit_gen (:8956). So a directory bmbt leaf written by FUA keeps submit_gen 0, its completion leaves the record open (xfs/xfs_mxfs_obligation.c:550), and the registry reports it committed-never-submitted: P285-F4-BLI-FREED-OPEN, P285-F4-REC truth=GEN-OPEN-NOT-DIRTY, P491-REL-UNDEST f4_open, P286-F4-ORPHAN and the orphan counter at unmount, all false for these buffers. With f4_gate=0 (default) the count changes nothing (relbar census-and-proceed :479-500, certificate counters :1072-1075, cause tags :706-711, P491-REL-UNDEST probe only, and the evict shutdown condition xfs_mxfs_evict.c:562-563 leaves f4_open out); it makes the telemetry unable to show a real committed-never-submitted directory buffer and would make f4_gate=1 defer every release of a btree directory after such a write.
defects.evidence: 0.90.131 release chain window lap 7 (run 20261019T140254Z, build 8DAEC6B8298ADB049222D74), test1 kernel ring tests/evidence/w2laps_0.90.131_dmesg_test1_140918Z.gz: P285-F4-BLI-FREED-OPEN lines 2080 (daddr 25850600 committed_gen 3512), 5939 (24784056, 3807), 12099 (24784056, 4312); P491-REL-UNDEST line 15112 (ino=25165952 held_mode=5 f4_open=2 comm=kworker/u5:15); P285-F4-REC truth=GEN-OPEN-NOT-DIRTY bli=0 dirty=0 in_ail=0 delwri=0 submit_gen=0 lines 26331-26332 (3646.40); P286-F4-ORPHAN lines 73137-73138 under umount (3759.44); F4-REGISTRY-TOTAL line 73141. Against a lost commit: the last P66-LEAFWRITE of both leaves (3637.287, numrecs 170+167) equals the in-core extent count (P62-IFLUSH-FORCE if_nextents=337 leafsum=337 at 3637.309), after the newest commit (gen 4312 by 3634.5) and before the release at 3641.1. Contradiction left open: that write is xfs_bwrite of the cached leaf (xfs/xfs_mxfs_dir_bmbt.c:1116-1126), whose submit should stamp submit_gen (pal/linux/xfs_buf.c:8956, mxfs_f4_submit) and whose completion should retire the record, yet the record read submit_gen=0 nine seconds later. Not audited: window laps run no chk_clean and the next lap reformats the LUN. ===== 2026-10-24, same-build A/B on candidate 0.90.134 attempt 2026-10-24T06:38:23Z (module BE3695D2590A65F742F9816), lane tests/evidence/lanes/g2b_w12_20261024T064106Z steps 4-9, 2/net/mesh/mpath path_fenced_return on g2b (test15 survivor, test16 victim), PF_KEEP_KMSG=1, each arm on a fresh prep; every row PASS. defects.summary: On the 0.90.131 release build posix_multi fails at 8 and 16 nodes on both transports: rank 1's ls of the 128 test files (posix_multi.sh:56-57) meets a cached shell of a reused number for most names, each one is poisoned (P-RELOAD-XINCARN-POISON, new in 0.90.131), and the lookup's retire waits for the revocation work's reference, queued on the inode BAST workqueue behind the drains: about 2.5 s per name.
defects.evidence: Boards: board_8-disk-caw-direct_g8_bL2_0.90.131.log:66, board_16-disk-caw-direct_g16_bL1_0.90.131.log:58, board_8-net-mesh-mpath_g8b_bL3_0.90.131.log:63, board_16-net-mesh-direct_g16_bL3_0.90.131.log:75 (FAIL posix_multi BUDGET_EXHAUSTED=1 rank 1 'step=pm own node1_file<FPN> exists', every other rank 'pm barrier count' then FAIL '... sees nodeN renamed content(exp=posix_N got=)'). The watchdog label is the previous step because ckeq's ls argument is evaluated before its step update. tests/evidence/run_posix_multi_20261019T152054Z-g8/kernlog_test7.gz 15:26:57-15:27:12: one set per name every ~2.5 s, comm=ls: P139-RECYCLE-UNLINKED, P-RELOAD-XINCARN-POISON incore_mode=0100644 disk_mode=0100644 (another generation) aliases=0 inuse=0, P566-POISON-N, P34H-INCARN-REVOKED nrpages=0; the first name's ladder visible (P34H-POISON-EVICT try 1..8 i_count=2, P566-POISON-DRAINWAIT drained_at 130 ms, P567); later ladders rate-limited out. 0.90.130 passed the row in 4-7 s with checks=56. On a fresh prep (tests/posix_multi_incarn_ab.sh, 8/disk/caw/direct g8, tests/evidence/20261019T164853Z_pmincarn_g8a) the row passed with lookup_dir_incarn_verify=1 in 3 s and 13 s: the stall needs dead shells left by earlier rows. H-PM1 (the lookup_dir_incarn_verify arm is the cost) REFUTED by that A/B. ===== BOARD CELLS this record accounts for (posix_multi FAIL: rank 1 BUDGET_EXHAUSTED at 'pm own node1_fileN exists', its peers' barrier checks failed): 8/disk/caw/mpath 2026-10-19T14:29:23Z (run 20261019T142249Z-g8b, board_8-disk-caw-mpath_g8b_bL1_0.90.131.log:53); 16/disk/caw/direct 2026-10-19T14:29:31Z (20261019T142249Z-g16, board_16-disk-caw-direct_g16_bL1_0.90.131.log:58); 8/net/mesh/mpath 2026-10-19T15:51:28Z (20261019T154607Z-g8b, board_8-net-mesh-mpath_g8b_bL3_0.90.131.log:63); 16/net/mesh/direct 2026-10-19T15:51:52Z (20261019T154607Z-g16, board_16-net-mesh-direct_g16_bL3_0.90.131.log:75).

Directed repro: run posix_multi repeatedly on one prep (p2 already took 13 s vs 3 s) and time rank 1's ls; build in a sibling (tools/sibling_sync.sh ~/src/mxfs-b) while main-tree queues run. ===== H-PM3 REFUTED as the stall's cause (tests/posix_multi_incarn_ab.sh KNOB=poison_revoke_idle_skip PRE_ROWS='fio_perf cache_coherency strong_consistency', 8/disk/caw/direct g8, ~/src/mxfs-b C4E512657B76E7AA7963116, console tests/evidence/pmrv_ab.console): p1_F1 PASS 3 s, p1_C0 FAIL BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, p2_F1 (switch 1) FAIL BUDGET_EXHAUSTED the same way. In p2_F1 rank 1's kernlog (~/src/mxfs-b/tests/evidence/run_posix_multi_20261019T172141Z-g8/kernlog_test7.gz:42170-42268) every name: P95-SAMETYPE-RELOAD (same mode, other generation), P-RELOAD-XINCARN-POISON aliases=0 inuse=0 dlm_mode=0 comm=ls, P-POISON-IDLE-NOREVOKE (the switch took effect), nothing for 2.4 s, P95C-SAMETYPE-WAIT resolved=0 rounds=201, then P34H-POISON-EVICT try=1 i_count=1 (retired at once) and the re-get adopts the new incarnation: 24 P95C-SAMETYPE-WAIT in the file, all resolved=0 rounds=201. The 2.4 s is the same-type resolver of xfs_lookup (xfs/xfs_inode.c, the while p95c < 200 loop) reloading a shell its first reload poisoned: it exits only when a reload clears i_dlm_stale, and a poisoned shell is never adopted in place. Directed A/B running: tests/recreated_dir_peer_mkdir.sh KNOB=sametype_poison_break (peer mkdir -p timed against 195 ms, posix_multi's per-name share of its 25 s budget), ~/src/mxfs-g D92BBDD701614A7502A4308, console tests/evidence/rdm2.console; the board-shape A/B (posix_multi_incarn_ab.sh KNOB=sametype_poison_break) follows on g8. H-PM3's switch (poison_revoke_idle_skip) stays default 1 in that build and is A/B'd on its own with H-PM4 on: with the loop gone, the retire's wait for a revocation reference (8 tries, 254 ms of sleeps, then a drain wait) is the next cost a name can pay. ===== TWO MECHANISMS, EACH MEASURED ALONE WITH THE OTHER HELD ON (tests/recreated_dir_peer_mkdir.sh, dir->dir reuse, REUSE_GAP=10; per-name budget 195 ms = posix_multi's 25 s report budget over 128 names). (2) After the break, the poisoned-shell retire waits out the reference of the revocation queued for the shell behind the inode BAST workqueue's drains (H-PM3, refuted earlier only as the cause of the 2.4 s stall, which the 200 rounds dominated): switch poison_revoke_idle_skip (a shell with no dentry, no page cache and no mapping gets no revocation). pm3b on D92BBDD701614A7502A4308 with sametype_poison_break=1: skip=1 laps 1-6 PASS 24-38 ms; skip=0 laps 7-11 FAIL 492-551 ms (console tests/evidence/pm3b.console). Open until the release boards' posix_multi rows pass at 8 and 16 nodes. ===== Mechanism (1) A/B completed on the release candidate D92BBDD701614A7502A4308 (run stab, 2/disk/caw/mpath g2c test29/test30, console tests/evidence/stab.console, evidence tests/evidence/20261019T174858Z_rdm_stab): sametype_poison_break=1 laps 1-6 PASS 24-36 ms; =0 laps 7-12 FAIL 2425-2453 ms, every lap P95C-SAMETYPE-WAIT and P-RELOAD-XINCARN-POISON (reached). defects.summary: On the 0.90.131 release build the lookup's type-flip resolver (xfs/xfs_inode.c, P95-TYPEFLIP-RELOAD) reloads a cached shell whose entry names another type; the reload finds the platter holding the new incarnation and poisons the shell (P-RELOAD-XINCARN-POISON, incarn_poison_unexposed, new in 0.90.131) instead of adopting it, and the resolver then reloads the poisoned shell for its remaining 200 rounds (a poisoned shell is never adopted in place) and fails the lookup -ESTALE (P201-TYPEFLIP-UNRESOLVED-FAIL): mkdir of a name that exists on the platter as the directory the entry names fails.
defects.evidence: dirent_type_integrity FAIL on board_8-disk-caw-direct_g8_bL2_0.90.131.log:99 (run 20261019T152054Z-g8, nodes_pass=2/8, test8 test9 test11 test12 test13 test14 each unresolved=1 failed_estale=1) and board_4-disk-caw-mpath_g4b_bL1_0.90.131.log:107 (run 20261019T142249Z-g4b, nodes_pass=1/4, test18 test19 test20 unresolved=2 failed_estale=2). g8 test8 kernlog (run_dirent_type_integrity_20261019T152054Z-g8, window from MXFS_DIRENT_WINDOW): 15:39:01 P95-TYPEFLIP-RELOAD ino=25703836 incore_ftype=1 dirent_ftype=2 name=r14 tries=6; 15:39:01 P-RELOAD-XINCARN-POISON ino=25703836 incore_gen=1029968493 disk_gen=1998383309 incore_mode=0100644 disk_mode=040755 aliases=0 inuse=0 dlm_mode=3 comm=mkdir; 15:39:04 P95B-TYPEFLIP-WAIT resolved=0 rounds=201; P201-TYPEFLIP-UNRESOLVED-FAIL ... name=r14 comm=mkdir; the same on all six failing nodes (same ino, gen, name). g4b test18: ino 23548 name=r1 and 23550 name=r2, each P95-TYPEFLIP-RELOAD, P-RELOAD-XINCARN-POISON incore_mode=0100644 disk_mode=040755, P95B resolved=0 rounds=201, P201 comm=mkdir. Also 4/disk/caw/direct (run 20261019T152054Z-g4, kernlog test4:107075 and test5:107313 at 15:40:39): P201-TYPEFLIP-UNRESOLVED-FAIL ino=4203183 incore_ftype=1 dirent_ftype=2 name=d2 comm=mkdir. The resolver loop (xfs_inode.c, the while p95w < 200 around mxfs_dlm_reload_inode) breaks only on a mode match or mode 0; the P201 relookup arm requires the platter equal to the in-core shell or contradicting the entry, and here the platter (directory) agrees with the entry, so neither fires. defects.summary: After a total storage outage of a 2-node TCP cluster (one node frozen and fenced, the other self-fenced when its storage hung), neither node can mount again without a reboot: the fenced node's rejoin mount waits two 64 s total-outage scans and is then refused because its own same-boot predecessor's record publishes its key (P-BOOT-KEY-UNCLASSIFIED, fail closed), and the survivor's remount is refused at once because its own predecessor departed dirty in the same kernel and waits for a peer to fence its key (P305-PR-SAME-BOOT-DIRTY-PREDECESSOR). Each node needs the other to fence its predecessor. Measured as an rc=124 'remount did not complete' only because the row's 45 s bound was shorter than the scans.
defects.evidence: Lap frke3, run 20261019T191249Z-g2e, build 92FBF2A83F12160EE95EA2E (D-RIG-SCST-RECONFIG-SUSPENDS-EVERY-LUN-BEHIND-A-FROZEN-GUESTS-COMMAND is the outage). board_20261019T191249Z-g2e_path_fenced_return/row.log:16 'test18 thawed at 19:16:13', :28 'ABORT: the remount of test18 (rejoin) did not complete: MXFS-RS-STATUS v=1 host=test18 rc=124'; board_2-net-mesh-mpath_path_fenced_return_chk_clean_g2e_frke3a.log:105 'BLOCK alloc_witness (node fault: test18:sync-wedged[mxfs-worker{MXFS}[msleep]...v5_boot_hb_fn...],sync{other}[super_lock]super_lock+0xe9/0x160<iterate_supers+0x5b/0xe0<ksys_sync...)'. test18's kernel log of the row: kmsg_test18_fromnode.gz (187362 lines; its uptime-to-wall mapping steps +131.126 s across the freeze at line ~187005/187066); the unmount after the thaw completed at uptime 8663.74 (P-TCP-RELEASE-POISONED for 7 AGs, DLM shutdown complete); the remount that follows is what timed out. ===== BOARD CELLS this record accounts for (run 20261019T191249Z-g2e, board_2-net-mesh-mpath_path_fenced_return_chk_clean_g2e_frke3a.log:104-106, the lap that ran through the host-wide storage loss of 19:14:14-19:15:03Z): 2/net/mesh/mpath path_fenced_return ABORTED 2026-10-19T19:19:00Z, alloc_witness BLOCKED 2026-10-19T19:19:23Z (test18 sync-wedged), chk_clean FAIL 2026-10-19T19:19:28Z (PRE-ASSERT: not mounted on test17 test18).
defects.next: Read test18's kmsg after uptime 8663.74: what the rejoin mount waited for (a dead survivor's slot, recovery, a barrier, the lease) and for how long; read the remount's own bound in tests/mpath/path_fenced_return.sh; decide whether a mount into a cluster whose only other member self-fenced is bounded by design (and then whether the bound is right) or hangs. ===== WHAT THE MOUNT WAS DOING (kmsg_test18_fromnode.gz:187328-187362): the rejoin mount began at uptime 8663.750 (TCP transport, PR key 0x4acfc087553ec557 re-registered on both paths, WE-AR held, disklock initialized, P-BOOT-STATE IDLE at 8663.809); nothing logged for 64.0 s; 8727.849 'P-BOOT-SCAN-FROZEN 2 occupied record(s) unchanged for 64041 ms -- TOTAL OUTAGE: 2 victim(s)', 'P-BOOT-SCAN-VERDICT victims=2 window_ms=62500 -- total outage, claiming', 'P-BOOT-CLAIMED ... provisional bootstrap owner; no slot, no grant, no filesystem write until RECOVERY_COMPLETE' (EOF: the row captured the log there). test17 had self-fenced and withdrawn (P163-WITHDRAW-STAMP), lease 'missed renewal 116/150' at its EOF. Harness bound: tests/mpath/lib.sh:480 pf_remount runs 'timeout 40 umount; timeout 45 mount' inside measure's 100 s ssh bound, shorter than the design's total-outage scan window (62.5 s) plus recovery; the sync on super_lock waited on this mount's superblock lock. H-RJ1 (to test): not a hang but the designed total-outage bootstrap outlasting a bound derived for a rejoin into a live cluster; open: whether the claimed bootstrap then completed recovery and mounted, and in what time. Test: the same shape (freeze V, take the survivor's storage until it self-fences, thaw V, remount V) with V's kmsg kept until the mount returns; read P-BOOT-CLAIMED -> RECOVERY_COMPLETE -> mount return. ===== ===== H-RJ1 TESTED (session 99e17361), tests/mpath/total_outage_rejoin.sh (new: freeze V, S fences V, mute both of S's paths until S closes its authority, unmute, thaw V, V remounts with its kernel log followed until the mount returns, then a bounded sync, then S rejoins), 2/net/mesh/mpath g2e (V=test18, S=test17), main tree 92FBF2A83F12160EE95EA2E, run 20261019T201525Z-tor1, evidence tests/evidence/board_20261019T201525Z-tor1_total_outage_rejoin (row.log, kmsg_test1{7,8}_fromnode.gz, boot_test18.txt, s_remount_test17.txt), console tests/evidence/tor1.console. test17 fenced test18 38 s after the freeze; test17 stopped itself 31 s after its paths were muted (7 lines). test18's rejoin: umount rc 0, then mount rc=32 after 129613 ms: P-BOOT-SCAN-FROZEN 'TOTAL OUTAGE: 2 victim(s)' at 64036 ms, P-BOOT-CLAIMED, a second P-BOOT-SCAN-FROZEN 63993 ms later, then 'P-BOOT-KEY-UNCLASSIFIED victim slot=1 node=942485699 publishes OUR key 0xb4921d4d127bc5aa -- a same-boot predecessor inside a total outage cannot be preempted by us; bootstrap refused (fail closed)', P-BOOT-ABORTED-BEFORE-SEAL, P-BOOT-MOUNT-REFUSED (dlm/v5_mount.c:5784-5794). A sync on test18 then returned rc 0. test17's remount (s_remount_test17.txt): mount rc=32 in 1037 ms, 'P305-PR-SAME-BOOT-DIRTY-PREDECESSOR slot=0 ... our previous incarnation departed dirty in this same kernel', 'TCP mount: SCSI PR register failed (-17)'. H-RJ1 CONFIRMED on its first half (not a hang: the designed total-outage bootstrap outlasted a bound derived for a live cluster) and the open question answered: the bootstrap does NOT complete; it refuses. NEXT: (1) whether a reboot of one node recovers the cluster (new boot, new key: it can preempt both victim keys and recover, after which the other node's dirty predecessor is fenced and its remount admitted) — measure it; (2) design, written before any patch: a same-boot predecessor this kernel itself unmounted has no I/O in flight (its unmount drained or failed every bio) and its key IS this boot's registration, so its death is provable locally; whether the bootstrap may classify it as fenced-by-local-proof and the dirty-predecessor remount may proceed when the bootstrap owner recovers its slice, and what in-flight-at-the-target window (SCST holds TMF-aborted commands up to 3x timeout) that proof must cover; (3) refuse at the first scan when the refusal is already decided by the own-key check, not after a second 64 s window.
defects.impact_why: Measured on the designed shape (tests/mpath/total_outage_rejoin.sh, 2/net/mesh/mpath g2e, main tree 92FBF2A83F12160EE95EA2E, tests/evidence/board_20261019T201525Z-tor1_total_outage_rejoin): the rejoin mount RETURNED (mount_rc=32 after 129613 ms, not a hang), a sync on the node right after returned rc 0, and the survivor's remount returned rc=32 in 1037 ms; no shutdown, crash or hang beyond the outage itself, which fenced both nodes by design, and no data was written by a refused mount. The defect is that the cluster cannot recover from a total outage without a node reboot, plus the 129.6 s before a refusal knowable at the first scan: recovery availability and pace, not integrity or stability.

defects.summary: tests/tooling/alloc_witness.sh fills each node's AG partition with creates until one carves a chunk, bounded by a fixed AW_FILL_MAX=8192. In multi-node mode a fully-free inode chunk is kept, not released (xfs/libxfs/xfs_ialloc.c:4789-4808, INODE-CHUNK-KEEP), so after the suite's path rows a node's partition can hold more free inodes in kept chunks than 8192: the fill ends with no carve, that rank aborts, the other rank waits for it at the rendezvous until the row's 120 s budget, and chk_clean then has no sealed witness (release=INDETERMINATE).
defects.evidence: BOARD CELLS: 2/net/mesh/mpath alloc_witness FAIL 2026-10-20T10:44:45Z (test31:BUDGET_EXHAUSTED test32:BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, run 20261020T094530Z-g2d, release chain wave bL1, build B0D2E3F5A70C96237681DF2, tests/evidence/board_2-net-mesh-mpath_g2d_bL1_0.90.131.log:127) and chk_clean FAIL 2026-10-20T10:45:13Z (:129, test31 verdict=CLEAN release=INDETERMINATE rc=0 errors=0: no trustworthy coverage witness). tests/evidence/alloc_witness/20261020T094530Z-g2d/rank2.txt (written 10:42:54Z): 'ABORT 8192 creates in the node's AG partition never carved a chunk; the free reserve could not be exhausted inside AW_FILL_MAX'; rank1.txt (10:42:37Z) FILL affine_ag=0 files=124 carved=1, SNAP S0, then nothing until the budget (10:44:48Z). Kernel logs run_alloc_witness_20261020T094530Z-g2d/kernlog_test3{1,2}.gz: P-TAUTH-PAGE-FULL 0, P-CAP-PARK 0, 'capacity=60' 0, rc=-122 0, hung task 0 (the one 'Shutting down' on test32 is the goingdown ioctl at 10:41:13, 'User initiated shutdown received', before the row: the path_peer_withdrawn row's injection). The cold audit tests/evidence/chk_clean_2node_20261020T104501Z.log (after the row, the fill's files still present: the witness removes nothing on abort): icount=39168 ifree=8410; AG 1 (rank 2's affine AG, partition = AGs with agno mod 4 == 1) count=20416 freecount=7303 over 319 inobt records, 113 of them fully free (kept chunks), AGs 5/9/13/17 64 free each: so before the fill AG 1 held about 7303 + 8192 free inodes, about 15.5k, against the fill's bound of 8192. Not D-TCP-4NODE-NOQUEUE-TRY-WAITS-9S-ON-FULL-LEDGER-PAGE-CREATES-STALL: no page filled and the fill's creates did not stall.
defects.next: After the release chain's boards end (no harness edit under a running chain): bound the fill by what the partition actually holds, read at the row's start (each partition AG's free count, plus the chunk the fill dir is in), or by the row's own budget left for its later phases, so 'never carved' means the cluster could not create, never that the bound was short; make the waiting rank stop when the other rank's file says ABORT. Then rerun alloc_witness,chk_clean on 2/net/mesh/mpath g2d on the release build, amend the two cells as the detector's (tools/criteria.py amend) with this record's evidence, and remove this record as FIXED AND VERIFIED (the lab).
defects.impact_why: No MXFS behaviour failed: the witness's fill made every one of its 8192 creates without an error and its node's partition simply held more free inodes than the fill's fixed bound; the cold audit after the row was CLEAN (errors=0).

defects.summary: scripts/release.sh runs the platform build checks in 'while IFS= read -r check; do ... eval "$check"; done <<< "$checks"'; the first check (scripts/vm_kbuild_check.sh, which runs ssh) reads the loop's stdin, so the here-string's remaining lines are consumed and every later platform's build check is skipped without a word.
defects.evidence: MEASURED in the 0.90.131 release chain (tests/evidence/full_verify_0.90.131.log lines 16-59, 2026-10-20T19:52Z): one line '=== MeshXFS 0.90.131 — platform build check: scripts/vm_kbuild_check.sh pve9 6.17.2-1-pve 7.0.14-19-pve ===' and then straight to '.deb packages on the debian12 lab node'; tools/platforms.py build-checks prints seven (pve9, pve92, ubuntu2404, rhel9, ubuntu2604, debian13, debian12). Read from scripts/release.sh:102-110.
defects.next: Fix after the 0.90.131 publish (the tree must stay the chain's build until then): eval "$check" < /dev/null; then run scripts/release.sh without --publish on a scratch output dir and confirm one '=== ... platform build check' line per released platform. ===== 2026-10-24: fixed in the tree for the next attempt: scripts/release.sh runs each check as eval "$check" < /dev/null (tools/platforms.py build-checks lists 7: pve9, pve92, ubuntu2404, rhel9, ubuntu2604, debian13, debian12). Verify on the candidate: its release:packages step's log must hold one '=== MeshXFS <version> — platform build check: ...' line for each of the 7, against the earlier releases' package logs (one line each, the defect); then remove --fixed.
defects.impact_why: A release-tooling fault: it decides which compile checks run before the packages are built, and touches neither the module, the packages nor a node; every released platform's claimed kernels still get a DKMS compile of the built package in that platform's packaged round (tests/packaged_round.sh install step, and on pve* a DKMS build for every kernel in /lib/modules).

defects.summary: GitHub issue #3 (same tester, Proxmox VE 9 + DRBD, followed docs/drbd-setup.md): proxmox02 down and back fine; then proxmox01 was shut down and proxmox02's shared storage stopped working. The log is proxmox02 booting with proxmox01 unreachable: the fence handler refuses to promote a Consistent (not UpToDate) disk while the peer is unreachable, so every Proxmox mount attempt fails until proxmox01 returns. The design (section 7, 'pve2 restarts while pve1 is down') waits for pve1 with no fence configured, but the user sees a hung storage, and the site has IPMI fencing that could have let the survivor fence and carry on.
defects.evidence: https://github.com/sshoecraft/meshxfs/issues/3 (opened 2026-10-20T20:39Z): proxmox02 boot 17:35:35; mxfs-drbd-fence 'refusing to promote this node (proxmox02) while proxmox01 is unreachable ... (this disk is Consistent)' repeated 17:35:47-52, 'drbdsetup-84 primary 0 terminated with exit code 17', 'State change failed: (-2) Need access to UpToDate data', pvestatd/pvedaemon 'mount error' every 10 s from 17:35:44; storage plugin 'older storage API' notice (0.90.130 plugin). Why proxmox02 rebooted is not in the report (user shutdown, HA watchdog on quorum loss, or Pacemaker stonith). MEASURED 2026-10-21 on the nested Proxmox VE 9.1 DRBD pair (pve9-3 .211 participant 0, pve9-4 .212), 0.90.132 build C909CF9904720C152222EEB: (1) supported setup, tests/pve_pair_failover.sh p0-poweroff (evidence tests/evidence/pve_pair_failover/20261021T030744Z-192.168.120.211): participant 0 systemctl poweroff, off in 18 s; participant 1 carried on 60 s, same boot, mounted, UpToDate/Outdated, no fence handler, load err=0 over 4.7M I/Os; participant 0 remounted 33 s after answering; all fsynced sets intact. (2) Pacemaker 3.0.0 promoting DRBD on both (promotable ocf:linbit:drbd, promoted-max=2, stonith-enabled=false, no-quorum-policy=ignore), pre-fix boot program, tests/pve_pacemaker_promoter.sh (evidence tests/evidence/pve_pacemaker_promoter/20261021T031427Z): at participant 0's poweroff Pacemaker's demote failed 03:24:46-03:24:50 'State change failed: (-12) Device is held open by someone' (MXFS still mounted; p_drbd_demote_0 'Error occurred' recorded) until mxfs-drbd@mxfs unmounted at 03:24:50; with stonith off nothing escalated and participant 1 neither ran a fence handler nor restarted (RESULT: OBSERVED p1_restarted=0). Not measured: the tester's stonith (fence_ipmilan) enabled, under which Pacemaker fences a node whose stop fails; a fenced participant 0 is a lost link that participant 1 loses on the tie-break and restarts for.
defects.next: Established from the issue's own log: an outside promoter ran on proxmox02 at boot -- 'drbd[1526]: Command drbdsetup-84 primary 0 terminated with exit code 17' at 17:35:47, 12 s after boot, on a disconnected Secondary; MeshXFS's boot program never promotes a disconnected node without an exclusion (cmd_boot waits Connected/UpToDate first). The tester then said (2026-10-21T02:40Z) they normally run Pacemaker+DRBD+stonith. Owner's call 2026-10-21: Pacemaker-managed DRBD is not slated for 0.90.132. Still unknown: why proxmox02 restarted (asked: journalctl -b -1 from proxmox02, proxmox01's shutdown log). Measure the supported setup's version of the trigger: tests/pve_pair_failover.sh p0-poweroff on the nested DRBD pair (participant 0 shut down on purpose; participant 1 must carry on, no fence, no restart). Participant 1 restarting while participant 0 is down waits by design under agent=self; authority=quorum takes over (quorum-test, D-DRBD-PAIR-NO-EXTERNAL-QUORUM-SO-P1-CANNOT-TAKE-OVER-WHEN-P0-DIES). With the 0.90.132 boot program the outside-promoter setup is refused at start (promoter-test).
defects.impact_why: Owner's scoping call 2026-10-21, restated: 2/net/mesh/drbd is part of 0.90.132, and GitHub #3's cluster runs DRBD under Pacemaker/corosync (the tester's own account, 2026-10-21T02:40Z; an outside promoter ran drbdsetup primary 12 s after boot in the issue's log), which docs/drbd-setup.md does not support and 0.90.132 does not claim. On the documented setup (mxfs-drbd@ only, drbd.service disabled, no Pacemaker), the trigger was measured on the 0.90.132 build C909CF9904720C152222EEB: participant 0 powered off, participant 1 carried on mounted with no fence and no restart, load err=0 over 4.7M I/Os, all fsynced sets intact (tests/evidence/pve_pair_failover/20261021T030744Z-192.168.120.211). This scopes the release; it disposes of nothing, and the record stays open until the tester's restart cause is known.

defects.summary: A mount inside the bootstrap's heartbeat-table scan (dlm/bootstrap.c reads the table twice a 62 s dead window apart) checks no signal, so SIGKILL to the mounting process takes effect only when the scan ends and the next wait that polls fatal_signal_pending (v5_mount.c) sees it. A unit stop or an operator's kill of a mount in that window waits up to ~64 s.
defects.evidence: scripts/drbd_rig.sh promoter-test manual with PROMOTER_CONTROL (lapq drbdprom6 lap 3, 2026-10-21, module C17A8788E8DA81D7CA5C333, test2): 'systemctl kill --signal=KILL mxfs-rig-boot' -> 'control boot program on test2 ended: failed ended_after=43s'. Earlier lap drbdprom2 lap 2: still 'deactivating' 15 s after SIGKILL. grep: fatal_signal_pending appears only at dlm/v5_mount.c:6700, 7809, 12555; none in dlm/bootstrap.c.
defects.next: Locate the scan's waits (mxfs_pal_sleep_ms in the bootstrap peek/scan) and make them return -EINTR on mxfs_pal_fatal_signal_pending, as v5_drbd_startup_fence does; measure the kill-to-exit time on the same lap (target: one poll interval, 2 s).
defects.impact_why: A killed mount returns once the scan's window ends (43 s measured); no data change, no crash, no host hang: the delay is bounded by the 62 s dead window.

defects.summary: GitHub issue #2: the tester's SyncTarget logged 'ASSERTION __dec_unacked(device) >= 0 FAILED in e_end_resync_block' throughout a resync (DRBD 8.4.11 in-kernel driver, Proxmox VE 9). The reply on the issue said whether MeshXFS triggers it would be checked; nothing had checked it.
defects.evidence: https://github.com/sshoecraft/meshxfs/issues/2 dmesg 14:07:13-14:07:25: 'Feature flags enabled on protocol level: 0xf TRIM THIN_RESYNC WRITE_SAME WRITE_ZEROES', 'Began resync as SyncTarget (will sync 4050944 KB)', the assertion repeated from 14:07:13, before this node's MXFS mount (14:07:18). Source read /src/linux/drivers/block/drbd/drbd_receiver.c: receive_rs_deallocated() (P_RS_DEALLOCATED, the thin-resync reply sent by the SyncSource for an all-zero block requested with P_RS_THIN_REQ, drbd_worker.c:1120) submits the discard at line 4799 and only then calls inc_unacked() at 4812, while its completion e_end_resync_block() calls dec_unacked() at 1866 from the ack sender; recv_resync_read() increments first (1883). P_RS_THIN_REQ is sent only when the disk's rs_discard_granularity is non-zero (drbd_worker.c:619/737). tests/evidence holds no occurrence of the assertion on this project's DRBD rigs, whose resource files set no rs-discard-granularity.
defects.next: Hypothesis: the assertion is DRBD's own counter race on the thin-resync path, needing rs-discard-granularity on the resource, and MeshXFS takes no part in it. Falsify on the DRBD rig (scripts/drbd_rig.sh) with mxfs.ko not loaded: set rs-discard-granularity on both nodes, zero a region on the SyncSource, force a resync (invalidate the target), and look for the assertion; then the same without rs-discard-granularity. Assertion with no MXFS module and only with the setting = DISPROVED as an MXFS defect. Ask the tester for 'drbdadm dump' to confirm the setting.
defects.impact_why: What the evidence shows is a DRBD driver log line during resync: the tester's pair finished the resync (14:08:06 resync done), both disks went UpToDate/UpToDate, and nothing in the log ties a lost write, a crash, a hang or a shutdown to it. It appears on the thin-resync path (rs-discard-granularity), which docs/drbd-setup.md and every rig resource file leave unset.
