defects.evidence: tests/evidence/drbd_rig/criteria.runs.jsonl: fio_perf FAIL 2026-10-13T16:52:16Z 'test1:BUDGET_EXHAUSTED:step=unknown report_s=115 elapsed_s=116 test2:BUDGET_EXHAUSTED'; then cache_coherency 16:52:33Z, strong_consistency 16:52:46Z, posix_multi 16:52:55Z, mmap_coherency 16:53:04Z, zero_silent_loss 16:53:13Z, dlm_fairness 16:53:22Z, dlm_membership 16:53:32Z, scaling_curve 16:54:03Z, dlm_scaling 17:03:54Z, rsync_paired 17:13:44Z, each status BLOCKED, outcome INFRA, reason 'NODE FAULT (not a filesystem verdict): test2:sync-wedged[no-diag]' (run.sh:1786 builds the tag; [no-diag] means no stack or {sub} classification was captured). The migrated lines carry no build, run id or evidence path. crash_consistency FAIL 17:23:57Z the same day ('the cluster did not reconverge to 2 members within 130s') is another unnamed incident on that board.
defects.next: Locate the run's evidence by time (tests/evidence/drbd_rig/20261013T16*, the DRBD verify .out of that day, netconsole.log and the nodes' kernel logs around 16:50-16:55Z) and establish where test2's sync was blocked: an MXFS writeback or log wait, DRBD (flush/ack), or the node's own root disk. Until then this blocks every release by default. ===== ===== 2026-10-24 (session 56): the run is 20261013T164854Z-g2 (tests/evidence/drbd_rig/20261013T164852Z-suite/suite.log:34-64, drbd_release_verify_0.90.128.out:69-161, run_fio_perf_20261013T164854Z-g2/). test2 was not wedged in sync: test1's node fence powered it off. test1's kernel log (run_fio_perf_20261013T164854Z-g2/kernlog_test1.gz, zcat line numbers): from 16:50:22 its lock requests to test2 as master timed out (:5662 'P-LKTIMEOUT-REMOTE type=1 ino=8388737 ag=0 master=1218516688 req=EX', :5664 P36-STACK fio in mxfs_dlm_open_protect; :5754-5780 the log worker's mxfs_sb_summary_lock), then :7215 '[16:50:38] drbd mxfs: PingAck did not arrive in time', :7216 'peer( Primary -> Unknown ) conn( Connected -> NetworkFailure ) ... susp( 0 -> 1 )', :7228 fence-peer, :7265 'fence-peer helper returned 7 (peer was stonithed)', :9092 P238-DRBD-FENCE-WITNESSED ... authority=shut off kind=25, :9236 '[16:50:46] P163-RECOVERY-COMPLETE slot=1 node=1218516688'. Every later ssh to test2 found 'No route to host' (test2.ccph:1, kernlog_test2.gz:1), which run.sh's pre-assert probe recorded as 'sync-wedged[no-diag]' (suite.log:42-61); the rig's node fence ran with delay test1 0 s, test2 10 s (drbd_release_verify_0.90.128.out:19). test1 also logged P-HB-SLOW write_ms=6445 (:7234) and P-DRBD-IOQ-STATS wait_max_ms=6410 (:8029); the host sampler hostdisk_2-net-mesh-drbd_fio_perf_20261013T164959Z_g2.txt and suite.log:39 show nvme0n1p2 wms_p95=205.3 ms, hostload 6.79. No kernel log of test2 exists for the window (netconsole.log carries no line attributable to it: its unique strings, the new UUID F0B07A42FCAF1D83 and episode 5d75aacc, appear nowhere). So the record is now: test2 stopped answering its peer (lock masters from 16:50:22, DRBD's ping 16 s later) under fio_perf on a loaded host, and was fenced; why it stopped is not known. Next: reproduce 2/net/mesh/drbd fio_perf with test2's kernel log streamed off the node (netconsole with a per-sender port, or a serial console file) and both nodes' DRBD ping and MXFS heartbeat timing kept, and read what test2 was doing from 16 s before the fence. ===== ===== 2026-10-24: located. Run 20261013T164854Z-g2 (tests/evidence/drbd_rig/20261013T164852Z-suite/suite.log:34-64; tests/evidence/run_fio_perf_20261013T164854Z-g2/). test2 was STONITHed at 16:50:41 by test1's DRBD fence-peer handler (kernlog_test1.gz: 7215 '[16:50:38] drbd mxfs: PingAck did not arrive in time.', 7228 'helper command: /sbin/drbdadm fence-peer mxfs', 7265 '[16:50:41] fence-peer helper returned 7 (peer was stonithed)', 8882 'P-DRBD-EXCL-DEATH node=1218516688 ... how=stonith'), so the sync-wedged[no-diag] tag of every row after fio_perf is run.sh's diag ssh (run.sh:1910, record's :1786) reaching a powered-off node, not a sync wedged in a live kernel. Before that, test1's lock requests mastered on test2 timed out from 16:50:22 (P-LKTIMEOUT-REMOTE master=1218516688, P36-STACK: fio in mxfs_dlm_open_protect, kworker xfs_log_worker in mxfs_sb_summary_lock), and the last message test1 received from test2 is at 16:50:03 (DLM_TRACE ... sender=1218516688). So test2 stopped answering its DLM and DRBD peers about 16:50:03-16:50:38 under fio_perf (host load 6.79, host disk wms_max 391.8 ms, suite.log:39). No kernel log of test2 exists for the window (kernlog_test2.gz holds only 'No route to host'); /var/log/libvirt/qemu/test2.log* (root-only) would give the domain's stop time. Next: read the libvirt log for test2 around 16:50Z, and reproduce fio_perf on the DRBD pair with test2's kernel log streamed off the node (netconsole) to see why it stopped answering. ===== ===== 2026-10-24: /var/log/libvirt/qemu/test2.log (read with sudo): '2026-10-13T16:50:40.198843Z qemu-system-x86_64: terminating on signal 15 from pid 468163 (/usr/sbin/libvirtd)', '2026-10-13 16:50:41.999+0000: shutting down, reason=destroyed'. The domain ran until the fence destroyed it, so test2 was a live guest that answered neither its DLM peer (silent from 16:50:03) nor DRBD's ping (16:50:38) for some 35 s; nothing records what it was doing. Next unchanged: reproduce with test2's kernel log streamed off the node.

defects.summary: tests/live_holder_wait.sh aborts before measuring when none of its eight candidate inodes is remote-mastered from test2; master locality is a hash re-decided at every cluster formation, so whether the lap can run depends on the formation it lands on, and the capture gate read it BROKEN
defects.evidence: capture gate, 0.90.134 dry run attempt 20261021T230333Z: GATE live_holder_wait fault: rc=2 fault_line=0 -> BROKEN, ABORT: none of the eight candidates is remote-mastered from test2 - this lap cannot measure the path it names. The same entry was OK in attempt 20261021T212712Z the same evening. ===== ===== 2026-10-22, cause: routing hash v2 clears an inode number's low three bits before hashing (include/mxfs/mxfs_tauth.h:505-507, MXFS_TAUTH_INO_SHARD 8), so mastership is per eight-inode shard and the lap's eight consecutive candidates (8389321-8389328 on attempt 20261021T230333Z, all local) were two draws. Fix in the tree: H creates objects until 16 distinct shards are represented (cap 160; spares kept until all exist, then removed), one candidate per shard, so on two nodes none remote is 2^-16 per lap; candidates removed at the end and on the no-match abort; setup bound 13 s from 0.9-1.2 s measured for 160 creates + removal + sync in each mode. Dry run attempt 20261022T031549Z gate: candidates in shards 1048640..1048643 (inodes 8389121, 8389128, 8389136, 8389144): three local, the fourth remote, target chosen remote at +35s, STAGE FAULT, ABORT, fault lap OK. The old eight (8389121-8389128) span only shards 1048640 and 1048641, both local on this formation: it would have aborted again. ===== ===== 2026-10-22 healthy lap through tests/capture_fault_gate.sh 0.90.134-harnessfix --healthy-only (tests/evidence/20261022T040204Z_capture_gate_0.90.134-harnessfix): GATE live_holder_wait healthy: rc=0 wall=268s fails=0 -> OK (bound 400 s). ===== 2026-10-23: tests/live_holder_wait.sh gained LH_SHARD_SELECT=0 (the control: eight candidates back to back, all kept) and LH_SETUP_ONLY=1 (stop after the candidates); the lap is tests/live_holder_shard_lap.sh. Precheck on g2b (test15/test16, 2/net/mesh/mpath, build B155E10D900872E6CE36289, lane tests/evidence/lanes/g2b_lhshard_precheck_20261023T072946Z): fix in, 16 candidates in 16 distinct shards twice (PASS); LH_SHARD_SELECT=0, 8 candidates in 2 and in 1 distinct shards (FAIL), e.g. inodes 8392896-8392903, one shard. ===== 2026-10-24 precheck on attempt 2026-10-24T06:38:23Z (lane tests/evidence/lanes/g2_w14_20261024T100229Z, 2/net/mesh/direct, test1/test2): control LH_SHARD_SELECT=0 lhpc2 FAIL exposed ('EXPOSED: the pre-fix harness's 8 candidates [8388736..8388743] were all measured mastered off H=test1 ... LAP lh_master FAIL: ABORT: none of the 8 candidates ... is remote-mastered from test2', tries=2); lhpc1 ABORT before measuring (its re-form prep was refused by the preflight's log-rate check during another lane's power-up, D-LANE-POWER-UP-FLOODS-THE-HOST-LOG-AND-ANOTHER-LANES-PREFLIGHT-REFUSES-ITS-PREP). Fix on (LH_SHARD_SELECT=1): lhpf1 PASS exposed (tries=1, target ino=8388736 master=remote), lhpf2 PASS exposed (tries=3, ino=16777352 master=remote).
defects.next: Control batch of tests/live_holder_shard_lap.sh with LH_SHARD_SELECT=0 (tools/harness_batch.py control --knob, 10 laps, bound 50 s, probe '^EXPOSED: candidates='), then the verification batch on the frozen candidate sized from it, then remove --fixed. The removal may retire 1/any:release:presteps:2026-10-21T23:22:19Z only with that run's own log line showing this abort (GATE live_holder_wait fault: ... ABORT: none of the eight candidates is remote-mastered). ===== Removal P20261023-b3dddc was rejected (data/reviews/P20261023-b3dddc.md): (1) the shard-to-master cause was read from the routing code, not measured; the failing run (live_holder_wait_fault.log:5-12, all eight candidates mastered by W across two shards) fits a formation where W masters everything as well; (2) the cause text has the node backwards: the harness aborts when the draws land on W (tests/live_holder_wait.sh:402-403, 'master=local (P7S-BAST-FIRE test1=0 test2=1)' with W=test2), not on H; (3) neither batch could discriminate: all 16 laps ran LH_SETUP_ONLY=1, which exits at :371-374 before the master probe at :381, and the lap's shard arithmetic int($3/8) and the fix's ino>>3 are both hard-coded, so the control reproduced the lap's own arithmetic, not the abort; (4) only two nodes are covered while the record reaches every configuration (on N nodes the fixed harness still aborts with probability (1-1/N)^16 by the proposal's own model: 0.118 at 8, 0.60 at 32). Approvable: a measured link from shard to master (several inodes in each of two or more adjacent shards on formations where their masters differ, or chk_mxfs -v plus tests/tauth/pageof.c predicting each probed master), the cause naming W, a verification resting on that measurement through the master probe (not setup-only), and evidence beyond two nodes. ===== ===== 2026-10-23: the rework answering the rejection of P20261023-b3dddc is in the sibling tree /home/steve/src/mxfs-a15 (tests/live_holder_wait.sh: NSHARD sized from the member count, ceil(16 ln 2 / -ln(1-1/N)), every member probed and a third member's shard named, LH_PROBE_ONLY=1 runs the real selection and master probe and also probes objects 1-8 the pre-fix harness made; tests/live_holder_shard_lap.sh: a fresh prep_cluster every lap, EXPOSED only when all eight old objects are MEASURED mastered off H, PASS/FAIL from the harness's own selection, the shard model recorded as evidence). Rig precheck from the sibling tree on g2b (test15/test16, 2/net/mesh/direct, module 79779BEAECBEA94844FDC72), evidence /home/steve/src/mxfs-a15/tests/evidence/20261023T21*_lhmaster_pre_*: fix in, 3 of 3 PASS, one exposed (pre_on2: the eight 8388736-8388743 all W's, candidate idx=17 ino 8388752 in shard 1048594 H's, SHARD-BOUNDARY 1048593 (test16) | 1048594 (test15), disagreeing=0); LH_SHARD_SELECT=0: pre_off1 EXPOSED and FAIL (the eight all W's, harness ABORT none remote-mastered), pre_off2 not exposed and PASS, pre_off3 ABORT (its prep_cluster overran 88 s; recorded separately). Exposure is one formation in two on two members, as the shard model predicts. Next, on the next frozen attempt: control (LH_SHARD_SELECT=0, laps until 10 exposed) and verification sized from it at 2/net/mesh/direct, then a 4-member formation (LHW_HOLD) for the reach beyond two nodes. ===== 2026-10-24: the control's settled lap cannot be replaced (check_batch_lap counts it against the plan) and measure refuses it at 9 of 10: D-MEASURE-REFUSES-A-BATCH-WHOSE-SETTLED-LAP-CHECK-BATCH-LAP-COUNTED-AS-RUN. With that fix on the next attempt the control closes at 9 of 9 exposed FAILs (precheck in a scratch tree) and the verification needs 7 clean laps; measure it then, not by adding a lap.

defects.summary: tools/lun_pool.sh binds a node by logging it in by hand (iscsiadm -o new, --login); on a node whose boot found no iSCSI node record open-iscsi.service is inactive, so nothing logs the pool session out before systemd stops the network at shutdown, and the node can hang past scripts/lab_power.sh's 90 s bound and be destroyed, as the 4K-native LUN's nodes did
defects.evidence: Mechanism measured with the same hand login on the 4K-native LUN (tests/fourkn_lun.sh), test31/test32: tests/evidence/20261022T150025Z_fourkn_shutdown_bare (after a merge lap) and 20261022T150432Z_fourkn_shutdown_bare (mxfs never loaded), both nodes HUNG: network down with the session up, lvm2-monitor's vgchange --monitor n opened the LUN for its label scan and its read was never answered (iSCSI ping timeout 9 s later, 120 s replacement timeout); starting open-iscsi.service after the login (20261022T154826Z_fourkn_shutdown_bare) logged the session out before the network and both nodes were off in 2 s. tools/lun_pool.sh:297-302 (single path) and :359-363 (multipath) delete every node record and log in by hand with node.startup=automatic, so a node is exposed until its next boot: a freshly built VM, or one whose records another tool removed (tests/fourkn_lun.sh's login deletes them all), in the boot of its first bind. Not yet observed on a pool LUN: at 2026-10-22 14:23 UTC every pool VM shut down with its session logged out (host kernel log logout_exec for test1, test2, test15, test16). ===== 2026-10-24, attempt 17 (lane tests/evidence/lanes/g2e_a17lp_20261024T103926Z, test17/test18, LP_BIND=paths2 LUN_POOL_ISCSI_UNIT=0, the fix out). Steps 2-5: four laps exposed (recordless boot, unit inactive, mpatha on two paths), and every one PASSed, both nodes off within the bound. Step 6 overran the lane's 108 s bound before its shutdown: the alloc --paths 2 bind had not returned when timeout killed the lap at 10:45:59. The bind outlived the lap and logged both nodes in at 10:46:13 (node journals). The pair, left up with the unit inactive and two sessions, was then powered off by hand at 10:51:4x and both were off in 5-7 s (lab_power.sh: test18 off after 5 s, test17 after 7 s). That is 5 of 5 clean unfixed multipath shutdowns this attempt. The journal capture (tests/node_journal_follow.sh, tests/evidence/20261024T1045Z_lunpool_mpath_journal) cannot answer what logs the multipath sessions out: the nodes keep a volatile journal, and the ssh stream ends when the network stops, so no shutdown sequence was recorded (nothing between test17's bind at 10:40:21 and its next boot at 10:40:45). Next: capture the shutdown on the node's serial console, or with a persistent journal read back with journalctl -b -1 on the next boot. A lap that overruns in its bind is a bind-time overrun, not a shutdown one, and the lap should say so (an ABORT naming the step, not the bound).
defects.next: Start open-iscsi.service after the bind's login in both lun_pool.sh paths and require it active, as tests/fourkn_lun.sh now does; verify with tests/fourkn_lun_shutdown_probe.sh on a pool LUN bound to nodes booted with no node record: unfixed both nodes hang, fixed both off in seconds. ===== 2026-10-22: the fix is in tools/lun_pool.sh (ISCSI_UNIT starts the unit after every bind; alloc refuses a bind whose unit is not active); fix diff tests/evidence/controls/D-LUN-POOL-HAND-LOGIN-AFTER-A-RECORDLESS-BOOT.fix.diff. Precheck OK on test15/test16 (fix in: both off in seconds; fix out: both destroyed at the 90 s bound). Control (10 laps) running in lane tests/evidence/lanes/g2b_lunpool_control_20261022T233620Z. Next: read its result; the verification batch on the candidate; remove --fixed. ===== Removal P20261022-f1425f was rejected (data/reviews/P20261022-f1425f.md): every lap of tests/lun_pool_shutdown_lap.sh binds with a plain alloc, so only the single-path login (tools/lun_pool.sh:338) was exercised, while the fix also changed the --also login (:357) and the multipath login (:421) that every */*/mpath configuration uses (run.sh:439). Needed: a --paths 2 form of the lap at an mpath configuration (2/net/mesh/mpath) and an --also form, each with a control (fix reverted) and a fix-on batch sized from it, on the candidate's source; the resubmission must also cite the chain's own evidence (tests/evidence/20261022T15*_fourkn_shutdown_bare). ===== 2026-10-24 (session 65): on attempt 2026-10-24T04:13:43Z the --paths 2 form at 2/net/mesh/mpath barely reproduces with the fix out: control b20261024-8fa209 (LUN_POOL_ISCSI_UNIT=0) failed 2 of 10 laps, one of them an overrun of the lap's 108 s bound (tests/evidence/lanes/g2b_a15_lunpool_20261024T042701Z/step3.log), a counted rate of 1 in 9, from which tools/harness_batch.py sized verification b20261024-6ed27f at 9514 laps. That batch cannot be run (about 6 days of laps); it was stopped after its eighth lap by ending the harness_batch process (the lap in flight left to finish), and it stays open, unapplied. The 2/disk/caw/direct pair (control b20261023-a1d925 10 of 10, verification b20261023-ce91a4 6 of 6 PASS, tests/evidence/lanes/g2b_a15_lunpool_20261024T042701Z/step1.log, step2.log) covers the plain single-path login. Next for the multipath login: read the two failing control laps' logs for what failed (the shutdown wait or something else), and establish whether the multipath login's sessions are logged out at shutdown by another unit (multipathd or iscsid's own node records) even without the fix, which would make the precondition absent there and the reach a reviewed narrowing rather than a verification.

defects.summary: On a DRBD pair with the default fence (agent=self with the fixed tie-break: no QDevice and no node fence configured), only participant 0 (the lower DRBD address) may carry on after a lost link. When participant 0 dies, participant 1 cannot tell that from a cut link, so it freezes, restarts and stays out until participant 0 returns: the pair survives the death of participant 1 but not of participant 0. Required (owner, 2026-10-22): in a 2-node cluster either node survives the other's death.
defects.evidence: Outside report, Proxmox forum thread 187097 post 873810 (2026-10-22), two VMs on virt-manager with vbmc as IPMI: 'If the node 02 dies, the node 01 remains, but not the other way around.' The owner's answer the same day: 'if you have a 2 node and 02 dies 01 should remain AND if 01 dies 02 should remain - if it doesn't thats a problem.' The behaviour is the documented default: docs/drbd-setup.md section 7 ('pve1 dies. pve2 cannot tell a dead pve1 from a cut cable, so it does not take over. It freezes, logs exactly this, restarts, and waits.') and docs/rulings/drbd-two-node-self-exclusion.md 'What it does not cover: Participant 0 dying'. tools/mxfs_drbd_fence_peer.sh:37-47: no config means agent=self; authority=quorum (a corosync QDevice) lets either participant win (removed D-DRBD-PAIR-NO-EXTERNAL-QUORUM-SO-P1-CANNOT-TAKE-OVER-WHEN-P0-DIES, 0.90.128, verified only with a QDevice); agent=exec/ssh needs a program that speaks the handler's fence verbs, and no IPMI adapter ships, so a site with IPMI (iLO, iDRAC, vbmc) gets the default. The release's DRBD failure tests (tests/drbd_release_verify.sh death-test) destroy only node 2, participant 1.
defects.next: The owner's planned work after 0.90.134: a node fence over IPMI (and Pacemaker), so a pair with a BMC fences whichever node died. On the rig, virtualbmc in front of the libvirt VMs gives each test node an IPMI BMC, so fence_ipmilan can be exercised without iLO or iDRAC hardware. Then a death test that destroys participant 0, on a pair with that fence and on one with authority=quorum, beside the existing destroy of participant 1. ===== No exception stands (P20261022-3473e9 rejected), and tools/release_run.py step_drbd runs tests/drbd_release_verify.sh and grades the DRBD board on every release whatever the table claims, so the DRBD work cannot wait for 0.90.135. No design lets participant 1 tell participant 0's death from a cut link without a third vote or a node fence (docs/rulings/drbd-two-node-self-exclusion.md, 'What established systems do'), so the defect can only be closed by never running that configuration: the DRBD attachment refuses to mount a dual-primary pair whose /etc/mxfs/drbd-fence.conf has neither authority=quorum nor a node-fence agent (agent=exec or agent=ssh), naming both remedies, so every pair that runs survives the death of either node. Verify on the DRBD rig: control with the refusal's switch off on a default pair (destroy participant 0, participant 1 restarts and stays out), fix on (the default pair refuses to mount; a pair with authority=quorum against the corosync-qnetd on serv survives the destroy of participant 0 and of participant 1). ===== ===== 2026-10-24 (session 56): fix built in the sibling tree /home/steve/src/mxfs-a15 for the next attempt (module B8EC569481B988532A1BDBF): the witness reports FENCE_AGENT and FENCE_AUTHORITY (tools/mxfs_drbd_witness.py), the report carries them (pal/pal.h fence_agent, fence_authority; pal/linux/drbd.c), and v5_drbd_arm (dlm/v5_mount.c) adds mxfs_drbd_judge_third_vote (dlm/drbdfence.c): a pair whose drbd-fence.conf is absent or agent=self without authority=quorum is refused with P-DRBD-ARM-REFUSED '... no third vote and no node fence (agent=self, authority=none): participant 1 could never outlive participant 0; set authority=quorum (a corosync QDevice) or agent=exec|ssh in /etc/mxfs/drbd-fence.conf'. drbd_third_vote=0 (dlm/v5_mount.c) admits it as before: the same-build control. scripts/drbd_rig.sh: its tie-break tests load drbd_third_vote=0 (TIEBREAK_MODARGS, set by install_self_authority, cleared by install_fencing and install_quorum_authority), NODE_REPO follows the tree's directory name as run.sh's does, and a new subcommand third-vote-test <1|0>. Docs: docs/drbd-setup.md section 7 and decision 12 of docs/rulings/drbd-two-node-self-exclusion.md (both in the sibling). Lap tests/drbd_third_vote_lap.sh <label> (g2, ARM=1|0): down, up, mxfs, third-vote-test, down; EXPOSED when the agent=self-alone pair asks to mount on both nodes; ARM=1 PASS when both mounts are refused naming the missing third vote; ARM=0 FAIL when participant 1 has not recovered participant 0's slice 74 s after participant 0 is destroyed (the defect). Next: a precheck of each arm on g2 from the sibling; on the next attempt a control batch with ARM=0, a verification sized from it, and remove --fixed; the quorum pair's survival of participant 0's death is scripts/drbd_rig.sh quorum-test death (the 0.90.128 removal of D-DRBD-PAIR-NO-EXTERNAL-QUORUM-SO-P1-CANNOT-TAKE-OVER-WHEN-P0-DIES), to run once on the candidate as support. At publish, README.md's DRBD section (now 'no third machine and no fence hardware', 'Fencing is on by default with no configuration') must say the pair needs a QDevice or a node fence. ===== 2026-10-24 (session 65): control b20261024-795358 (lap:third_vote at 2/net/mesh/drbd, ARM=0, candidate 0.90.134 attempt 2026-10-24T04:13:43Z, module B947A20F3C2FE3A67ABF6F3) failed laps 1-8 with the fix out, every one exposed: 'participant 1 (test1) did not carry on after participant 0's death: no recovery' (tests/evidence/lanes/g2_a15_20261024T041432Z/step6.log). Lap 9 (started 2026-10-24T05:47:47Z) is NOT a lap of that build: the session rebuilt the tree's mxfs.ko for about two minutes (srcversion 3E3690F75295961510B9DC7, a source edit for the next attempt) and the lap's drbd_rig.sh loaded it on test1 and test2 (read back from /sys/module/mxfs/srcversion at 05:50Z); the frozen build was restored byte for byte at 05:50:14Z. Its run must not be counted in this control's rate. The lane was stopped after lap 9 (control never closed; its verification never declared). Next, on the next attempt: a fresh control and verification on that attempt's module.

defects.summary: On the 2/net/mesh/direct4k board (build 9594B08726D6732D2ED5E87, test1/test2 on a 4096-byte pool LUN), the pre-row sync check before dlm_membership found test2 unable to finish 'timeout 12 sync' within 12 s; the follow-up D-state read found no blocked mxfs/writeback task, so the row recorded BLOCKED/INCOMPLETE node-fault test2:sync-wedged[no-diag]. Why test2's sync took more than 12 s is not known.
defects.evidence: Ledger data/criteria.runs.jsonl:7548, 2/net/mesh/direct4k:dlm_membership:2026-10-22T19:43:42Z INCOMPLETE run 20261022T193055Z-g2 (no evidence directory: run.sh records the node fault before the row runs; run.sh:1763-1806). test2's kernel log (tests/evidence/run_dlm_scaling_20261022T193055Z-g2/kernlog_test2.gz, boot 19:31:14 to 19:49:46): no hung_task, BUG, Oops, WARNING, 'blocked for more than' or 'Shutting down' in 19:35-19:50; at 19:42:12 P-LKTIMEOUT-REMOTE type=1 ino=180355073 ag=0 req=EX then P36-RETRY retries_left=59 and P36-STACK from xfs_log_worker -> mxfs_sb_summary_lock -> mxfs_v5_dlm_inode_lock -> dlm_lock_retries_impl (the superblock summary lock), granted the same second (P74-GRANT gen=843); the next grant of ino=180355073 is at 19:43:43 (gen=1126) with P-SB-WRITE-SUBMIT and P-SB-RUNTIME-COVER, one second after the sync check gave up; no kernel line 19:43:44-19:44:04. Every other row of that board run before and after passed (dlm_fairness 19:43:25, scaling_curve, dlm_scaling, rsync_paired, fourkn_cdb, fourkn_merge, fourkn_lbs_refusal, node_responsive, kernel_health, sustained_load...). ===== 2026-10-22: run.sh's pre-row sync check now reads, for a sync still running at 11 s, its own stack and wait channel and every D-state task's (SYNCSTACK lines in the node-fault reason). Lane tests/evidence/lanes/g2d_tcp4k_sync_probe_20261022T233927Z (test31/test32, 4096-byte pool LUN, build 9594B08726D6732D2ED5E87): dlm_fairness and dlm_membership five times, all 10 rows PASS, 20 pre-row sync checks completed: not reproduced, and not a rate. ===== 2026-10-24 rate measurement on attempt 2026-10-24T06:38:23Z (lane tests/evidence/lanes/g2d_w14b_20261024T101343Z, 2/net/mesh/direct4k on g2d test31/test32, one forced prep, then dlm_fairness and dlm_membership alternating five rounds each): 10 of 10 rows PASS (dlm_fairness 2-3 s, dlm_membership 4-7 s, against 30 s budgets); no row's pre-row sync reached run.sh's 12 s bound (no 'sync-wedged' line in step3.log-step12.log). 0 of 10 at this configuration, which disposes of nothing: the original refusal is unexplained.
defects.next: Establish what test2's sync waited on: rerun 2/net/mesh/direct4k dlm_membership (and the rows before it, dlm_fairness) with a sysrq-w / /proc/<pid>/stack capture of the sync task itself taken inside the 12 s bound (run.sh's diag reads only after the bound, and only D-state tasks of named comms), and read whether sync_fs waits on the superblock summary lock's EX acquisition from the peer. Measure how often the pre-row sync exceeds 12 s on this configuration and on 2/net/mesh/direct (512) before narrowing anything.

defects.summary: A node whose filesystem has shut down and whose PR key is gone (self-fenced) keeps its mount and its authority-ledger publisher, which retries every page it holds against RESERVATION CONFLICT about 100 times a second without end (P-TAUTH-PUBLISH-FAIL rc=-52, then P-TAUTH-RECONCILE, per page), so a fenced node hammers the shared LUN and floods the target's log until it is powered off.
defects.evidence: test21 on 8/net/mesh/mpath, build 9594B08726D6732D2ED5E87, after D-8NETMESH-SURVIVOR-SHUTDOWN-FALSE-FRESH-AG-GRANT-AFTER-TAKEOVER shut its filesystem down at 19:56:11 (ledger run 8/net/mesh/mpath:path_peer_withdrawn:2026-10-22T19:58:42Z). Its kernel log (tests/evidence/flood_test21_20261022T200054Z/test21_kernlog_boot.gz, decompressed lines): 819084-819089 (19:56:14) P305-RESV-HEALTH state=SELF_GONE, P277-PR-FULLSTATUS own key ABSENT, P277-FENCED-SELF-WITHDRAW, P131-SELF-FENCE [PR_CONFLICT_FENCED]; 823160-823163 (19:56:32) P-PR-OWNKEY-GONE, P-PR-SELFFENCE, P131-SELF-FENCE [PR_KEY_PREEMPTED]; first 'P-TAUTH-PUBLISH-FAIL page=182 copy=0 seq=47 rc=-52 -- uncertain' at 819197 (19:56:19), last at 914587 (20:01:55, the log's end): 31,510 of them, every one rc=-52, over 85 distinct pages, each followed by P-TAUTH-RECONCILE; per minute 4070, 5149, 4790, 5949, 5984, 5568 (19:56-20:01), each matched by an 'sd 4:0:0:0: reservation conflict' line; 530 P-TAUTH-FROZEN-NOT-CONSUMED rc=-5 in the same span. test21's state at 20:00:55 (tests/evidence/flood_test21_20261022T200054Z/test21_state.txt): /dev/mapper/mpatha still mounted on /mnt/shared, both paths active. On the lab host the target logged ~100 'Reservation conflict (dev mxfspool04, initiator test21)' lines a second (6,031 in the minute to 20:00:44, all test21), and mxfs-clyde-guard halted the rig on FLOOD at 19:57:21 (.rig_halt, snapshot /src/mxfs/.evidence/guard_20261022_195717_34475: 400 of 400 lines that conflict). The flood stopped when test21 was destroyed at ~20:01:00 (0 conflicts in the next 5 s). ===== 2026-10-23 (session 49): 8/net/mesh/mpath path_peer_withdrawn twice on candidate 0.90.134's module C54C14B681D148267D084FC as variants (MXFS_TEST_ENV=PF_KEEP_KMSG=1, default window and path settings; lane tests/evidence/lanes/g8_a13_peerwithdrawn_kmsg_20261023T192856Z): both PASS, 'victim=test14 recovered_two_paths_s=8 recovered_one_path_s=9 reinstate_s=21 survivor_stall_two_ms=9687 survivor_stall_one_ms=9065 ... fails=0 max_stall_ms=10439' (tests/evidence/board_20261023T193036Z-g8_path_peer_withdrawn/row.log) and 'recovered_two_paths_s=9 recovered_one_path_s=10 reinstate_s=18 survivor_stall_two_ms=6202 survivor_stall_one_ms=7154 ... max_stall_ms=7535' (board_20261023T193518Z-g8_path_peer_withdrawn/row.log), every node's whole kernel log kept (kmsg_<node>_fromnode.gz). Two passes dispose of nothing; they say the row alone does not reach this record's trigger on this module, so its rig lap has to force it. ===== 2026-10-24 (session 79): a real-target rig lap, drafted and held (tests/evidence/drafts/held/tests/fenced_ledger_rig_lap.sh: prep, both nodes on pathload, V's dl_auth_closed_park set at run time, then V's authority closed by P's plain PREEMPT of V's key or by V's heartbeat paused 45 s; 40 s of P's load), prechecked at 2/net/mesh/direct on g2e (V=test17, P=test18, attempt-18 module 8DBA16AEB7FDD3066C9C1BC). All four arms VACUOUS stage=no-request: V logged P290-AUTH-CLOSED (PR_CONFLICT_FENCED after preempt, AUTHORITY_LEASE_EXPIRED after the pause) and withdrew, and nothing reached its ledger afterwards (P-TAUTH-PUBLISH-FAIL, -FROZEN-NOT-CONSUMED, -PAGE-AUTH-CLOSED, -HANDOFF-AUTH-CLOSED all 0 after the closure; preempt PARK=1 had 6 refused publishes 0.9 s BEFORE it). Host conflicts from V: 7 and 184 (preempt, PARK=1 and 0), 0 and 0 (pause). P's side (test18_kmsg.txt): after the preempt P declared V dead only on heartbeat expiry ~11 s later, fenced it by a witnessed LU reset, replayed its slice and completed recovery (P163-RECOVERY-COMPLETE total=303/352 ms); after the pause P saw P163-WITHDRAW-SEEN and fenced by PREEMPT AND ABORT. P's longest operation 18530/20896 ms (preempt), 10602/10962 ms (pause). P then logged 'heartbeat received from unknown node <V>' 51-59 times to the end. Evidence tests/evidence/20261024T141549Z_fledger_flp1, 20261024T141810Z_fledger_flp0, 20261024T142009Z_fledger_flh1, 20261024T142210Z_fledger_flh0 (stdout.txt in each). So at two nodes the only peer is the recoverer and stops routing to V once it declares it; the incident's peers kept routing to a withdrawn test21 for minutes (P-LEASE-WITHDRAWN-RENEWAL 'kept for mastership retention' is logged in every lap here too). ===== 2026-10-24 (session 80): the 8-node precheck of the held lap, f8p1 (8/net/mesh/direct, g8 = test7..test14, V=test7 P=test14, INJECT=preempt PARK=1, attempt-19 module A27A67A3E501890BE9985E0; tests/evidence/20261024T144431Z_fledger_f8p1/stdout.txt). V's authority closed at 639.60 s (test7_kmsg_full.gz P290-AUTH-CLOSED reason=PR_CONFLICT_FENCED). After it, on V: 0 P-TAUTH-PUBLISH-FAIL, 0 P-TAUTH-FROZEN-NOT-CONSUMED, 0 P-TAUTH-PAGE-AUTH-CLOSED, 0 P-TAUTH-HANDOFF-AUTH-CLOSED (0 in the whole boot), and the host logged 0 'Reservation conflict' from test7's initiator 14:47-14:52Z: as at 2 nodes, the lap is VACUOUS for this record. The survivors declared V dead 10-27 s after its closure (649-666 s on their clocks) and routed nothing to it. The lap itself overran its 400 s bound: after the fence could not prove exclusion, V's recovery was declared RECOVERY_BLOCKED and the survivors' queued operations stayed parked (filed as D-8NETMESH-RECOVERY-BLOCKED-LEAVES-QUEUED-SURVIVOR-ACQUIRES-PARKED-FOREVER). So neither 2 nor 8 nodes reaches the case this record describes with an out-of-band preempt; the original (test21, 8/net/mesh/mpath) kept its peers routing to it, which needs a closure the peers have not acted on. Next: find from the original evidence what kept its peers from declaring it dead (whether its heartbeat kept landing after its key was gone) and inject that instead.
defects.next: Find where the ledger publisher decides to retry an uncertain publish (dlm/ tauth publish and reconcile paths) and what it consults about the node's state: a shut-down, self-fenced mount must stop publishing (and stop every other write) once its key is gone, not retry each page forever. Reproduce on a 2-node TCP pair: shut a node's filesystem down while it holds ledger pages and preempt its key, then count its P-TAUTH-PUBLISH-FAIL lines and the target's conflicts per second. ===== Verify P20261023-6664ba (batch b20261023-c63530) was rejected (data/reviews/P20261023-6664ba.md): every lap was four simulated nodes in one process on the lab host, whose authority close is a stub flag and whose ledger file never refuses a write, so no lap could produce the RESERVATION CONFLICT retry loop (0 P-TAUTH-PUBLISH-FAIL lines in any control or verify log). Needed: board-row laps at 8/net/mesh/mpath on the candidate's module where a node's filesystem shuts down and its PR key is preempted while its peers still name it, with a kernel-log probe on the fenced node (P290-AUTH-CLOSED, then a peer's LOCK_REQ/FREEZE_REQ/FROZEN reaching it, or the fix's P-TAUTH-*-AUTH-CLOSED lines), graded on no P-TAUTH-PUBLISH-FAIL loop, no target 'Reservation conflict ... initiator' flood and no survivor operation stalled past 30 s; a rate for those laps (a control there with the fix reverted, or a --transfer for the reviewer to check); and a drift check cited after the last lap. ===== Removal P20261023-6c4c99 was rejected (data/reviews/P20261023-6c4c99.md): the control is the frozen source with only the fix reversed and the batches are sound, but the harness's store never refuses a write (tests/tauth/fenced_node_ledger_test.c:23-25), so neither batch had a RESERVATION CONFLICT, an uncertain publish or a reconcile; in test21's log the FROZEN arm accounts for at least 28,034 of 31,510 refused publishes (670 printed + 27,364 suppressed), and the other ~3,476 are pinned on dlm_page_ensure_mine only by reading (dlm/dlm.c:4629 logs nothing when its write fails). Needed: a real-target run with the fix out and in on the candidate's module (the record's 2-node TCP step is the template), counting P-TAUTH-PUBLISH-FAIL and the target's conflicts per second after P290-AUTH-CLOSED (fix out the flood, fix in none plus P-TAUTH-PAGE-AUTH-CLOSED or P-TAUTH-HANDOFF-AUTH-CLOSED), or a harness store that refuses a closed node's writes; a probe on the dlm_page_acquire activation (dlm/dlm.c:4629) so every refused publish is traced to a gated entry point; the fix-on batch passed through an approved verify first. The rig run's 75 s stall and test28's mount timeout are now named by D-NETMESH-SHARED-DIR-LOCK-QUEUE-JAMS-60S-AFTER-PEER-WITHDRAWS and D-8NETMESH-REJOIN-MOUNT-AFTER-PEER-WITHDRAWN-ONE-PATH-TIMES-OUT-AT-60S. ===== The lap at 4 nodes or more, where peers other than the recoverer keep a withdrawn node as master under mastership retention (the incident's 8/net/mesh/mpath shape): V withdrawn by the preempt while two peers run load in the shared directory, the probe counting what reaches V's ledger after P290; precheck both PARK arms before any batch. ===== 2026-10-24 (session 84), the original evidence read for what the injections miss (tests/evidence/flood_test21_20261022T200054Z/test21_kernlog_boot.gz, decompressed line numbers): test21 was not a live node whose key was preempted. Its filesystem shut down FIRST, at 19:56:11 (:819052 'P378-TRANS-READ-FAIL ... metadata read failed inside a transaction; DIRTY transaction -> forcing shutdown', :819048 P-SESSION-POISON (force-shutdown)), and it declared a voluntary death at once: :819049 P-WITHDRAW-QUEUE, :819053 P-WITHDRAW, :819054-819056 'disklock: heartbeat thread exiting' / 'heartbeat stopped', :819057 'P163-WITHDRAW-STAMP slot=0 node=462431191 rc=0'. Its key was gone 3 s later (:819084 P305-RESV-HEALTH state=SELF_GONE 19:56:14, :819087 P290-AUTH-CLOSED reason=PR_CONFLICT_FENCED), and the refused publishes began at 19:56:19 (:819197, first P-TAUTH-PUBLISH-FAIL). No heartbeat, lease or withdraw line follows :819090 in the file; no P-LEASE-WITHDRAWN-RENEWAL names node 462431191. After :819192: 31,510 'reservation conflict', 31,510 P-TAUTH-PUBLISH-FAIL rc=-52, 31,510 P-TAUTH-RECONCILE, 670 P-TAUTH-FROZEN-NOT-CONSUMED, 66 'dlm_frozen_activate: N callbacks suppressed'. So the trigger is a shutdown-first voluntary death while the node holds ledger pages, which the preempt and pause arms (withdrawing through P277 or the lease) never produce. Drafted: an INJECT=shutdown arm of tests/evidence/drafts/tree/tests/fenced_ledger_rig_lap.sh (XFS_IOC_GOINGDOWN NOLOGFLUSH on V under load; the existing grade counts what reaches V's ledger after P290-AUTH-CLOSED). Precheck queued at 8/net/mesh/mpath on g8 in attempt 20's solo lane: PARK=1 (fsd20p1) and the control PARK=0 (fsd20p0).

Not the same configuration as D-FIO-VS-XFS-SEQW-63PCT-ON-2-NET-MESH-MPATH-WHILE-HOST-NVME-SHARED (2/net/mesh/mpath, 63%). ===== 2026-10-23, SECOND CONFIGURATION: 4/net/mesh/mpath fio_perf_vs_xfs FAIL 2026-10-23T01:17:46Z (run 20261023T011432Z-g4, build 16A5F5DDDB4852C9D5DB236, test3-test6, data/criteria.runs.jsonl:7893) 'seqW=40% seqR=89% randW=201% randR=292% worst(write)=40% (threshold>=70%, wsrc=xfs-baseline, rig=scst-fio)' against .xfs_fio_baseline.net-mesh-mpath.scst-fio.json (seq_write_1m 1404 MiB/s, seq_read_1m 1294, file dated 2026-10-04). The pool LUN images moved from the NVMe root to /mxfs (/dev/sda, a SATA Samsung 870, ~512 MiB/s) on 2026-10-22 (CHANGELOG.md 0.90.134 entry, 'Rig host: LUN images, test VMs and evidence live on /mxfs'); the 512-byte yardsticks .xfs_fio_baseline.{net-mesh,disk-caw}-{direct,mpath}.scst-fio.json date from 2026-10-01/04, before it (seq write 1324-1404 MiB/s), while native XFS on a pool LUN on the 870 measured 511 MiB/s seq write and 539 MiB/s seq read (.xfs_fio_baseline.net-mesh-direct4k.scst-fio.json, 2026-10-22, 5 runs). MXFS here wrote 40% x 1404 = ~562 MiB/s and at 4/net/mesh/direct 42% x 1324 = ~556 MiB/s, at or above that. ===== 2026-10-23, the 512-byte yardsticks re-captured on the 870 (lane tests/evidence/lanes/g2_xfs_yardstick_512_20261023T141853Z: tools/xfs_baseline_refresh.sh 512_20261023 test1, 14:18:53-14:34:07Z, the only rig lane up; test1 nproc=2, pool LUN 02 of 512-byte blocks; tests/evidence/xfs_baseline_512_20261023.log, runs in tests/evidence/xfs_baseline_512_20261023_runs/). The old yardsticks were 1324 (net-mesh-direct) and 1133 (disk-caw-direct) MiB/s seq write. Against the new net-mesh-direct yardstick this record's 4/net/mesh/direct run (42% x 1324 = ~556 MiB/s) is about 109%, over the 70% floor: the hypothesis that the yardstick, not the write path, failed it holds for this cell. NOT YET MEASURED: the mpath yardsticks (.xfs_fio_baseline.{net-mesh,disk-caw}-mpath.scst-fio.json, 2026-10-04, seq write 1404 MiB/s) that graded the 4/net/mesh/mpath cell, since tools/xfs_baseline_refresh.sh captures only the direct configurations of a 512-byte LUN; and fio_perf_vs_xfs re-run at 4/net/mesh/direct and 4/net/mesh/mpath against re-captured yardsticks on a quiet host.

defects.summary: On 16/disk/caw/mpath path_all_lost (run 20261011T225324Z-g16, build not recorded), test16 lost both paths, was fenced, unmounted and mounted again (REMOUNT umount_rc=0 mount_rc=0), and its load after rejoining never reported: an open of ino 125829259 spun in mxfs_dlm_open_protect (load pid 11788 in state R) -- 2000 P95-OPEN-PROTECT-RESTART in 85 ms, then 'P-INODE-WEDGE-FENCE ino=125829259 mode=5 -- release wedged; refusing DLM acquire' with about 13 million refused acquires suppressed over 65 s -- instead of failing the open. The load was still running when the next row started, which aborted on it (STRAY killed=1 left=1). The row's FAIL never reached the run ledger (the boards were migrated without it).

defects.next: Read whether today's mxfs_dlm_open_protect (xfs/xfs_mxfs_open.c) ends an open whose inode's release state is WEDGED with an error or restarts it for ever, and why ino 125829259's release wedged on the rejoined mount (stuck_kmsg_test16.txt before line 54794: the release-proof lines for that inode). Then a reproducer: an inode whose release is forced WEDGED, opened on a mounted node, must fail the open within stall_limit_s; and 16/disk/caw/mpath path_all_lost on the current build with kernel logs kept. ===== 2026-10-23 (read, build 16A5F5DDDB4852C9D5DB236): today's mxfs_dlm_open_protect no longer restarts an open on a wedged release: xfs/xfs_mxfs_open.c:589-597 fails it with -EIO (P95-OPEN-REFUSED) when mxfs_release_proof_enforce is set and i_mxfs_rel_state is MXFS_RELSTATE_WEDGED, and :598-604 ends the loop on a fatal signal (P95-OPEN-KILLED); test knob dbg_openprotect_wedge_ino (:41-45, tests/open_wedged_inode.sh) forces the state. What stays open: why ino 125829259's release wedged on the rejoined mount at all (a wedged release refuses every acquire on the inode for the life of the mount, so the open now fails with EIO on a live node instead of spinning), read from stuck_kmsg_test16.txt before :54794; and 16/disk/caw/mpath path_all_lost on the current build with kernel logs kept. ===== ===== 2026-10-24 (session 56): this run's wedge is the one CHANGELOG.md:3370-3403 (0.90.124) traced and fixed under D-RECYCLED-INODE-INHERITS-WEDGED-REL-STATE, naming this run (tests/evidence/board_20261011T225324Z-g16_path_all_lost/) and this inode: 'its unmount wedged 125837620 at teardown (P-INODE-WEDGE ... teardown=1, 437 s). It remounted at 502 s, and at 506 s the first acquire on 125829259, an inode the new mount had just read, was refused as wedged (P-INODE-WEDGE-FENCE) with no wedge of it in that mount'. Re-read here: in stuck_kmsg_test16.txt between the rejoined mount's envelope (:52062, 495.67 s) and the first P-INODE-WEDGE-FENCE (:54794, 506.97 s) the inode is named on 2 lines only, :53570 P218-CLUSTER-PASSENGER ... nocore=1 skipped=1 and :54794, and no release-state, release-proof or P95 line comes before :54794. The cause was mxfs_dlm_inode_init never assigning i_mxfs_rel_state, so an inode allocated in slab memory whose last occupant wedged started WEDGED; it now starts ACTIVE (xfs/xfs_mxfs_dlm.c:3912-3921, P-RELSTATE-RECYCLED), and since then a wedged open fails with EIO instead of spinning (xfs/xfs_mxfs_open.c:589-604). That removal's verification was tests/relstate_recycle_inject.sh on 0.90.124 against a control build without the assignment, not batches on this record. Next: a same-build switch for the assignment (a module parameter that skips the reset, so the control runs on the frozen candidate), tests/relstate_recycle_inject.sh as the batch lap (EXPOSED: P-RELSTATE-RECYCLED >= 1; PASS: no P-INODE-WEDGE-FENCE and every read and append returns), a control with the switch off and a verification sized from it at 16/disk/caw/mpath, then remove --fixed citing the 0.90.124 trace. ===== 2026-10-24: the same-build switch exists (relstate_init_active, xfs/xfs_mxfs_dlm.c:3955-3963; tests/relstate_recycle_inject.sh RRI_INIT_ACTIVE=0 is its control arm), and no batch has run on it. Attempt 20: a precheck of each arm on g2e at 2/disk/caw/mpath (tests/evidence/lanes/queue_g2e_a20.txt; the control arm has never run on a build carrying the open fix, and on 0.90.124's control build its cat and sh stayed in the kernel until the node was reset), then the control and verification of lap:relstate_recycle at 16/disk/caw/mpath on test1/test2 of a g16 formation in the solo lane (queue_solo_a20.txt), bound 60 s a lap; then remove --fixed citing the 0.90.124 trace (CHANGELOG.md:3370-3403).

defects.summary: When a peer dies silently (killed, or every path lost), the survivors declare it dead only when its disklock heartbeat expires, 17 checks or ~34.8 s after its last heartbeat, and resume ~7-9 s later after the membership change; a survivor operation that needs the dead node therefore stalls 40-61 s, over the 30 s stall limit, at every node count on both lock managers

HISTORY (measured, graded PASS under the rows' own 120 s bound before run.sh graded stalls against stall_limit_s): data/criteria.runs.jsonl path_fence_degraded / path_fenced_return / path_all_lost on 2026-10-14 to 2026-10-21, survivor stalls 39.8-61.6 s at 2/disk/caw/mpath (40345, 41817, 42096 ms on 71AC6107043DD5BE3D9181A), 2/net/mesh/mpath (39825, 41758, 41419), 4/disk/caw/mpath (41143, 41958), 4/net/mesh/mpath (44310, 43440, 43523), 8/disk/caw/mpath (41441, 42856), 8/net/mesh/mpath (41635, 46999, 42570), 16/disk/caw/mpath (61570, 41687, 40242). path_peer_withdrawn (a death with a withdrawal) stalls 9-12 s on 9594B08726D6732D2ED5E87 and 16A5F5DDDB4852C9D5DB236, and path_fenced_return on 16A5 measured 26529 ms with fenced_s=21. ===== ALSO 16/net/mesh/mpath:path_fence_degraded:2026-10-20T13:42:36Z (data/criteria.runs.jsonl:5123, INCOMPLETE 'run died while this test was executing', status ABORTED): the row had finished; tests/evidence/board_20261020T130158Z-g16b_path_fence_degraded/row.log:345 (mtime 2026-10-20T13:42:36Z) 'RESULT: PASS src=test | measured=victim=test32 fenced_s=35 resumed_s=13 reinstate_s=18 survivor_stall_ms=45705 acked=16236 elapsed=227s fails=0', the chain was stopped as it ended so no verdict reached the board; its survivors stalled 45.7 s on the silent death of test32 (tests/evidence/incident_remaining_evidence_20261023.txt:1353-1417). ===== 2026-10-23, heartbeat path avoid (build 33DB08D36BBA2E810760F70: every heartbeat read a passthrough on the PAL's chosen path, hb_io_bound_ms=2000, a path with no answer in that time or a transport host byte passed over for 30 s) at a 20 s window (dead_timeout_ms=20000), variants with PF_KEEP_KMSG=1, lanes tests/evidence/lanes/g8_pathfo_20261023T094644Z and g4_pathfo_20261023T094647Z. Survivor stall (max_stall_ms, ledger): 8/disk/caw/mpath path_fence_degraded 26213 (41943 on CA76F), path_all_lost 28908; 4/disk/caw/mpath path_fence_degraded 24788, path_all_lost 980; 4/net/mesh/mpath path_fence_degraded 29387, path_all_lost 27678; 8/net/mesh/mpath path_all_lost 30130 FAIL (fenced_s=21 resumed_s=10; on CA76F 30953 FAIL). Same-build control path_avoid=0 hb_io_bound_ms=8000 on 4/disk/caw/mpath path_fence_degraded: 44632 FAIL. Two stalls began before the fault, during a single-path outage, and ran on through the 20 s window: 8/disk/caw/mpath path_fenced_return 43031 FAIL (test7 and test10 last completed 17.4 s before test14 was frozen, while test14's own path a was down; the other survivors 26152-27408, tests/evidence/board_20261023T095449Z-g8_path_fenced_return/stalls.txt) and 8/net/mesh/mpath path_fence_degraded 45043 FAIL (test7, test10, test11 last completed 16.5 s before the kill, during their own path a's failover; the others 28419-29407, tests/evidence/board_20261023T095932Z-g8_path_fence_degraded/stalls.txt). On the TCP lock manager survivors resume 8-10 s after the fence (fenced_s=21), on COMPARE AND WRITE 4-6 s. ===== 2026-10-23, the takeover's phases from four kept whole kernel logs (survivor's kmsg_<node>_fromnode.gz; raw extracts by a log sweep of board_20261023T061326Z-g2b_path_all_lost, board_20261023T060247Z-g2b_path_all_lost, board_20261023T100249Z-g8_path_all_lost, board_20261023T094810Z-g8_path_fence_degraded): after the heartbeat declaration the PR fence and its certificate take 0.2 s and the seal 0.2-0.4 s, then the elected survivor's foreign replay spends 4.5 s proving the dead node's slice stable before replaying it: board_20261023T060247Z-g2b_path_all_lost kmsg_test15 'P-FRSTAB-STABLE slot=1 passes=2 unstable_seen=0 wall_ms=4528' (xfs/xfs_log_recover.c mxfs_slice_stabilize: a full read, then mxfs_fr_stab_passes=2 re-reads each after an msleep of mxfs_fr_stab_interval_ms=2000; DRBD skips them). defects.summary: During a foreign replay the surviving node writes allocation-group header blocks (AGF) without holding that group's lock: PROBE-A AG-META-WRITE-NOT-HELD fires 4-10 times in every lap of the open-EFI gate, fix on and fix off; the probe exists because such a write can erase a live peer's change to the header, which no record has shown cannot happen here
defects.evidence: Review of P20261023-f2db37 (data/reviews/P20261023-f2db37.md:290-291): 10 and 7 times in the verification laps of b20261023-30233a and 4 to 9 in the control laps of b20261023-dc6d35, each on the survivor during the replay's writes; e.g. tests/evidence/20261023T120439Z_capture_gate_openefivd1 dmesg_test1.txt:2296 '[ 2234.539643] mxfs: PROBE-A AG-META-WRITE-NOT-HELD agno=1 daddr=2065329 ops=agf comm=kworker/u5:2 pid=5401 cached=0 holders=0 demoting=0 relpend=0 bflags=0x240022', with its stack from :2300 through xlog_do_recovery_pass and mxfs_xlog_recover_foreign_slice. The probe: pal/linux/xfs_buf.c:11925. On these 2-node laps the only peer is the dead victim. ===== 2026-10-23 code read (frozen tree of attempt 2026-10-23T18:32:24Z): pal/linux/xfs_buf_item_recover.c:1353-1420: on an untrusted (foreign or adopted) replay an image whose on-disk LSN would veto it is applied (OVERRIDE-APPLY) only when its item's token verdict is APPLY and its class is AG or INODE; the comment states APPLY for class AG means the fence-time manifest shows the victim held that AG at death and the live CAW slot still carries the victim's bit with unchanged lineage (P-RMAN live check, a mismatch aborts the attempt), and that the dead slot is zeroed only after P163-RECOVERY-COMPLETE, so no later tenure can have written the block. A foreign replay's AG buffer write is tagged b_mxfs_recov_image (:1570-1578). PROBE-A (pal/linux/xfs_buf.c:11965-12012) tests only this node's own grant (pag_dlm_cached, pag_dlm_holders, pag_dlm_demoting, pag_dlm_release_pending) and reads neither b_mxfs_recov_image nor the replay's verdict, so it fires on every foreign replay write of an AG header whatever authorised it. ===== 2026-10-24, the four-node lap tests/foreign_replay_ag_lap.sh (g4, test3-test6, the victim test6; prechecks, not a batch). The victim makes 48 files of 4 MiB in one directory and syncs; each survivor takes its share's inode grants (chmod); the victim runs an unsynced allocate loop in the same directory and is destroyed; each survivor at once truncates its share, every file concurrently, timed on its own clock; the replayer's ladder entry is its P163-RECOVERY-COMPLETE time less total=, clocks joined by ssh round trip. Build 9C7B7B00C5DE523F1D378C8 (the main tree after the sibling merge, PROBE-A now prints recov=): tests/evidence/20261024T002358Z_fragag_frpre2_tcp (4/net/mesh/direct): files in AG 3, replayer test3, recovery complete 41105 ms after the kill, the replay wrote AGs 3 and 4 (PROBE-A on test3 6 lines, all recov=1), 32 truncates by test4/test5 in AG 3 issued during the replay, 0 completed before its ladder entry, 48 of 48 returned 0, no PROBE-A on test4 or test5, chk_mxfs clean; tests/evidence/20261024T002626Z_fragag_frpre2_caw (4/disk/caw/direct): files in AG 3, recovery complete 40573 ms after the kill, replay wrote AG 3 (6 PROBE-A lines, recov=1), 32 of 32 live truncates issued during the replay all completed after it, chk_mxfs clean. Earlier on the sibling build B8EC569481B988532A1BDBF: tests/evidence/20261024T001807Z_fragag_frpre_caw PASS (serial truncates, 2 exposed); tests/evidence/20261024T002045Z_fragag_frpre_tcp VACUOUS (files in AG 11, the replay in AGs 3-4: the load ran in its own directory), which moved the load into the files' directory. Every lap's truncates waited 39.6-42.7 s (max_stall_ms 40552-42684): the silent-death detection of D-SILENT-PEER-DEATH-TAKES-35S-TO-DETECT-SO-SURVIVORS-STALL-OVER-30S, not this record. Tree sweep (12829 AG-META-WRITE-NOT-HELD lines in 1961 evidence files, 390 directories of 3+ nodes): every line within 60 lines of a foreign-replay or recovery line of the same worker, and in multi-node runs only on the replaying node, before its P163. ===== 2026-10-24, a 4-node replay with live peers that fired the probe and was never cold-audited (the case the next step asks for, unmeasured): board 4/net/mesh/direct crash_audit 2026-10-10T14:05:46Z, tests/evidence/board_20261010T134422Z-g4_crash_audit/dmesg_survivors.txt holds nine 'PROBE-A AG-META-WRITE-NOT-HELD' lines (grep -c = 9), all test5's while it replayed the victim's slice: :22353 '[test5] [ 6734.926908] mxfs: PROBE-A AG-META-WRITE-NOT-HELD agno=1 daddr=2065329 ops=agf comm=kworker/u6:8 ... cached=0 holders=0', stack in mxfs_dlm_foreign_replay_work_fn (:22356); :22402-22413 agno=1 agi/bno/cnt/ino/fino; :22446-22451 agno=2 agf/bno/cnt; :22459 'foreign replay of slot 1 complete'. test3 and test4 were alive and mounted (oracle.log:7 survivors=[test3 test4 test5]). The oracle's file checks passed (oracle.log:53, :60 PASS 876 acknowledged files) but read no AG header, and the post-run chk could not execute because the owner's make clean had removed tools/chk_mxfs (CHK_RC=127), so the headers test5 wrote were never compared with the live peers' view. Infra-proven proposal P20261023-b0fdf1 rejected for this reason (data/reviews/P20261023-b0fdf1.md). ===== 2026-10-24, the measurement batches on candidate 0.90.134 (attempt frozen 2026-10-24T06:38:23Z, module BE3695D2590A65F742F9816), lane tests/evidence/lanes/g4_w12_20261024T064222Z steps 4-5 (g4, test3-test6): at 4/disk/caw/direct batch b20261024-9e6cd0, 10 of 10 laps exposed and PASS, 'measured ... failed 0 of 10 exposed laps'; at 4/net/mesh/direct batch b20261024-0f5859, 8 laps exposed and PASS (e.g. 'LAP foreign_replay_ag PASS: 32 live truncate(s) in replayed AGs all waited for the replay (test3, 16888 ms after the kill); chk clean'), and laps 6 and 8 (08:52:06Z, 08:56:56Z) ended 'RESULT: VACUOUS ... stage=no-overlap' ('no survivor other than the replayer changed an AG the replay was writing, so nothing here tests the exclusion'; every other check of the lap passed, chk_mxfs clean; tests/evidence/batch_laps/b20261024-0f5859/20261024T084936Z-319695*.log, 20261024T085428Z-f1b4f4*.log). defects.next: Read the probe's own comment and conditions (pal/linux/xfs_buf.c near :11925) and the foreign replay's AG header writes (mxfs_xlog_recover_foreign_slice): which lock or recovery barrier stands in for the AG lock during a replay, and whether a live third node could hold that AG and change its header meanwhile. Then a 3-node or larger death with a live peer allocating in the replayed AG, the probe and the AG headers checked on every node. ===== Not yet read: where ri_mxfs_verdict is set for class AG (the fence-time manifest and the live check) and whether an image whose AG the victim did not hold at death can reach pass 2 by any path; and, on the TCP lock manager (net/mesh), what holds a dead node's AG grant against a live node's acquire until P163-RECOVERY-COMPLETE, as the CAW slot's bit does on disk/caw. If both hold, PROBE-A is a detector that cannot tell an authorised replay write from an unauthorised one; the 3-node lap (a live peer allocating while a third node's death is replayed) then tests the claim. ===== ===== 2026-10-23 code read (candidate attempt 2026-10-23T20:41:09Z tree), the two questions the next step left open. (1) Which images reach pass 2: xfs/xfs_log_recover.c mxfs_report_replay_authority (:3802) sets every buf item REFUSE by default (:3912) and replaces it with mxfs_shadow_eval_token's verdict (:3965-3969); for class AG that is APPLY only when the block's AG is the token's resource (:3439-3456), the owner slot is the victim's (:3478), the epoch matches or an earlier-lineage pair applies (:3483-3521), and mxfs_shadow_manifest_lookup (:3230-3407) finds the AG in the fence-time manifest with holds, the grant epoch and lineage (:3541), the live CAW slot read agreeing with the manifest entry or the attempt aborting (P-RMAN-POSTSEAL-MUTATION, :3321-3377); REDUNDANT items are skipped in pass 2 (:5377). So an AG image reaches pass 2 only for an AG the victim held at death. (2) What keeps a live node out of that AG until the replay is done: on TCP, v5_tcp_declare_dead (dlm/v5_mount.c:14073, comment :14048-14072) never purges a slotted victim; its grants stay frozen in the master table until v5_dead_grants_retire (:18436) runs in the recovery-complete ladder (:19090), so a live node's conflicting acquire queues behind the frozen grant (or is refused while the recovery is blocked, dlm/dlm.c:15603-15620); on CAW the victim's slot bits stay until the ladder's step 1, mxfs_dlm_caw_purge_node (dlm/v5_mount.c:18959-18972), and a live acquire past the base timeout only gives up when its blockers are dead (dlm/dlm_caw.c:7194-7216: the break leaves the wait for the timeout path, it grants nothing). PROBE-A (pal/linux/xfs_buf.c:11965-12012, inline in xfs_buf_submit_ex) tests only this node's in-core grant fields and reads neither b_mxfs_recov_image (set for a foreign replay's pass-2 buffers, pal/linux/xfs_buf_item_recover.c:1570-1578) nor the verdict, so by this read it cannot tell an authorised replay write from an unauthorised one. This is a code read, not a measurement: the record is disposed of only by the 3-node lap (a live peer allocating in the replayed AG while a third node's death is replayed, the peer's acquire timed against P163-RECOVERY-COMPLETE, the AG headers checked on every node and by chk_mxfs), and the detector then tells replay writes apart (b_mxfs_recov_image and the replay task) instead of firing on them. ===== 2026-10-24: the four-node lap is built and prechecked on both lock managers (above). Next, on the next frozen attempt: a batch of the lap (no switch removes the exclusion, so this is a measurement for remove --disproved, not a control and verification), at 4/disk/caw/direct and 4/net/mesh/direct, at least 10 exposed laps each, then propose remove --disproved citing each lap's ordering and chk_mxfs, and the detector change (PROBE-A not firing on a recov=1 image written by the replay task) as its own fix. ===== 2026-10-24: why calibration b20261024-0f5859 (4/net/mesh/direct) could not be measured: its laps 6 and 8 (iso 08:52:06Z, 08:56:56Z; logs tests/evidence/batch_laps/b20261024-0f5859/20261024T084936Z-3196956a.log and 20261024T085428Z-f1b4f413.log) ended 'RESULT: VACUOUS ... stage=no-overlap' (rc=3, recorded INCOMPLETE by tools/batch_lap.py:181). In both, every one of V's 48 inodes was in AG 11 ('V's files: 48 in AGs 11(x48)') while the replay wrote AGs [3] and [3 4]; in the 18 other laps of both batches the inodes' AG was the replayed AG (2 or 3). P131-SELF-FENCE [PR_KEY_PREEMPTED]'. File times (stat, UTC): rs_stderr/test32_LdPVlv 13:03:43.326 (the remount's ssh began), remount_test32_rejoin.txt 13:05:23.109 (its rc=124 record): about 100 s. The rs_stderr file holds only the ssh banner. The survivors' stalls were 19.5-21.8 s (row.log:71-127, errors_in_window=0). No kernel log of any node was kept: the directory has no kmsg_*_fromnode.gz and no kern_*.txt, follow_test32.txt is 0 bytes (the row's kmsg_keep skips a row that ABORTs, D-PATH-ROW-ABORT-KEEPS-NO-KERNEL-LOG-SO-A-HUNG-REJOIN-LEAVES-NO-EVIDENCE), and tests/evidence/netconsole.log holds no test32 line. The lane's next step found test32 unmounted (step10.log:27 'marker stale: test32 live=... want=... MOUNTED') and the power-down destroyed it (step11.log:16-17 'test32: still up after 90 s, destroying'). Related, cause not established: D-8NETMESH-REJOIN-MOUNT-AFTER-PEER-WITHDRAWN-ONE-PATH-TIMES-OUT-AT-60S (a TCP rejoin mount timing out at 60 s after a peer withdrew, 8/net/mesh/mpath). ===== What the bounds say (tests/mpath/lib.sh:486-489, pf_remount): the remote command is 'timeout 40 umount $MNT; ... timeout 45 mount -t mxfs ...; ... echo REMOUNT ...' under an ssh bound of 100 s (measure ... 100). Both remote steps are bounded by timeout(1), so a umount and a mount that merely failed or overran would still have printed the REMOUNT line within about 85 s; the ssh reached its 100 s bound with no line (rc=124, stdout=[]), so the umount of the self-fenced filesystem or the mount after it did not return to SIGTERM: a task in uninterruptible sleep on test32. The power-down's 90 s grace then expired with test32 still up (step11.log:16), which a task stuck in D state would also explain. Which call it was, and its stack, are not known: no kernel log was kept.
