defects.summary: On 2/net/mesh/mpath path_flap with a 12 s death window, test18's load stalled 81.7 s during the flaps and 120.3 s after them, 5.5 million of its operations returned errors, test18 could not read every file test17 had acknowledged with its checksum, both nodes logged a shutdown, withdrawal, death declaration, BUG, oops or hung task, and test17 saw the membership fall below 2, in a row that kills no node.
defects.evidence: Run 2/net/mesh/mpath:path_flap:2026-10-23T17:22:40Z (FAIL, 169 s), a variant run (MXFS_EXTRA_MODARGS=dead_timeout_ms=12000, MXFS_MPATH_TMO=2, MXFS_TEST_ENV=PF_KEEP_KMSG=1: a 12 s death window and the 2 s path timescale under evaluation for D-SILENT-PEER-DEATH-TAKES-35S-TO-DETECT-SO-SURVIVORS-STALL-OVER-30S), build 08D63764A9352FBDD5A76CD, lane tests/evidence/lanes/g2e_mpathtmo2_k6_20261023T162033Z. Measured 'victim=test18 flaps=10 flap_s=4 stall_ms=81690 settle_s=0 acked=29984 elapsed=166s fails=12 max_stall_ms=120272'. Failed checks, from the run's reason: 'F4: test18's longest stall, ms (got 81690)'; 'F4_after: test18's longest stall, ms (got 120272)'; 'test18: no operation returned an error in the whole run (got 5503784)'; 'test17 acknowledged files (> 0) and test18 reads every one with its checksum (got no)'; 'test17 logged no shutdown, withdrawal, death declaration, BUG, oops or hung task (got 1)'; 'test17 saw no membership below 2 (got 1)'. ===== 2026-10-23 evidence read (board_20261023T171936Z-g2e_path_flap): all 29390 of test17's files read on test18 failed 'read_error=EIO' (verify_test17_on_test18.txt:1-201), read after test18's own shutdown, so they are the shut-down node's errors, not data the files lost; test18's 594 files read on test17 all matched. test18 logged P-WITHDRAW at [993.6], P290-AUTH-CLOSED reason=AUTHORITY_LEASE_EXPIRED overdue_ms=4104 at [1005.6] and P131-SELF-FENCE [PR_KEY_PREEMPTED] at [1015.8] (kmsg_test18_fromnode.gz:168770, :171886, :172946); test17 saw the withdrawal (P163-WITHDRAW-SEEN) and recovered test18's slice. The row also failed 'the target holds the same reservation keys at the end as at the start (got differ(2))'. Hit lists: /tmp/claude-1000/-home-steve-src-mxfs/b943d379-d576-4e63-a466-c398808883d0/scratchpad/hits/. ===== 2026-10-23 (session 48), test18's whole kernel log read in order (log sweep; raw lines, board_20261023T171936Z-g2e_path_flap/kmsg_test18_fromnode.gz): both paths registered at mount (':120447 P-PR-PATHS-REGISTERED dm-1 key=0x4ef62bfe92211b9e paths=2 registered=2'); the row's mark ':120861 [967.219600]' (17:20:01.5Z by the nearest realns line); path a flaps from 17:20:22.9Z (links.log). At the first flap's return the iSCSI connection of sd 4:0:0:0 was dropped and logged in again inside the 2 s session recovery timeout (no 'session recovery timed out' and no 'Failing path' before it): ':168753 [993.604095] connection2:0: detected conn error (1022)', ':168756 [993.612189] sd 4:0:0:0: Power-on or device reset occurred', ':168757 sd 4:0:0:0: reservation conflict', ':168760 reservation conflict error, dev dm-1, sector 21432631 op 0x1:(WRITE)', ':168761 P277-RESV-CONFLICT node 3636049448 count=1 -- data-path write bounced with SCSI RESERVATION CONFLICT', ':168770 P-WITHDRAW -- FS shut down', 8 ms after the re-login. Only after it ':170848 P290-AUTH-SUSPENDED' (1001.5), ':171886 P290-AUTH-CLOSED ... overdue_ms=4104' (1005.6), and test17's preempt ':172943 P-PR-OWNKEY-GONE' (1015.8). test17 declared nothing on its own window: ':160673 P163-WITHDRAW-SEEN slot=1 node=3636049448 -- peer declared voluntary death (FS shutdown)'. So the 12 s window is not what shut test18 down: a write the session re-sent on the re-logged-in nexus was refused, and one refused data write shuts the filesystem down. pal/linux/kern.c:5967-5970 already records that 'a reinstated iSCSI session can be unregistered on SCST for tens of milliseconds, and a log write refused then shuts the filesystem down'. With the 5 s path settings a 4 s flap is not detected as a connection loss at all (NOP-Out 5 s plus 5 s answer), which is why the default rows never re-logged in. ===== Code read 2026-10-23 (session 48): even where the late-path fill runs (lease >= V5_PR_FILL_MIN_LEASE_MS, dlm/v5_mount.c:10941-10949), it never re-checks a path it already counts as registered: mxfs_pal_scsi_pr_fill_paths (pal/linux/kern.c:7074-7083) marks every path in the map's known[] list 'known to hold the key' (t.r[i] = 0) and skips it (:7097), and the scsi_device of a path whose iSCSI session logged in again is the same object, so a registration the target dropped at the re-login is never restored by the fill. At a 12 s window the fill does not run at all (lease 8 s). ===== 2026-10-23 (session 49), the refusal's cause read from the target's source (/src/scst): a login that iscsi-scst does not process as a session reinstatement (the old session already shutting down) gets a new tgt_dev from scst_pr_init_tgt_dev, which links the existing registrant only if reg->tgt_dev is NULL (scst/src/scst_pres.c:1193-1200); the registrant is still linked to the old session's tgt_dev, so the new one has none, and scst_pr_is_cmd_allowed refuses its WRITE (scst_pres.c:2399, :2419-2422; caller scst_targ.c:2348-2355). Only the old session's final free, queued to SCST's management thread (scst_lib.c:7482-7531, :5805-5834), moves the registrant over (scst_pr_clear_tgt_dev, scst_pres.c:1225-1238, commented 'It should never happen'). A real reinstatement holds the new session's commands (iscsi-scst/kernel/iscsi.c:175-201, reinst_pending_cmd_list) until scst_reassign_retained_sess_states moves the registrant (scst_lib.c:14595-14606, called from iscsi-scst/kernel/nthread.c:175-177), so it has no gap. The node stayed registered throughout: the target refused a write from a retained registration, which SPC keeps across an I_T nexus loss. Not yet measured on the rig (the target-side order of login, refusal and handoff). ===== 2026-10-24 (session c74395b6): lane tests/evidence/lanes/g2e_pathflap_scst7_20261024T014649Z on SCST .7 (test17/test18, MXFS_EXTRA_MODARGS=dead_timeout_ms=12000, MXFS_MPATH_TMO=2, build 9C7B7B00C5DE523F1D378C8, a fresh prep before every row): 2/net/mesh/mpath path_flap PASS x3 (board_20261024T014754Z max_stall_ms=2547, 015253Z 1168, 015804Z 4089), path_mount_degraded PASS (020200Z max_stall_ms=6126, mount_one_path_ms=6740); 2/disk/caw/mpath path_flap PASS (020619Z max_stall_ms=6269), path_mount_degraded PASS (021021Z max_stall_ms=6161, mount_one_path_ms=6505). Clean runs on a changed target are not a disposition: whether .7 removed this record's cause (the re-login gap) is unproven until a run's re-logins are shown to meet a still-active old session and pass, against a .6 control that fails at the same settings. ===== 2026-10-24 (session 79): the .7 qualification's flap1 and flap2 NOT EXPOSED verdicts were the arm's clock mapping, not the target: D-SCST-FLAP-ARM-CLOCK-OFFSET-READS-SSH-SETUP (the single-call midpoint offset +229/+240 ms with 460/481 ms round trips). With X's offset taken as 0, in each of their 13 gap logins (flap1 sids 1d 1f 21 23 25 27, flap2 29 2a 2b 2d 2f 31 37) the write X issued before the login was blocked ~4 s and ended 33-54 ms after the host-logged login, carried by the new session while the target still held the old one READY, with 'PR: moving reg ... (shut_phase 0' at each and no 'Reservation conflict' for X in either run (host_kmsg.txt). That reading is by clock arithmetic, not by the arm. On the open-session offset (draft of the arm; tests/evidence/scst7_flapclk_20261024T140955Z), three more .7 runs on test15/test16, pool-04, two paths at MXFS_MPATH_TMO=2: each EXPOSED (one gap login with a write across it) and VERDICT PASS, conflicts_for_X=0, handoff=1, 1, 2. So .7 has 4 exposed passes graded by the arm (flap3 and these three) and 0 failures. ===== 2026-10-24 (session 80): lane tests/evidence/lanes/g2e_a19_20261024T143227Z, six path_flap rows at 2/net/mesh/mpath on attempt 19 (module A27A67A3E501890BE9985E0, MXFS_EXTRA_MODARGS=dead_timeout_ms=12000, MXFS_MPATH_TMO=2, PF_KEEP_KMSG=1, test17/test18, victim test18, each after a forced prep): all PASS, flaps=10 flap_s=4, stall_ms 6202, 8229, 4184, 6363, 4359, 6326, acked 2578-3358, fails=0 (data/criteria.runs.jsonl path_flap 2026-10-24T14:37:49Z, 14:42:07Z, 14:46:24Z, 14:50:38Z, 14:54:55Z, 14:59:33Z; evidence tests/evidence/board_20261024T14{3415,3856,4310,4727,5143,5553}Z-g2e_path_flap). 0 of 6 reproduced the 120 s stall: not a disposition (cannot-reproduce is not DISPROVED); the rate is now at most 1 in 7 counting the original failure.
defects.next: Measure the gap: on a formed 2/net/mesh/mpath pair with MXFS_MPATH_TMO=2, drop one path's connection for ~4 s while a writer runs, with READ KEYS down that path in a loop from the node, timestamping when the re-logged-in nexus shows the key again against the first refused write (scsi logging or the P277 line). Then decide the fix at the cause: a reservation conflict on a nexus that just reported POWER ON/RESET (the re-login) is checked against READ KEYS before it counts as a fence, and the refused write is retried once the key is back, instead of shutting down on the first one. Control: the same drop with the check's switch off. ===== 2026-10-23 (session 49): consulted gpt-6-astra on tolerating the refusal in MXFS (docs/rulings/silent-peer-death-under-the-stall-limit.md, 'A target that refuses a retained registration after a relogin'). Ruled: READ KEYS listing the key is no authorization for a retry; a journal-write retry also needs a durability proof (a later PREFLUSH/FUA commit never covered the refused write) and a crash-recovery proof of the hole; a data retry must keep the operation pending (redirtying breaks unwritten-extent conversion); every completion class must be covered from the first conflict. Preferred: fix the target's handoff (hold the new session's commands until the registrant is moved, as reinstatement does, synchronized with PR removal and task abort), or gate a recovering path below the filesystem before it carries I/O. Next: (1) measure the gap on the rig (2/net/mesh/mpath, MXFS_MPATH_TMO=2, a 4 s cut of one path under load): the host's /sys/kernel/scst_tgt/devices/<lun>/pr_state and iscsi-scst session log against the node's first refused write; (2) the target fix is in the lab's SCST, which the owner runs, so ask the owner whether to patch iscsi-scst's non-reinstatement login (or the registrant handoff) on clyde; (3) independently, decide whether the release's path timescale stays at 5 s (where a 4 s flap does not log in again) or moves to 2 s, which the silent-death compound case asks for. ===== 2026-10-23 (session 50), the target-side order measured from the lab host's own kernel log for the run (journalctl -k, clyde, local time CDT = UTC-5; test18's first flap return at 17:20:27Z): 12:20:27.021340 'iscsi-scst: __iscsi_state_change:436:***ERROR***: Connection 00000000438e3d53 with initiator iqn.2004-10.com.ubuntu:01:test18-mxfs-node unexpectedly closed!'; .021424 'TM fn NEXUS_LOSS_SESS/6'; .021498 'session_free:291:Freeing session 00000000e671fc13 (SID 1c1b0200003d0200)'; .023615 'iscsi_session_alloc:93:Session 00000000105ed92b created ... sid 0x1c1f0200003d0200' (a new session, not a reinstatement); .029334, .030333, .031331, .033330, .035330 five 'scst_set_cmd_error_status:1758:Reservation conflict (dev mxfspool06, initiator ...test18...)'; .042337-.042541 'Processing thread mxfspool064_0..7 finished' (the old session's per-device threads ending as its tgt_dev is freed, which is where scst_pr_clear_tgt_dev moves the registrant). The same order at the next flap: 12:20:35.149336 connection closed, .150620 new session 0000000030a396f9 created, .152330 'Reservation conflict'. So every refusal fell between the new session's creation and the old tgt_dev's release, 6-14 ms after the login, as the source read predicts. The negotiated parameters show 'DefaultTime2Wait 0'; iscsi-scst pins DefaultTime2Wait to 0 (iscsi-scst/usr/param.c:380, min 0 max 0), so the target cannot be configured to have the initiator wait before re-login: the window closes only in SCST's code (the handoff) or below the filesystem on the node. ===== 2026-10-24: SCST +caw-abort-reclaim.6 (lab/scst-pr-registrant-handoff.patch) qualified on clyde with tests/scst_pr_abort_shutdown_race.sh. The handoff arm first measured nothing of it: it re-logged in with iscsiadm -u/-l, and open-iscsi builds a session's ISID from its session id, so a login after a logout is a new session id and a new ISID, a different I_T nexus holding no registration; every write after it was refused RESERVATION CONFLICT, as SPC requires (tests/evidence/scst6_qual_20261024T003721Z, registrant ISIDs 0x100003d0200 and 0x200003d0200 for sids 1 and 2). The arm now resets path 1's TCP connection (ss -K, as a path flap does) so iscsid recovers the same session, and in a second part resets it again and issues PREEMPT AND ABORT inside the first hold. On .6 (tests/evidence/scst6_qual_20261024T005406Z, pool LUN 06, knob 8000 ms), both runs VERDICT PASS: 'handoff: X path1 connection reset ... left=FAILED@1 back=LOGGED_IN@42 (+8983 ms) ... write at +9859 ms: rc=0', host 'scst_pr_init_tgt_dev:1288:PR: moving reg iqn...test1-mxfs-node,i,0x100003d0200/2 (... key 0x0000000abcd40801) from shutting-down sess ... to new tgt_dev', 'host: handoff=2 conflicts_for_X=0 earlier_session_aborted=1 held_in_shutdown=2 bad=0', the P&A at +3.1 s of the second hold printing 'earlier session ... of the nexus (shut_phase 1): aborting its commands' and 'PR ABORT ALL admitted on session ... in shut_phase 1'; no BUG, Oops or CRITICAL in the host log. The window arm and the stress arm (20 iterations) passed on .6 (tests/evidence/scst6_qual_20261024T003330Z), and tests/scst_pr_bounds_check.sh passed. So on .6 a registered nexus that loses its connection and logs in again keeps its registration through the old session's teardown, on the target in isolation. Next: the path rows on .6 (lanes g2e_pathflap_scst6, g8_mpathtmo2_scst6 again after the 8-node marker fix, D-RUN-SH-MARKER-PARAMS-PASSED-AS-ONE-ARGUMENT-EMPTY-THE-MARKER-AT-8-NODES), reading each relogin's host lines against the node's first write after it. ===== 2026-10-24 (session 59): .6 does NOT close the relogin gap of a path flap. Lane tests/evidence/lanes/g2e_pathflap_scst6_20261024T005021Z step 3, 2/net/mesh/mpath path_flap (test17/test18, dead_timeout_ms=12000, MXFS_MPATH_TMO=2, build 9C7B7B00C5DE523F1D378C8, SCST 3.11.0-pre+caw-abort-reclaim.6, run 20261024T005133Z-g2e, data/criteria.runs.jsonl:11629) FAIL: test18's stalls 77221 ms and 120377 ms, 5371774 errors, test17's 31927 files EIO on test18, test18 shut down. Host kernel log 00:52:29Z (pool-02, test18, first flap's up): 'Connection 0000000049fcade2 ... unexpectedly closed', NEXUS_LOSS_SESS on the old session, then 'Session 000000004f7961b3 created' (same ISID 0x0300003d0200), then 16x 'Reservation conflict (dev mxfspool02, initiator ...test18...)', and NO 'PR: moving reg' line for test18 (the window's only four are the qualification test's, test1/pool-06); test17's PREEMPT AND ABORT then logged 'PR ABORT: registrant ...test18...,i,0x300003d0200/2 ... earlier session 000000006381753f of the nexus (shut_phase 0)'. iscsi-scst calls scst_unregister_session only at session_free (00:52:30Z, 'Freeing session 0000000048647836'), so when the new session's tgt_dev was initialised the old SCST session was still SCST_SESS_SPH_READY and .6's handoff condition (shut_phase != READY) was false. test18: '[122.805475] sd 3:0:0:0: reservation conflict', '[123.018217] P277-RESV-CONFLICT count=1', '[123.018237] P-SESSION-POISON ... (force-shutdown)'. The .6 qualification's handoff arm reset the TCP connection with ss -K, which ends the old session before the initiator logs in again; a flapped path brings the old connection's close and the new login in together. Next: .7 - the new tgt_dev of a nexus takes the registrant from any other session of the same I_T nexus (same TransportID with ISID, same relative target port): iSCSI cannot hold two sessions with one ISID, so the newer is the nexus; the earlier session's in-flight commands stay in PREEMPT AND ABORT's reach through .6's scst_pr_abort_nexus_sessions. Qualify it with a flap-shaped handoff arm (path dropped with iptables for 4 s, not ss -K). ===== 2026-10-24 (session 65): the three SCST .7 path_flap PASSes above never reached the re-login race, so they say nothing about whether .7 closes it. Host journal for each row's window (copies: tests/evidence/pathflap_relogin_read_20261024/j1.txt .6 run 005133Z, j2-j4.txt .7 runs 014754Z, 015253Z, 015804Z; journalctl -k, CDT): in the failing .6 run test18's first flap return closed the old connection at 19:52:29.074331 and created the new session at .076399, 2 ms later (j1.txt:17, :31), and 16 'Reservation conflict ... test18' lines followed within 221 ms (j1.txt:38-53). In each .7 run test18 logged only two connection closes, and each new session came 3-18 s after its close (j2.txt:171 20:49:15.757 -> :210 20:49:33.811; j3.txt:408 20:54:14.204 -> :465 20:54:16.974; j4.txt:513 20:59:27.597 -> :567 20:59:45.399), after the old session was gone; no 'moving reg' or 'PR:' line names test18 in any of the four windows, and the .7 runs have no test18 reservation conflict. The host-only .7 qualification (lane tests/evidence/lanes/host_scst7_qual_20261024T013522Z, tests/scst_pr_abort_shutdown_race.sh flap arm, test1 on pool-06, evidence /home/steve/src/mxfs-a17/tests/evidence/scst7_qual_20261024T013522Z) reached the gap shape (handoff from a READY session) 6, 7 and 3 times in its three runs, but flap1 and flap2 sent no write across a gap login ('NOT EXPOSED: 40 flap(s), 6 gap login(s), 0 write(s) sent across one', step7.log; same in step8.log, 7 gap logins), and flap3 sent one ('EXPOSED: 1 of X's writes went out on a new login while the target still held the old session of X's nexus READY ... VERDICT PASS', step9.log, host 'scst_pr_init_tgt_dev:1296:PR: moving reg ... from earlier sess'). So .7 has one exposed pass. Next: a .7 qualification sized to give each run several writes across gap logins (the flap arm's writer paced so a write is in flight at each re-login), then the rig row with its re-logins read against the host log, counting only runs whose test18 re-login came inside the old session's life. ===== The rig row: 2/net/mesh/mpath path_flap with MXFS_EXTRA_MODARGS=dead_timeout_ms=12000 MXFS_MPATH_TMO=2 MXFS_TEST_ENV=PF_KEEP_KMSG=1 on SCST .7, each run's test18 re-logins read against the host log (a re-login inside the old session's life, 'PR: moving reg ... shut_phase 0'), counting only runs that met one; then a rate for the row and a verification on the candidate.

defects.evidence: Review of P20261023-8d639f (data/reviews/P20261023-8d639f.md): batch b20261022-548ef2 (lap:jdt_gate_fault at 2/net/mesh/direct) was launched with no --stall pattern (tests/evidence/lanes/netdirect_verify_round2_20261023T035741Z/summary.log:61); the harness wrote 'INFO A's last-member unmount: A_UMOUNT_RC=0 ms=31006' (tests/evidence/20261023T043949Z_capture_gate_jdtv1/join_during_takeover_fault.log:8); tools/batch_lap.py stall_graded reads only 'max_stall_ms=' (:301) and declared --stall patterns (:311); neither tests/capture_fault_gate.sh nor tests/join_during_takeover.sh prints max_stall_ms=, and no lane summary has passed --stall. Split out of D-BATCH-LAP-RECORDS-NO-STALL-SO-A-HARNESS-LAP-OVER-THE-STALL-LIMIT-GRADES-PASS, whose fix grades what reaches the grader. ===== 2026-10-24, attempt 17 (lane tests/evidence/lanes/g2_a17_20261024T102925Z steps 5, 7 and 9: fix on, GATE_RELAY_STALL=0, JDT_MAX_STALL=0): all three prechecks UNMEASURED with the worst operation 12.4-12.9 s. defects.evidence: 2026-10-24, attempt 17 of 0.90.134 (frozen 2026-10-24T10:25:09Z): lap 5 of control b20261024-bda0e1 (tests/live_holder_shard_lap.sh lhmc5 at 2/net/mesh/direct, g2) recorded INCOMPLETE rc=2 at 2026-10-24T10:41:54Z (tests/evidence/batch_laps/b20261024-bda0e1/20261024T104052Z-68ff9925.log: 'STAGE prep rc=1 wall=62s', 'LAP lh_master ABORT: prep_cluster rc=1'); its prep log tests/evidence/20261024T104052Z_lhmaster_lhmc5/prep_1.log: '--- pre-prep: VMs up at +2 s (10:40:54) ---', 'lun_pool: pool lock not taken in 60 s: /home/steve/disks/pool/.lock', 'ERROR: no pool LUN of 512-byte blocks for [test1 test2]'. In that minute lanes g4c_a17tf (a 4-node multipath prep from 10:41:37Z), g2e_a17lp (tests/lun_pool_shutdown_lap.sh, which clears records, boots and binds two nodes with --paths 2) and g2d_a17b were allocating; other preps of the same lanes logged waits of 2-16 s ('lun_pool: pool lock waited N s'). The lock's holder is not named anywhere: <pool dir> holds only lunNN.owner/.paths/.wwid/.tmo. ===== 2026-10-24, the holder named for the refusal of lap lhmc5 (2/net/mesh/direct, 10:40:54-10:41:54Z): run.sh runs its host preflight holding the pool lock (run.sh:2547, PREFLIGHT=(tools/lun_pool.sh quiet clyde_preflight.sh), 300 s wait, tools/lun_pool.sh:861-862), and the preflight's kernel-log-rate check waits inside it for any lane's VM power-up to finish (scripts/clyde_preflight.sh:252-260, /tmp/mxfs_host_powerup.lock, which scripts/lab_power.sh:159-162 holds for a whole 'up'). Lap pw8c4 of g8b took the pool lock at 10:40:47 (tests/evidence/20261024T104044Z_peerwin_pw8c4/prep.log:4 'pool LUN held at +1 s', :6 preflight starts 10:40:48), and its preflight waited 58 s (:51) on lane g4c's 'lab_power.sh up group:g4c' (tests/evidence/lanes/g4c_a17tf_20261024T104047Z/summary.log :8-9, 10:40:47-10:41:37), then passed at 10:41:54 (:62). Every alloc behind it waited: lhmc5 gave up at 60 s (10:41:54); tff2 and g4c got the lock at 10:41:54-55 after 16-17 s. No release ran under the lock in the window (no 'releasing' line in the 899 evidence files of 10:35-10:50Z; SCST shows only test17/test18's boot relogin and logout on pool-07 at 10:40:43-45 and test7-10's boot logins on pool-02 at 10:41:16-35). CAUSE: two locks taken in an order that makes the pool lock wait for a power-up: run.sh holds the pool lock while the preflight waits for the power-up lock. Next: draft the fix (run.sh waits for the power-up lock before it takes the pool lock for the preflight, and holds both, the preflight told not to wait again), with a switch for the control; a lap that starts a power-up and a prep beside it and times an alloc from a third caller. ===== 2026-10-24: fix drafted for the next attempt in tests/evidence/drafts/tree/run.sh. When the run uses the pool, run.sh takes /tmp/mxfs_host_powerup.lock shared (240 s, the preflight's own bound) before it takes the pool lock for the preflight (lun_pool.sh quiet), and holds it across the gate. The gate runs with that descriptor closed, so nothing it leaves running keeps the hold. The gate's own shared wait is then immediate, and no power-up can start while the pool is held quiet. PREFLIGHT_POWERUP_FIRST=0 waits inside the pool lock, as before: the control. Lap drafted: tests/evidence/drafts/tree/tests/pool_lock_powerup_lap.sh. It holds the power-up lock exclusive for 40 s, starts a pooled prep of the lane's group under it, and times a third caller's 'lun_pool.sh quiet true': PASS under 5 s, FAIL longer; bound 236 s. The holder logging drafted earlier (tests/evidence/drafts/tree/tools/lun_pool.sh) goes in with it. Next: apply both at the next attempt, precheck each arm once, then control and verification.

defects.summary: tests/join_during_takeover.sh ARM=stall cannot reach the case it grades, and it grades the vacuous lap as a FAIL. The stall arm pauses A's takeover pass (dl_takeover_pause_ms=45000, dl_no_ondemand_takeover=1, set once the pass is seen in flight) and expects B's root acquire at mount to wait on the transition and be refused after 30 s. But A's own lone remount always takes the root inode's page over on demand before the pass, so B's root request meets no transition, B mounts in seconds, and the lap FAILs every refusal check instead of saying it measured nothing.
defects.evidence: 2026-10-24, attempt 17, lane tests/evidence/lanes/g2_a17_20261024T102925Z steps 5, 7 and 9 (tests/jdt_gate_stall_lap.py, the gate's jdt entry at NFILES=4000, JDT_PASS_PACE_MS=30, ARM=stall EXPECT=clean, 2/net/mesh/direct; the inner runs went to the lap's scratch ledger, not the release board). All three: 'B's mount inside the pass: B_MOUNT_RC=0 ms=7401' (12533, 12421 for the other two), then 'FAIL B's mount inside the stalled pass was REFUSED (rc != 0) got=0 want=1' plus six more FAILs, and UNMEASURED. In tests/evidence/20261024T105759Z_jointk_jdtstall-join_during*/dmesg_A_followed_1.txt, A mounts at [1716.911692] and logs 'P960-ONDEMAND-SERVED type=1 ino=128 ag=0 page=5093' at [1717.268750], before its 'Ending clean mount' at [1717.418963]: its own root acquire. B mounts from [1736.406413] to [1738.933359] with no AUTH-TRANSITION line, and the lap's own summary reads 'B: transition rx=0 wait=0 ... stalled=0', 'A: ondemand=1 served_root=1'. The pass itself was held (activations 251 at B's issue and at its return). No recorded run has ever passed the check 'B's mount inside the stalled pass was REFUSED' (0 files under tests/evidence). Every earlier stall-arm run aborted before B's mount, the pass not seen in flight. ===== 2026-10-24, a second difference from the arm's design: the stall arm's checks (tests/join_during_takeover.sh:539-555) encode 0.84.8 (CHANGELOG '0.84.8 -- A joiner is held at the settle gate until the incumbent's beacon carries the two-node view'). There, the incumbent's join prepare waited behind its own ledger takeover, so a paused pass kept its beacon at the zero view, and B was held at the settle gate until the 60 s backstop refused it. In these three laps B's settle gate logged nothing ('B settle gate: lines=0 refused=0 pending_live=0 confirmed=0') and A's worker never waited ('A worker: transition_wait=0 stalled=0'). So A installed the two-node view with its pass held. Before the arm is redesigned, establish from the code which change took the incumbent's prepare off the takeover pass, and that B's acquire of a page the held pass has not reached still meets AUTH_TRANSITION, waits, and is refused by the 30 s watchdog with no shutdown. That is what the redesigned arm must measure. If no change accounts for it, it is an MXFS behaviour change to examine as a defect of its own. ===== 2026-10-24, the incumbent's install read from the code. It is not a behaviour change. v5_join_transition (dlm/v5_mount.c:14281-14333) installs the view as soon as the join prepare (mxfs_dlm_join_prepare, xfs/xfs_mxfs_join.c:394-489: the freeze and the cached-view drop) returns 0, and nothing on that path waits on the departure worker's takeover pass (v5_depart_run, :4202). The two are coupled only when one of the prepare's own acquires lands on a page the pass has not reached and meets AUTH_TRANSITION (dlm/dlm.c:4827-4849, 14992-15008). In 0.84.8 the incumbent's 16k-page authority made that happen. Here, at 4000 files with A idle after its lone remount, it did not: A logged 'P-JOIN-INSTALLED ... attempts=1 ms=247' at [1736.266291], with no AUTH-TRANSITION line on either node. So the stall arm's precondition (the incumbent's beacon held at the zero view by its paused pass) is not guaranteed on any build. The redesign must create the waiting acquire itself: B (or A's prepare) acquiring a page the held pass has not reached, which meets AUTH_TRANSITION and is refused by the 30 s watchdog (dlm/dlm.c:11900-11987, P960-AUTH-TRANSITION-STALLED; fallible callers return -EREMCHG).

Its answers, hypotheses to measure and not findings: (1) a plain PREEMPT leaves the preempted nexus's accepted commands running (SPC-4 Preempting; only PREEMPT AND ABORT aborts them), so the out-of-band case is a real zombie-write window, and a later PREEMPT AND ABORT cannot reach it because the key is gone; (2) LOGICAL UNIT RESET aborts every task of every I_T nexus on the LU, FUNCTION COMPLETE means none continues, and registrations and the PR generation survive it, so reset + READ KEYS (key still absent, generation unmoved) is a sound exclusion proof by the standards; (3) the bystander cost is what the sole-member guard at dlm/v5_mount.c:13454-13462 exists for, and it is real on this target: SCST vdisk defaults TAS=0 (/src/scst/scst/src/dev_handlers/scst_vdisk.c:134) and terminates another initiator's aborted command 'without delivery or notification' (/src/scst/scst/src/scst_lib.c:14417-14427), so a live member's in-flight command waits out its 30 s SCSI timeout; setting TAS=1 by MODE SELECT is rejected (not portable, shared page, reverted by the reset itself, and an aborted CAW is still ambiguous); (4) the sound general route proposed is a cluster-wide quiesce before the reset: every live member stops submitting LUN I/O (filesystem, log, disklock heartbeat, CAW and PR passthrough), drains its in-flight requests including any in SCSI error handling, and acks; the prover resets, re-reads keys, and releases the quiesce; a member that does not ack must be PREEMPTed itself before the reset is relied on. No such quiesce exists in the tree (grep -i quiesce over dlm/ and pal/ finds only the CAW teardown quiesce). Design work: a quiesce barrier on both transports (on disk/caw the request travels over the LUN being quiesced, so its ack has to land before the gate closes), bounded well inside the lease and the 30 s stall limit. ===== 2026-10-24: design written, docs/rulings/out-of-band-key-removal-surrender.md (consult claude-opus-5-5: PREEMPT AND ABORT aborts the whole task set of each I_T nexus whose registration it removes, including commands queued before an earlier plain PREEMPT, SPC-4 r37 5.12.11.5 / SAM-4 5.6; REGISTER from such a nexus cannot be refused). A departed node that is still running and has stopped every writer of its own registers its recorded key again on every path, once per incarnation, and holds it until it reads it preempted; the prover's unchanged re-drive then finds the key present and certifies with the usual PREEMPT AND ABORT, no LU reset and no cluster quiesce. Precondition: D-SELF-FENCED-NODE-LEDGER-PUBLISHER-RETRIES-FOREVER-ON-RESERVATION-CONFLICT fixed first (its publisher bypasses the write gate and would land writes once the key is back). Next: that fix, then the re-registration behind a same-build switch, then the fenced-ledger lap INJECT=preempt at 4 and 8 nodes graded on certification and every survivor operation inside 30 s. ===== 2026-10-24 (session 87): the surrender drafted for the next attempt, behind its own switch (module parameter pr_surrender, default 1; 0 never registers again, as before: the same-build control). tests/evidence/drafts/tree/dlm/v5_mount.c v5_pr_surrender_tick, on every PR-worker tick: only with authority closed on the PR conflict (close_reason PR_CONFLICT_FENCED), the scsipr context still holding the key as its live registration, and no heartbeat beat able to land (drafts/tree/dlm/disklock.c mxfs_disklock_hb_quiet: the heartbeat thread has returned, hb_exited, and no heartbeat I/O is outstanding on a worker, abandoned ones included). The own slot's descriptor decides: one naming this incarnation that has certified or whose attempt passed its command-submission boundary (MXFS_RECOV_F_FENCE_CMD_MAY_HAVE_RUN) means a peer's PREEMPT may have removed the key, and nothing is registered (P-PR-SURRENDER-NOT-NEEDED); an attempt that met the key absent submitted nothing and leaves no such mark (the f8p1 prover wrote its intent and then found the key absent); an unreadable descriptor, 10 tries, refuses. Otherwise drafts/tree/dlm/scsipr.c mxfs_scsipr_surrender runs the mount's register (same-key probe, REGISTER on every path of a multipath map, READ KEYS verify) and keeps the key as a fence target (registered=false, never unregistered by this context), P-PR-SURRENDER. Then v5_pr_surrender_watch: once the slot shows a fence of this incarnation certified, or the slot passed to another incarnation, a key still standing is given back (mxfs_scsipr_surrender_return, P-PR-SURRENDER-RETURNED; the sole-survivor gate certifies with the key absent and could do so between the read and the REGISTER), a key gone prints P-PR-SURRENDER-PREEMPTED. All three sources pass tools/draft_syntax_check.sh (0 errors, 0 warnings). Lap: tests/evidence/drafts/tree/tests/fenced_ledger_rig_lap.sh GRADE=certify INJECT=preempt (SURRENDER=1/0 written to V at run time): EXPOSED V's P277 key gone and a survivor's P-PR-FENCE-ABSENT; PASS a survivor's P236-FENCE-CERTIFIED, no P238-FENCE-BLOCKED, every survivor operation within 30 s. Next attempt: prechecks of both arms at 4/net/mesh/direct and 8/net/mesh/direct, then a control (SURRENDER=0) and a verification sized from it. defects.evidence: Read from the code at the review of verify P20261024-4975c4 (data/reviews/P20261024-4975c4.md), which noted that its approval covers merge_overrun_lap.sh alone and that these two calls have no mount-point check; no run of either has been seen to kill a node's services
defects.next: Fix drafted for the next attempt: tests/evidence/drafts/tree/tests/closure_mount_race.sh and tests/evidence/drafts/tree/scripts/drbd_rig.sh run the fuser only while 'mountpoint -q $MNT' holds (bash -n clean). Then a lap per site that runs the cleanup with $MNT already unmounted and reads the node's ssh, journald and udevd main pids before and after it (the merge_overrun lap's check, tests/merge_overrun_lap.sh:77-96), with the guard switched off for the control.

defects.summary: The late-path fill (mxfs_pal_scsi_pr_fill_paths, pal/linux/kern.c:7105-7244) admits a REGISTER on a path that holds no registration of the node only if now + MXFS_PR_PATH_TIMEOUT_MS (5 s) + 1 s is before the earliest time a peer may fence the node (:7211-7226), and a REGISTER whose outcome is unknown is followed by an unregister and the path taken offline (:7230-7238, mxfs_pr_path_quarantine :7086-7103). Nothing establishes that a command the initiator gave up on after its timeout can no longer execute at the target: the ruling says a REGISTER is bounded only by a confirmed end of the original task, not by an abort sent or a later READ KEYS, and that taking the path offline does not stop a write already queued at the target behind the delayed REGISTER. A REGISTER executed after the fence puts the fenced key back on its nexus, and no READ KEYS can tell.
defects.evidence: Design ruling docs/rulings/silent-peer-death-under-the-stall-limit.md: ':237-251' (B, the time from admission until the REGISTER has completed or can no longer execute, includes 'a confirmed cancellation, not merely an ABORT TASK sent'; 'If cancellation has no enforced upper bound, no finite threshold proves the absence of a registration after the fence'; a timed-out REGISTER's nexus is quarantined and 'only an established end of the original task releases it'), ':256-260' (what must be measured first: admission-to-dispatch delay, when the timeout fires, how SCST cancels a queued or running PR OUT, transport recovery and any hidden retry), ':300-306' (the late REGISTER is a fencing problem of its own; three ways to close it). Code: pal/linux/kern.c:7214 admission against the initiator's timeout only; :7230-7235 unknown outcome -> unregister and SDEV_OFFLINE, with no confirmation that the original task ended at the target. Raised by review data/reviews/P20261024-234c4f.md, which rejected the removal of D-MPATH-MOUNT-DEGRADED-12S-WINDOW-REGISTRATION-MISSING-AND-SHUTDOWNS for leaving this untracked. No run has shown it: no P-PR-PATH-FILL-LATE or P-PR-PATH-QUARANTINED line has been read from any rig log. ===== 2026-10-24, the lab target's source read (/home/steve/src/scst, this host's SCST build; read only, nothing run): (1) an aborted command never executes: scst/src/scst_targ.c:2361-2365 __scst_check_local_events 'if (unlikely(test_bit(SCST_CMD_ABORTED, &cmd->cmd_flags))) ... goto out_uncomplete' runs before local exec, and PR OUT re-checks after taking the PR lock (scst/src/scst_local_cmd.c:940-945 'We can be aborted by another PR command while waiting for the lock'); PR OUT runs synchronously in the command thread (scst_targ.c:2644 [PERSISTENT_RESERVE_OUT] = scst_persistent_reserve_out_local). (2) ABORT TASK answers only once an affected command already sent for execution is done (scst_targ.c:5262-5279, cmd_done_wait_count). (3) LUN RESET walks every tgt_dev of the device, every session, with no registration test, aborting each queued command including one not yet initialised whose lun matches (scst/src/scst_lib.c:13236-13264 scst_process_reset), and waits for any command already executing (done_counted, scst_targ.c:5274-5279). (4) An iSCSI connection close sends SCST_NEXUS_LOSS_SESS, aborting every command of the session, and waits for executing ones before the session is freed (iscsi-scst/kernel/nthread.c:257-286, :382). (5) While SCST activity is suspended (global /sys/kernel/scst_tgt/suspend, or a management write), a received command that is not aborted stays parked on scst_init_cmd_list and executes on resume (scst_targ.c:4303-4325, scst_main.c:944-991), and an ABORT TASK for a command that already has its tgt_dev, a LUN RESET and a TARGET RESET are delayed until resume (scst_targ.c:5802-5808, :5848-5858, :6714-6728). (6) Two sessions of one initiator name with different ISIDs are distinct registrants (iscsi-scst/kernel/iscsi.c:3830 transport id '%s,i,0x%llx' with the ISID; scst/src/scst_pres.c:146-179 tid_equal compares the whole string). So on this target a REGISTER can execute after the initiator gave up only if the target received it and had not executed it when the initiator's error handling ended (a stalled or suspended target), and the target did not see that path's session end before resuming (the path's network cut). A LUN RESET issued after the fence's PREEMPT AND ABORT ends every such command.
defects.next: Measure B on the rig, as the ruling lists, at 2/disk/caw/mpath: hold one path of a node unanswering (the target's portal for that path dropped at the host, or the SCST device's commands held), let the fill issue its REGISTER there (dbg_pr_fill_pause_ms to place it), and read from the target side (SCST's PR log for that I_T nexus) whether and when the REGISTER executes against when mxfs_prout_path returned and what the SCSI error handler did (abort task, LU reset, session drop). If every timed-out REGISTER is shown ended at the target before the initiator call returns, the admission bound holds and that measurement is the evidence; if one can execute later, close it in the fence (an unresolved REGISTER keeps the certificate from being issued, or the fence aborts the tasks of every nexus of the LU), with a same-build switch and a lap that delays a REGISTER past a peer's PREEMPT AND ABORT. ===== 2026-10-24: closure from the source reading above (not yet built): (a) before a late REGISTER is issued the node makes durable, in its own heartbeat slot, that a late REGISTER of its key may be outstanding, and keeps it there until the REGISTER's outcome is known (a quarantined path keeps it for the mount's life); (b) a fence of a node whose last slot carries it does PREEMPT AND ABORT, then a LOGICAL UNIT RESET, then READ KEYS and PREEMPT AND ABORT again if the key is back, before it certifies. The admission bound makes every such REGISTER issued before the earliest fence, and a REGISTER's bytes not received by the time its session is torn down are never delivered, so after the reset no earlier REGISTER can execute. The existing witnessed LU reset (pal/linux/lureset.c, dlm/scsipr.c:3475 mxfs_scsipr_lu_reset_admit) admits only a sole registrant and needs a mode for other registrants present, whose aborted commands are retried. Lap: a target-side hold of the late REGISTER until after a peer's PREEMPT AND ABORT (a TEST ONLY knob in the rig's SCST PR OUT path, before its ABORTED check), the fix's switch off as the control (the key back on the late nexus after the certificate), on (the key absent after the certificate).
defects.impact_why: a hazard read from the code against a design ruling, not yet observed: a REGISTER that executes at the target after a peer's PREEMPT AND ABORT registers the fenced node's key again on that nexus, so a write the node still has queued there can land after the survivors replayed its log (docs/rulings/silent-peer-death-under-the-stall-limit.md:300-306)
